News.title: Teacher, 27, arrested over ‘inappropriate relationship with student’ as school describes charges as ‘deeply concerning’
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

TEACHER DETAINED Teacher, 27, arrested over ‘inappropriate relationship with student’ as school describes charges as ‘deeply concerning’

A HIGH-SCHOOL sports teacher has been accused of having an inappropriate relationship with a student.

Christian G. Payton, 27, turned herself in on Wednesday, almost two months after police received a report alleging that an athletic trainer had sent sexually explicit images to a student.



Payton was employed at Indian Creek High School in Illinois at the time of the alleged offences.

She has now been charged with four felony counts of official misconduct and four felony counts of distributing harmful material to a minor.



Payton also faces four misdemeanour counts of distributing harmful material to a minor.

The charges allege that she sent sexually explicit images of herself to a 17-year-old student while working as an athletic trainer, according to court documents.



She allegedly sent the images on April 2, 4, 7 and 11.

Payton was released under the Illinois SAFE-T Act, a 2021 criminal justice reform law that ended cash bail for defendants awaiting trial.

Under the terms of her release, she is prohibited from contacting the alleged victim or anyone under the age of 18.

She has also been ordered not to leave Illinois and must report to the court’s probation department.



Police stressed that the charges are only allegations and that Payton is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

In a statement, Indian Creek School District Superintendent Chad Willis described the allegations as “deeply concerning and disappointing”.

He told Shaw Local: “The safety and well-being of our students is and always will be our highest priority.

“Indian Creek School District is cooperating fully with law enforcement and the appropriate authorities as they conduct their investigation.”

Payton attended Rochelle Township High School and graduated in 2017.



Payton is due to appear in court on August 27.

This comes after a female dance teacher was accused of sexually abusing two of her students.

Emily Pryor Albino, 23, taught children at X-Treme Dance Studio in Laurel, Delaware before being arrested after a chilling tip-off.

Detectives immediately launched a probe – and arrested Albino two days later.

She was charged with four counts of first-degree sexual abuse of a child.

Officers also said that the suspected sex pest had exchanged explicit messages with her students.

The exact age and gender of the alleged victims has not been made public.

News.title: Shocking moment Kosovo politician throws EGGS at country’s acting prime minister as gov chamber plunged into chaos
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a politician lobs eggs at her country’s acting prime minister, plunging parliament into chaos.

The government chamber erupted into the one-sided food fight after interim PM Albin Kurti failed to announce a new president.



Unbelievable footage shows opposition MP Time Kadrijaj reach into her handbag and hurl at least five eggs at Kurti.

Suited men swarmed around her but she ignored them and fired off two more eggs in quick succession before being bundled out by security.



Elections had been held on June 7 – but there was no common consensus over who should be the next leader of the country.

Kosovo has already been gridlocked for much of last year after no party secured a majority in parliament.



Frustrations finally boiled over when Kurti begged parliament for an extension on appointing a new president.

He said: “Consultations are continuing and we have not yet reached an agreement [on the president]. Therefore, I am asking for additional time to avoid new elections.”

The announcement was too much for Time Kadrijaj – who promptly reached into her bag and began pelting the acting PM.

She appeared to have come prepared for the food-based rampage, even popping out from behind fellow MPs to throw the raw goods.



The woman was removed and the session adjourned.

But an unrepentant Kadrijaj posted a clip of the egg-based chaos to social media – where it quickly went viral.

Tensions had been brewing for some time as the acting PM tried to reach 61 votes – the critical number needed to elect a new president.



His party – which roughly translates as ‘self-determination’ – won 53 seats.

The Democratic League of Kosovo secured 18 seats, while the opposition – Kosovo Democratic Party – secured 22.

Kurti has been scrambling to form a coalition which will tip his majority party into power – but so far, he has had little success.

New elections will be triggered if Kurti is unable to form a coalition.

Under Kosovan rules, a parliament must be formed within 30 days after an election.



The deadline passed last month – leaving politicians scratching their heads about what happens next.

News.title: Urgent hunt for ‘violent’ sex attacker on the run after woman ‘seriously assaulted by man riding delivery bike’
News.content:
FIND HIM Urgent hunt for ‘violent’ sex attacker on the run after woman ‘seriously assaulted by man riding delivery bike’

A WOMAN has allegedly been seriously sexually assaulted by a “violent offender” believed to have been riding a delivery bike

Police have urgently appealed for information after the attack in West Barnes, London, just before midnight on Thursday night.

The attacker is said to be a man aged around 30 and is described as approximately 5ft 9″ with brown medium to long hair and brown eyes.

He was said to be wearing jeans, a belt with a gold belt buckle, black trainers and a black padded coat.





The police added he was said to speak with an accent and could be of West Asian or Eastern European heritage.

He was also said to be wearing a white helmet and be riding a pedal-assisted e-bike with a green/black delivery box on the rear.

The Metropolitan Police said there will be an increased presence in the area while officers carry out “urgent inquiries”.

DCI Rebecca Roberts who leads the rape and serious sexual assault teams for southwest London said: “My teams are doing all they can to identify and apprehend this violent offender.



“We are seeking to identify a man described as being approximately 5ft 9”, approximate age 30, with brown, medium to long hair and brown eyes.

“He was wearing jeans, a belt with a gold belt buckle, black trainers, and a black padded coat.

“He was described as speaking with an accent and could be of West Asian or Eastern European heritage.

“The man was wearing a white helmet and was riding a pedal-assisted e-bike with a green/black delivery box on the rear.



“I would encourage anyone who remembers seeing anything out of the ordinary near Meadowsweet Close or the nearby playing fields to come forward to police.

“Any piece of information could be vital to our investigation.

“We understand incidents of this nature cause significant concern within the community, and we are deploying additional officers in the area to provide reassurance and support.”

Any potential witnesses have been urged to contact the force.

News.title: Shocking moment ‘late passengers run across tarmac to try and catch their flight’ before cops escort them away
News.content:
THIS is the alarming moment two passengers strut across the tarmac in a desperate bid to catch their flight – only to be escorted away by cops.

Shocking footage shows the two glamorous women dashing onto the runway as their plane prepares to taxi for take-off.



With their luggage in hand, they frantically wave at the pilot, urging him to stop.

The pair then turn their attention to an airport worker, who quickly radios air traffic control to alert them to the bizarre situation.



Moments later, two more members of staff rush over and attempt to lead the women away from the aircraft.

The passengers reportedly arrived late for their Aeroflot flight at Moscow’s Sheremetyevo International Airport in July.

Rather than accept they had missed their flight, they took matters into their own hands and stormed onto the tarmac.

They were quickly escorted away and forced to reschedule after missing the departure.



Footage of the extraordinary incident quickly went viral on social media, with users reacting with a mixture of shock and disbelief.

One user wrote: “Do they think this is a bus?”

Another said: “Hey ladies, rules are rules for a reason, despite how much money you have.”

A third added: “The level of obliviousness.”

Under Russian law, the women could reportedly face fines of up to £45 for their actions.



The penalty can rise to as much as £260 for an international violation.

This is not the first time a passenger has made a desperate last-minute attempt to stop a plane from leaving.

In May, another Russian passenger reportedly missed boarding after getting stuck in the airport bathroom.

Realising the plane was about to leave without him, he ran onto the tarmac in a bid to stop the aircraft.

But his desperate attempt failed, and he was handed a £30 fine as the flight departed without him.

News.title: Missing woman, 60, found dead in ‘unexplained’ circumstances at London home as cops issue urgent appeal for clues
News.content:
SEEKING ANSWERS Missing woman, 60, found dead in ‘unexplained’ circumstances at London home as cops issue urgent appeal for clues

THE body of a woman has been found in “unexplained” circumstances at her home in London as police make an urgent appeal for information.

Nicole Beling, 60, was found dead at her house after a family member alerted the police and one man, 61, has been arrested on suspicion of murder.



She was reported as missing just after midnight on July 17 and police attended her home in Dittoncroft Close, Croydon, later that morning.

After searching the property officers found her body.



A man was arrested at the scene on suspicion of murder before being released under investigation.

He was arrested again on August 1 and bailed while police continue their enquiries.

Cops are still investigating the cause of her death and it is currently being treated as “unexplained”.

Detective Chief Inspector Alison Foxwell, who is leading the investigation, said: “A formal murder investigation has not been launched at this time and we are keeping an open mind as to the circumstances surrounding Nicole’s sad death.

“We want to hear from anyone who knew Nicole or may have information that could assist the investigation – and help us find answers for her family.

“My thoughts remain with Nicole’s family and loved ones.”



A spokesperson for the police said: “Police were called at around 00:05hrs on Friday, 17 July after a woman was reported missing by a family member.

“She was graded as a high-risk missing person and officers attended her home in Dittoncroft Close later that morning to conduct enquiries into her disappearance.

“Following a search of the property, officers discovered the body of the woman. She was sadly pronounced dead at the scene.

“She has been formally identified as Nicole Beling, 60, from Croydon. Her family are being supported by specialist officers.

“A 61-year-old man was arrested at the scene on Friday, 17 July on suspicion of murder and later released under investigation.



“He was further arrested on Saturday, 1 August and has been bailed while enquiries continue.

“At this time, Nicole’s death is being treated as unexplained. Her cause of death remains under investigation.

“Enquiries into the circumstances of her death continue and are being led by specialist officers from the Met’s Specialist Crime Command.”

News.title: Musician killed in horrific crash with tractor as tributes paid to ‘universally adored’ dad as cops appeal for CCTV
News.content:

'MISSED ENORMOUSLY' Musician killed in horrific crash with tractor as tributes paid to ‘universally adored’ dad as cops appeal for CCTV

A MUSICIAN has died after a horrific collision with a tractor as his family pay tribute to an “incredible” dad.

Nathan Smith, who supported the Wombats with his band MFK, died in hospital after the crash on Shelton New Road, in Cliffe Vale, Stoke-on-Trent.

Police, paramedics and an air ambulance raced to the scene at 8.20am on Wednesday

The 45-year-old pedestrian was taken to hospital in a critical condition but died a short time later.





Staffordshire Police said the tractor driver remained at the scene to help the police with their enquiries.

Nathan, of Hartshill, ran a recording studio alongside playing in several bands, one of which played with the Wombats at Trentham Gardens.

In a statement, his family said: “Nathan was a self-taught electric bass player, who played in various Stoke bands and ran the UTC recording studio in Longton with his friend and fellow Big Cash Prizes band member, Tom Bath.

“He was supremely talented and in recent years enjoyed success with a new Stoke band MFK, culminating in supporting the Wombats at Trentham Gardens.



“Nathan was so much more though. A wonderful son, grandson and an incredible father.

“He charmed everyone he met and was universally adored.

“He will be missed enormously by so many people.”

The force said his next of kin are being supported by specialist officers and that inquiries are ongoing.



Officers have urged anyone with information to get in touch by calling 101 and quoting incident 186 of August 5.

A spokesperson for the force previously said: “We are appealing for information after a man sadly died following a collision in Stoke-on-Trent today (Wednesday 5 August).

“We were called just after 8.20am to Shelton New Road in Cliffe Vale following reports of a collision.

“West Midlands Ambulance Service and Midlands Air Ambulance also attended the scene.

“A tractor and a pedestrian were involved.



“The pedestrian, a man, was taken to hospital by ambulance and was sadly pronounced dead a short time later.

“His next of kin have been informed.

News.title: At least 8 dead and ten injured after packed bus plunges off mountain road in India leaving passengers trapped inside
News.content:
AT LEAST eight people have been killed and another ten injured after a bus plunged off a mountain road.

The bus had been travelling across northern India when it suddenly veered off the edge of a cliff and flipped over – trapping passengers inside.



The tragedy unfolded shortly after 6:30am on Saturday.

The bus had been carrying 18 passengers from Bairagarh to Chamba along a road known for its narrow lanes and steep drops.



It was about 2 miles into its journey when it crashed off the side of the road and plunged down, trapping several people inside the wreckage.

Locals raced to the scene and alerted the police.

Firefighters, cops and workers from the National Disaster Response Force hauled passengers from the mangled wreckage.

The Chamba District Disaster Management Authority confirmed that eight people were killed and ten were wounded in the horror crash.

The victims included the driver and the conductor.

Rescue teams rushed six people with serious injuries to Pt Jawaharlal Nehru Government Medical College and Hospital in Chamba, officials said.



A probe has been launched into the cause of the crash.

Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu offered condolences to the victims’ families after the “deeply tragic” incident.

He said: “I extend my deepest condolences to the families who have lost their loved ones in this tragic accident. May the Almighty grant eternal peace to the departed souls and give the bereaved families the strength to bear this immense grief.



“Instructions have been issued to the district administration to ensure that all the injured are immediately admitted to nearby hospitals and receive proper medical treatment. I pray to God for the speedy recovery of all the injured.”

It comes as the region is lashed with heavy monsoon rains – flooding roads and causing closures.

The area in which the crash occurred is under an orange weather warning with rains expected to batter Himachal Pradesh early next week.

News.title: Hundreds of Brits fall sick after visiting some of UK’s top beaches ahead of fifth heatwave of year
News.content:
TROUBLED WATERS Hundreds of Brits fall sick after visiting some of UK’s top beaches ahead of fifth heatwave of year

HUNDREDS of tourists are falling sick at some of Britain’s most affluent beaches ahead of the fifth heatwave of the summer.

New figures show high reports of illness across the UK’s beaches, those accredited under British Blue Flag meaning they’ve passed strict tests for cleanliness.

Marine conservation charity Surfers Against Sewage (SAS) says it’s received 765 reports of sickness across 406 locations so far this year, reports the Mirror.



Further stats show more than 15,000 days – or 41 years – have been taken off work due to illness contracted from UK’s waters since 2019.



SAS says polluted water has resulted in the likes of ear infections and gastroenteritis, as well as respiratory and skin issues, meaning time off work.

Nearly half the reports so far this year have been since May 1 – with Britain currently experiencing its fifth heatwave of the summer so far.

The Met Office has forecast potential temperatures of 36C next week, with meteorologists predicting the annual record for days exceeding 30C will be smashed.

Beaches with prestigious Blue Flag status have the highest water quality, minimal waste and good biodiversity – as well as being safe and accessible.

Bournemouth tops the list for most reports with 16, while 13 came from Croyde Bay in North Devon, and Polzeath in North Cornwall came third on the list.

Polzeath is a favourite spot for a number of celebrities, as well as former PM David Cameron who bought a £2million home nearby in 2017.

He has been frequently pictured at the beach with wife Samantha – while the likes of Princes William and Harry often surfed there growing up.



Coldplay frontman Chris Martin and TV chef Gordon Ramsey have also made homes in the area.

Other beaches ranking highly on the list include Rest Bay in Porthcawl, Wales, with 12 reports of illness, while Exmouth in Devon has 10, and Portreath, North Cornwall, has nine.

The top 10 is rounded off with Saunton Sands in North Devon, Swanage Central in Dorset and Ogmore in Barry, Wales, all with eight reports – and Woolacombe Village, North Devon, with seven.

However, the location which resulted in the most days off work at 1,014 is St Mary’s Bay in Kent.

SAS, which campaigns against pollution on UK beaches, says sewage dumping is “making us sick” and has been ongoing for “decades”.



Its latest stats show water companies across England recorded 2,487 pollution incidents in 2024 alone – amounting to a whopping 4.7million hours.

Jo Morley, head of campaigns at SAS, told the Mirror: “Thousands of water users are reporting this to us, and this is likely just the tip of the iceberg.

“From gastroenteritis and ear infections, to weeks off work and hospitalisations. This is a public health crisis.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

She added: “There is no official Government data, and no legal protections for people using the water.”

The Sun has approached SAS for more information.

News.title: Victims urged to come forward as police accused of 'litany of failures' over murderer and rapist
News.content:
Police have urged more victims of Simon Levy to come forward, as London's victims' commissioner said a "litany of failures" had allowed him to kill two women and rape a third.

Andrea Simon called for a review on the "failure to monitor him appropriately" when the 40-year-old was known to police as a sexual predator.

British Transport Police said women who recognised Levy as their attacker should report it, while the Met Police said it had investigated whether he had more victims, including further murders.

Meanwhile, the Independent Office of Police Conduct (IOPC) said a police constable is under investigation for gross misconduct, and a detective sergeant is facing a misconduct investigation.

On Friday, Levy was found guilty of murdering two women and raping a third in London while he was being monitored by the Met Police for being a convicted sex offender. He had previously committed a string of sex attacks.

The BBC reported how a series of grave failings by police, prosecutors and the courts left Levy free to murder, rape and sexually assault women.

Levy is due to be sentenced on Wednesday.

News.title: Widdecombe police reopen investigation into incident at Farage's home, BBC understands
News.content:
Counter-terrorism police investigating the killing of Ann Widdecombe have reopened an inquiry into an incident at Nigel Farage's south London home, the BBC understands.

It is understood to relate to what the Reform UK leader described as a "lit incendiary device" being pushed through his letterbox in April 2025.

Counter Terrorism Policing (CTP) London said it was looking into an "attempted burglary" at a property as part of the Widdecombe murder investigation, but did not confirm the home was linked to Farage or why it might be connected to the killing of the former MP.

CTP London has also referred itself to the police watchdog over how the initial investigation into the Farage incident was handled.

Police said at the time that "damage was caused to a door but nothing was stolen".

Both CTP London and the Metropolitan Police were involved in enquiries. No arrests were made and the investigation was closed.

But on Friday, CTP London said a new line of inquiry had been identified that was not "pursued by them at the time".

The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said it had "decided to independently investigate the conduct of a Counter Terrorism Policing London staff member following a referral received earlier [on Friday]".

A statement continued: "The conduct relates to an allegation the individual failed to identify and pursue a line of enquiry relating to an attempted burglary reported in April 2025."

CTP London said it would "full engage" with the watchdog's investigation, adding: "The victims and families in both investigations have been updated today, and we continue to support them."

Ann Widdecombe, the 78-year-old former Conservative minister and Reform UK spokeswoman, was found dead at her home in Devon last month with serious injuries.

Joshua Kerry, from Rotherham in South Yorkshire, was later charged with her murder.

Kerry was initially arrested on suspicion of murder on 11 July, before being additionally arrested on 13 July on suspicion of the commission, preparation or instigation of acts of terrorism.

Widdecombe had served as Tory MP for Maidstone in Kent for 23 years and was appointed to ministerial roles in Sir John Major's government in the 1990s.

News.title: Chasing a ghost: How BBC tracked a fugitive spy chief after months-long hunt
News.content:
For months we drew a blank in our hunt for Luka.

And then we had our first breakthrough.

One of those listed in the book, who we tried calling again, finally answered the phone.

He had been the guard for Luka's apartment block, he told us, and eventually agreed to give us the number for someone he said had been Luka's personal bodyguard - a man we are calling Mahmoud.

It took weeks to secure an interview with Mahmoud. Meetings would be scheduled but he would not show up, or he would request a meeting in a private space such as a car or apartment, which our reporter judged too much of a risk.

They eventually met at a hotel one night, just before midnight. Broad-shouldered and physically imposing, Mahmoud seemed to be considering every answer carefully before he spoke.

He told us he was angry with Luka for leaving him behind when the regime fell. As word had spread in December 2024 that Assad's rule was on the brink of collapse - with rebels advancing on the capital - Luka had said he would stay and defend Damascus, Mahmoud told us. But by the early hours of the next morning, Luka had disappeared, taking a large sum of money with him from the office safe, Mahmoud said.

Mahmoud refused to share any contact details for Luka or his family, but did give us a number for Luka's driver, who he believed had driven the former spy chief out of the capital that night.

This man proved even harder to reach.

When he answered the phone, his voice was nervous and unsteady. He repeatedly insisted he was just a driver, and knew nothing of Luka's activities. Multiple meetings with us were never kept, and eventually he stopped replying.

We turned our attention to Luka's possible escape routes, including neighbouring Lebanon - where the Iran-backed group Hezbollah had close links with the Assad regime.

One senior source in the Lebanese government told us he understood Luka had passed through Lebanon on a "good Russian passport but with a different name", before flying out to Russia.

We managed to find a man, now based in Lebanon, whose name was listed in Luka's contacts book, but under a number that no longer worked. He is one of many wanted by the new Syrian government, because of his close association with the Assad regime.

This man, who we cannot identify, said he had a number for Luka.

We saw it, and realised it had a Russian country code.

Russia was a key backer of the Assad regime, and in the days after his fall, Assad released a statement confirming that he had fled there. Many of his inner circle were believed to have followed him.

Back in Luka's apartment in Damascus, we had found clues that Luka also had strong links to Moscow - awards from Russia's foreign spy service, and even a New Year's card addressed to him from a senior Russian official.

Now, the Russian telephone number for him suggested we finally had proof that he was - as we had predicted - in Russia.

News.title: Sturgeon hasn't spoken to Murrell since he was jailed for embezzling SNP funds
News.content:
Sturgeon also told Dale that she only discovered Murrell was due to plead guilty a week before his first public court appearance.

It later emerged he had been negotiating his plea for months, a fact which she said "hit me like a tonne of bricks".

Sturgeon said: "He was still lying to me right up until the day he pled guilty."

The former first minister added: "He was very isolated over that period, he very rarely left the house, he wasn't communicative, I was a bit worried about his well-being and his mental health.

"And then, now I think: 'What a mug, why were you worried about him?' He didn't worry about me. He didn't worry at all about what he was doing.

"What he has subjected me to is beyond anything I could ever have comprehended.

"I don't understand why he did it, he had no need to do it, I don't think I will ever understand his motivations.

"But whatever that motivation was, he could not have stopped and ever thought about me.

"But I was, until recently, still worrying about him."

Sturgeon - who had stepped down as first minister in March 2023 - was arrested In June 2023 but was later told that she was no longer under investigation.

The former first minister announced her separation from Murrell last year.

News.title: I went for a full body MOT and the results came as a shock
News.content:
Annabel Mason-Thompson went for a Neko Health scan in September last year, knowing she had a suspicious-looking mark on her back - but it wasn't flagged by the technology.

"I felt a bit let down if I'm honest," the 50-year-old says. "Their AI scanner failed to pick up any of my four cancerous lesions.

"It was only when I went into the doctor's room after the scan and I pointed out my red mark did they take a look at it."

Further examination confirmed the mark was suspicious, so Neko Health contacted Annabel to say she would need treatment and wrote a letter to her private dermatologist to say the "lesion requires evaluation with a view to possible excision".

Her dermatologist found three more cancerous marks which needed urgent treatment.

"Luckily," she says, "they were all slow-growing basal cell carcinomas. I had to have two cut out and two taken off via cryotherapy."

Neko Health says "member safety and clinical excellence are at the heart of everything" it does. The company said its clinical team did identify a "lesion of concern" and it was reviewed by two of its dermatologists before a referral was made for potential treatment.

"We know that no one system is foolproof," Nilsonne says, "which is why we have multiple lenses - it is crucial that the technology and human expertise work together."

His company's latest data shows that of the 4,362 scans carried out on clients who visited Neko Health's Stockholm headquarters last year, 1.2% discovered life-threatening conditions such as melanoma and leukaemia. A further 4% spotted significant health conditions that required further treatment, and 1.2% flagged conditions that could be reversed such as pre-diabetic blood sugar levels.

While the figures are not representative of the population and only account for those who can afford to pay for this kind of preventive healthcare, Nilsonne says this is an indicator of how medicine should look in the future.

But GPs disagree. Prof Victoria Tzortziou Brown, president of the Royal College of GPs (RCGP), says they haven't seen "convincing evidence" private broad screening tests "improve health outcomes".

She says the results from these private scans can also place an additional strain on the NHS as clients come back for further tests and potential treatment, even "where the findings prove to be clinically insignificant".

News.title: He's been frozen on Everest for 30 years, now 'Green Boots' may finally be coming home
News.content:
For 30 years, a dead body known as "Green Boots" has been lying in the snow, nestled under an overhanging rock, not far from Mount Everest's summit.

The lime mountaineering boots worn by an Indian climber who died in 1996 have been a grim trail marker for many climbers on their way up the world's highest peak ever since.

Now India is looking for a specialist high-altitude recovery team to undertake a complex and risky mission to retrieve what they say is Dorje Morup's body â arguably the most famous of the hundreds whose bodies have been left frozen on the mountain.

Warning: This story contains a picture of a dead body.

They hope they are on the cusp of returning his remains to friends and family who never gave up hope he'd come home.

"On some days, before I went to sleep, I would think that there'd be a knock on the door tonight and that when I opened, he would be there," Morup's wife told the BBC.

"When he comes home, I will ask him: 'Where were you all these years?'"

News.title: Digital cameras and wired earphones are back and 'a bit more real'
News.content:
Luckily I'm out with my photography-loving best friend, who helps adjust the settings on the camera and gets snapping while I'm otherwise engaged on the dancefloor.

The mere sight of us pulling out the camera and squinting through its tiny viewfinder draws attention â "I've not seen one of these in years", a man remarks.

He's right â digital cameras had their heyday in the late 1990s and early 2000s, just before smartphones took off.

There are currently 42 million active film camera users globally, more than a third of these aged 18â30 and largely influenced by social media trends, according to a market research report, external last year.

So why, when we're surrounded by more advanced tech here in 2026, are they seemingly making a resurgence?

For Lily Redman, a 26-year-old content creator from South Wales, digital cameras "capture a quality that my phone just can't replicate".

She's been taking one on nights out and to concerts and feels the flash on her phone "is grainy and too high definition" compared to the "more smooth" finished product on a digital camera.

"I think people are looking for a bit of grit or something that feels a bit more real," she says.

That may also explain why low exposure photos taken on iPhones and Androids â where people dodge ready-made filters to artificially crank down the exposure setting and produce a darker image â are also popular on socials right now.

With digital cameras offering an element of surprise when you plug in the memory card reader to your computer at home, digital cameras capture a moment in time.

"If I look back at photos my mum took when I was two, they look so old but when I look at photos I took five years ago, they look like they were taken yesterday," says Redman.

"Phone photos have warped our perception of time."

News.title: How a former GB Olympian curbed his porn problem - and the signs and steps to recovery
News.content:
Former Team GB diver Freddie Woodward was a teenager when he realised he had a problem with porn.

"Every time I sat down to revise, all I wanted to do was open those sites," he revealed.

By age 12, he was regularly visiting what he calls "hardcore" sites. As his career progressed - which included representing his country in the Olympics - he was watching adult content several times a day.

Now aged 30, the Olympian has told the BBC how he eventually curbed his habit by shifting his mindset.

"You can't be the person who is trying to quit porn. You have to be someone who doesn't watch porn, and that takes a lot of work," he said.

So how can you spot when a porn habit has become unhealthy, and how can you tackle it?

Although it has become a common phrase, "porn addiction" is not an officially recognised condition in its own right.

"We know a lot of people have a problem with porn," explains sex and relationship psychotherapist Silva Neves, who says the matter has become more prevalent among clients at his private practice.

But experts are divided as to whether it is a true "addiction" â like someone might experience with drugs, for example â and how best to deal with it.

Researcher Campbell Ince, from Australia's Monash University, says the vast majority of clinicians now agree people can suffer from "problematic porn use", but there is still a lot to figure out about its causes and treatments.

This means there is no definitive list of symptoms or treatments available to those worried they may be addicted.

Some clinicians approach it as a compulsive sexual behaviour disorder, a condition recognised by the World Health Organization.

This is sexual behaviour that "feels out of control, is causing significant distress, and despite repeated attempts to control it, they can't," explains psychotherapist Dr Paula Hall, who works privately at the Laurel Centre, a sex and porn addiction centre, and also runs a not-for-profit service.

The NHS does say, external it is possible to be addicted to "just about anything", including sex.

News.title: Woman attacked by bed bugs during Travelodge stay
News.content:
Thirteen days after Hannah Stephenson stayed a night in a Travelodge hotel, she is still itching with red lumps over her body - a nightmare she would not wish on her "worst enemy".

The 31-year-old from Bassingbourn had been out with friends in Cambridge and decided to book a one-night stay at the hotel on Newmarket Road on 26 July to save money instead of getting a taxi home.

The next morning, she woke up to a "horrible realisation", feeling itchy with red lumps over her body and blood spots smeared on the bedding â the tell-tale signs of bed bugs, she said.

A Travelodge spokesperson said: "We are deeply sorry for Ms Stephenson's experience and how distressing an incident like this can be."

Stephenson said a lovely evening with friends had turned into a horrible morning.

"It was just a lovely wholesome time of Cambridge sightseeing and pubs, and now it is tarnished by these bedbug bites," she said.

"It wasn't until I saw the blood and the bugs that I realised what had happened."

News.title: Strictly dancers Ola and James Jordan separate after 23 years of marriage
News.content:
Former Strictly Come Dancing stars James and Ola Jordan have confirmed they have separated after more than 20 years of marriage.

The former professional dancers were regulars on the show for several series after first featuring in 2006.

The couple's manager Vickie White confirmed the split, which was first reported by the Sun newspaper, external.

She said in a statement: "It is with great sadness that I can confirm that James and Ola began a trial separation some time ago.

"Their shared priority remains co-parenting their daughter, Ella, and they are committed to putting her wellbeing first.

"They would greatly appreciate your understanding as they navigate this difficult time."

Ola Jordan won the Open Polish Championship in 1999 when she was 17 years old and became James' dance partner shortly afterwards in March 2000.

She moved to England a month later and the pair got married in October 2003.

James appeared on Strictly from 2006 to 2013 while Ola appeared on the show until 2015.

Ola's celebrity partners included wildlife presenter Steve Backshall and Welsh sprinter Iwan Thomas, while James danced with former international gymnast and broadcaster Gabby Logan, as well as The One Show presenter Alex Jones.

News.title: Hundreds flying out of Birmingham Airport left without luggage
News.content:
She described seeing a "build up" of luggage at the airport, after problems with the luggage belt, but had been assured by staff that it would be loaded on to the plane.

But on arrival at Dalaman they were told by the pilot that no bags had been loaded.

"We have heard nothing about compensation, no communication when our luggage is expected, we've heard nothing about who is liable for it. Is it the airport? Is it TUI? Is it our travel insurance? Who are we meant to go to? We've had nothing from anybody", Chapman said.

"It's just radio silence from the airport, apart from literally telling people 'we've got an issue'".

The first day of their holiday was spent travelling to a shopping centre to buy essentials for "for the next few days" but she added "we have no idea how long this is going to last".

"There are families all over the world at the moment with nothing and no idea of what's going on," she said.

"It's really important that Birmingham Airport are held accountable, and sort this out."

News.title: Man guilty of fatal shooting of teen outside club
News.content:
A man has been found guilty of fatally shooting an 18-year-old outside a Wembley nightclub.

Tyrece Balcha was found with gunshot wounds outside the Crystal Club in Atlantic Crescent at about 05:30 GMT on 21 September 2025. He was taken to hospital, where he died four days later.

A jury at the Old Bailey found Ashley Wallace, 40, of Shenley Road, Southwark, guilty of murder and possession of a firearm with intent to endanger life.

At the same trial, two men were found not guilty of murder. A woman was cleared of possession of a firearm, possession of a firearm with intent to endanger life, and perverting the course of justice. The jury did not reach a verdict on a fourth man.

CCTV footage showed that Balcha had been involved in an altercation inside the club before being followed outside and shot.

Wallace fled the scene in a vehicle and was arrested on 25 September after police traced the car to south-east London.

A revolver carrying Wallace's DNA was found inside the vehicle, and investigators established that the bullet recovered from the murder scene had been fired from the gun.

News.title: Siân Phillips to step back from acting aged 93 after memory issues
News.content:
One of Wales' most celebrated actresses, Dame SiÃ¢n Phillips, is stepping back from full-scale stage acting after experiencing memory issues during rehearsals.

The 93-year-old made the decision after struggling to remember her lines while preparing for a recent production, according to The Times.

However, Phillips said she would continue performing in smaller projects, including a production with Michael Sheen's Welsh National Theatre next year.

Her career has spanned more than 80 years across stage, television and film.

Phillips told The Times she decided to stop taking on major stage productions after struggling to remember her lines during rehearsals for Atonement at Chichester Festival Theatre earlier this year.

According to the newspaper, she said she would continue performing in her show It's All Greek and is also due to appear in Samuel Beckett's Rockaby for Michael Sheen's Welsh National Theatre next year.

Born in Betws, near Ammanford, Carmarthenshire, in 1933, Phillips grew up speaking Welsh before learning English by listening to the radio.

She began performing as a child, appearing on Welsh-language radio from the age of 11, before studying at the University of Wales and later winning a scholarship to the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art.

She performed in radio productions such as The Archers and an adaptation of John le Carre's Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Spy, opposite Sir Alec Guinness.

Before her acting career took off, she worked for BBC Wales as a bilingual announcer and newsreader.

Phillips went on to become one of Britain's most acclaimed actresses, appearing in productions including Doctor Who, Calendar Girls, Dune, and I, Claudius.

She won a Bafta for her portrayal of Livia in the BBC's I, Claudius and received a Tony Award nomination for playing the title role in Marlene.

She was appointed a Commander of the Order of the British Empire (CBE) in 2000 for services to drama, and then a Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire (DBE) in 2016.

News.title: The 'cheap Cotswolds' attracting new residents
News.content:
More people are leaving cities behind in search of cheaper homes, more space and easier access to the countryside, with the Forest of Dean emerging as an increasingly popular destination for buyers priced out of nearby Bristol.

The Gloucestershire district, which lies between the River Severn and the Welsh border, has long been known for its ancient woodlands, market towns and rural communities.

Estate agents say it is now drawing new residents from across the South West who want countryside living without the price tag associated with the nearby Cotswolds.

Local estate agent Glen Webb said many buyers see the area as a more affordable alternative to one of England's most sought-after rural locations: "The Forest is really such a brilliant asset to Gloucestershire. It's a cheap version of the Cotswolds and people sort of love it for that reason."

News.title: Bristol Airport disruption a 'shambles' as flights restart
News.content:
Widespread disruption continues at Bristol Airport after a runway defect saw all flights suspended.

Hundreds of passengers were stranded after the airport's runway was closed from 18:00 BST on Friday until 08:00 on Saturday. While the runway has since reopened, the airport's website says the majority of flights are delayed or cancelled.

A spokesperson for the airport apologised for any inconvenience caused and advised passengers to check the status of their flight with their airline.

Dave Blackwell, travelling home from the Greek island of Rhodes, said it had been "a shambles" since his flight back to Bristol was diverted to Newcastle.

"We were in Rhodes Airport for three hours with no information. Now we have all been told our flight is going to Newcastle and then a five or six-hour bus ride - why Newcastle? How appalling," he said.

News.title: Passengers 'stranded' at locked train station
News.content:
Translink has apologised after rail passengers were left stranded on a platform when a late-night train arrived into a station that was already shut for the night.

A group of about 30 customers were stuck on the platform at Newry Train Station for more than 45 minutes in the early hours of Saturday.

One of the passengers, Anne Greer, told BBC News NI it raised safety questions for the public transport company as the customers had no safe way to exit the station.

Translink said the firm was "looking into the incident" but added its train crew "remained with the passengers to ensure their safety while the issue was resolved".

The train was among a number of extra late-night services which are running to and from Belfast during the Fleadh Cheoil na hÃireann (Music Festival of Ireland).

It was scheduled to leave Belfast at 23:59 BST on Friday and it arrived in Newry at about 01:20 BST on Saturday.

"To our surprise the entire station was closed, so we couldn't exit," Greer said.

"So we're all trapped on the platforms for over 40 minutes."

She said the train crew "helped as much as they could, but there was nothing they could do".

"They were completely gobsmacked as to why they've arrived into a completely closed and locked train station."

Greer said she and other passengers tried to contact Translink but they could only find phone numbers for call centres which had also already closed for the day.

News.title: Argentina v South Africa LIVE: Latest score and updates as Pumas make strong start to rock Springboks
News.content:
( Getty )

Argentina and South Africa continue a busy period of international action with an intriguing clash in Buenos Aires.

This encounter serves as something of a warm-up for the Springboks with four Tests to come against New Zealand as the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series launches, a mouthwatering new venture. Rassie Erasmus and his side dare not overlook a Pumas team with the ability to exploit even the very best – though the hosts are heavily depleted by injury and unavailability.

It makes the task tall for Felipe Contepomi’s side, though they will count on fervent home support as ever. Back in the Springboks ranks are Siya Kolisi, Eben Etzebeth and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu and Erasmus is again able to examine his depth – which will be required as the world champions look to keep their outstanding recent record intact over the next six weeks.

He didn’t score many points in his brief stint in the pros — but an ex-NBA player running for Congress appears to be going to great lengths to make one.

Former NBA bust and current Republican Senate candidate Royce White has announced plans to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft, claiming he now identifies as transgender — for athletic purposes, anyway.

"I'm transgender. I'm a woman. I identify as sometimes identifying as a woman for purpose of basketball, professional basketball, so I'll be declaring for the WNBA draft in 2027 as well," White, 35, told Fox News Saturday.

White’s announcement comes one day after former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom said he also plans to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft. Freedom’s statement followed comments from WNBA player Sophie Cunningham about transgender athletes that renewed a heated debate on the league’s policies for transgender players. It also comes as President Donald Trump has made barring transgender athletes born male from competing in women’s athletics.

White, a 6’8” forward who played just three games in the NBA, all in 2014, continued Saturday, “I think I’d be unstoppable. But I’m a team-first guy. I’m a pass-first kind of player. I do the little things. I led my team in all five major stat categories at Iowa State University, so I do a little bit of everything. I’ll do whatever the coach needs me to do. I’ll do whatever the girls need me to do.”

open image in gallery Former NBA player and U.S. Senate candidate Royce White announced Saturday that he plans to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft amid controversy over the league’s transgender eligibility policies ( AP )

“I think it’s only fair,” he added.

Freedom said he reviewed the WNBA’s eligibility rules before announcing his plans to enter the league and believes he meets the requirements to play.

The WNBA’s 2026 collective bargaining agreement states in Article XIII that “only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA.” However, the 409-page agreement does not define what qualifies as a “woman” for eligibility purposes.

Following Freedom’s announcement, the Women's National Basketball Players Association said in a statement: “We embrace justice equity, diversity, and inclusion. Those are the values that unite this Union and allow it to protect women’s sports while creating transformational change,” the statement read.

“Hate, abuse, and demonization of any person or group of people, including transgender people, only fuel fear, division, and harm. We will continue to have hard conversations,” the group added in the Instagram post. “But we will not be used as political pawns.”

White said Saturday that the WNBA could end the controversy by clearly stating its policy on whether males are eligible to compete in women’s sports.

"I think the WNBA could come out and make a definitive statement about guys with a pair of balls playing in the Women’s Association," he said, adding he will continue moving forward in his draft bid unless the league addresses the controversial issue.

open image in gallery Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom was the first to declare for the 2027 WNBA Draft on Friday ( AFP/Getty )

open image in gallery The WNBA’s transgender athlete debate intensified in July after Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham criticized trans participation in women’s sports ( Getty )

White further claimed he could take legal action if he is not drafted or signed by a WNBA team.

“I have to file a discrimination lawsuit, right? I mean, that’s, that’s ridiculous,” he told Fox News. “We’re gonna have to have a huge legal battle about discrimination if I can’t play.”

White was selected 16th overall by the Houston Rockets in the 2012 NBA Draft out of Iowa State but never played for the team because of severe anxiety and a fear of flying.

Nowadays, he is running in Minnesota’s August 11 Republican primary for U.S. Senate. White previously ran as the Republican nominee against Democratic Sen. Amy Klobuchar in 2024 but lost the general election.

The debate over transgender athletes in the WNBA intensified last month after Cunningham, a guard for the Indiana Fever, criticized trans participation in women’s sports.

“I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men,” Cunningham told ESPN, later doubling down on her comments, claiming they were “common sense.”

The Independent has contacted the WNBA and WNBPA for comment.

Three New Yorkers are suing Mayor Zohran Mamdani over his recently implemented tax on luxury second homes, accusing the mayor’s office of causing chaos and wrongly suggesting thousands of people might owe taxes on homes that don’t actually qualify.

The suit does not challenge the underlying tax law. Instead, it accuses the Mamdani administration of failing to follow state notice requirements and setting off a “panic” in late July by releasing a list of nearly 1 million properties that might be hit with pied-à-terre surcharge, then mailing about 17,000 notices to a smaller group of property owners.

The state court action seeks to have those notices declared “null and void.”

“The mayor wanted a headline, and he got one,” attorney Randy Mastro, a former top aide to Eric Adams and Rudy Giuliani who is representing the group, told Gothamist. “Thousands of people who owe nothing have been confused, exposed, and put to real expense so this administration could make a political point. That is not lawful notice.”

The Independent has contacted the mayor’s office and New York City departments of law and finance for comment.

open image in gallery New Yorkers are suing Mayor Zohran Mamdani over the ‘panic’ created by his tax on luxury second homes ( Getty )

The lawsuit has ties to Mamdani’s political rivals.

One of the plaintiffs is Rachel O’Brien, who is married to Republican City Councilmember Frank Morano, whose father is another plaintiff. Mastro, meanwhile, served as first deputy mayor under Adams and as Giuliani’s chief of staff.

The city has defended its approach to the tax, which applies to homes worth more than $5 million and co-ops and condos worth more than $1 million that are not used as primary residences.

It argues it was bound under state law to release the list of properties, and it has since given homeowners an extension of until September 18 to apply for an exemption.

New York will “vigorously defend the city against this suit” Mamdani spokesperson Matt Rauschenbach told The New York Times.

open image in gallery The tax plan, which is expected to net $500 million annually, previously caused controversy when Mamdani filmed a video promoting it outside the home of Wall Street billionaire Ken Griffin, who threatened to pull his company Citadel out of a skyscraper project in Manhattan ( AFP/Getty )

The pied-à-terre tax, passed in May, will bring in an estimated $500 million annually. The mayor argues the tax is necessary to strengthen the city’s budget and expand social services.

Mamdani has pitched the tax as only impacting the “richest of the rich,” whose buildings are “sitting empty” while their owners are “able to reap the huge financial rewards“ of holding property in New York City.

“This is a fundamentally unfair system that hurts working New Yorkers,” Mamdani, who ran on taxing the rich, said in April. “Now, it’s coming to an end.”

The tax has faced criticism from wealthy New Yorkers since the beginning, though some experts argue that their claims the tax will set off capital flight are overblown.

“I don’t think a lot of the typical concerns about migration are concerns when it comes to the pied-à-terre tax,” Emily Eisner, executive director and chief economist at the left-leaning Fiscal Policy Institute, told The Guardian. “I’m not concerned about dampening real estate markets.”

Mamdani angered figures across the business world in April by standing outside of Wall Street billionaire Ken Griffin’s luxury building to promote the tax.

In the fallout, Griffin and his hedge fund threatened to pull out of planned skyscraper project, though the development is still moving forward with Griffin’s Citadel as an anchor tenant.

Mamdani’s pied-à-terre tax is part of a larger wave of populist policies bubbling up from the Democratic party’s left flank.

In California, a proposal for a one-time tax on billionaires to make up for Trump administration health funding cuts has angered the state’s vaunted tech industry and divided Democrats in the state.

Donald Trump’s estranged niece has likened his suddenly voluminous hairstyle to Hermey the Elf from the animated “Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer,” claiming the recent hair obsession mirrored one his late father went through as he struggled with dementia.

Speaking on SiriusXM host Dean Obeidallah’s YouTube show, Mary Trump reacted to viral online speculation surrounding the president’s hairstyle that was sparked during a campaign rally in Nevada this week.

“I’m not going to say anything about whether it looked good or not. I don't really care,” Mary Trump told Obeidallah. “However, he looked like Herby the Dentist from ‘Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer’ — that’s what, that was my takeaway.”

She went on to draw parallels between the president’s hair consciousness and his late father, developer Fred Trump. According to Mary, the elder Trump grew increasingly preoccupied with his hair loss after being diagnosed with Alzheimer’s disease, eventually wearing an ill-fitting toupee and dyeing both his hair and mustache.

“He would leave the dye on too long. So he would end up with a magenta mustache,” she said, adding that family members, including Donald Trump, found the situation embarrassing. “And now here’s Donald potentially... being all obsessed about his hair kind of like his dad.”

President Trump’s suddenly opulent hair at an appearance in Las Vegas (pictured) has sparked debate online, including comments from his estranged niece, Mary Trump, claiming his sudden hair obsession mirrors his late father’s struggle with dementia ( AFP/Getty )

Obeidallah noted during the interview that the elder Trump began showing signs of dementia around the same age Donald Trump is now, questioning whether the sudden shift in appearance could be connected to cognitive changes.

President Trump has repeatedly touted having aced cognitive tests administered by his White House health team.

The commentary follows a flurry of viral reactions to the president’s speech at the Red Rock Casino Resort and Spa in Las Vegas, where he spoke on economic policies, endorsed local Republican candidates and referred to Canadian leadership as “nasty.”

Social media users quickly began debating the source of the president's updated look.

“Is Trump rocking a wig, or what the hell is going on here?” one user user asked, after posting: “Trump's hair, uh, has a lot more volume than normal.”

Former Republican Rep. Adam Kinzinger, who previously voted to impeach Trump, also weighed in, posting on X: “Trump has a weave!!”

The official Democratic National Committee account posted a photo of the president from three months earlier featuring a flatter, slicked-back style to emphasize the contrast.

Supporters defended the president’s appearance.

“This is proof that President Trump is aging in reverse,” one supporter wrote on X. “His hair looks absolutely amazing today.”

The president has previously acknowledged his efforts to maintain his signature hairstyle. At a CPAC conference in 2018, he admitted to the audience, “I try like hell to hide the bald spot, folks. I work at it.”

During a 2015 campaign stop in South Carolina, he brought a woman on stage to verify his hair was real, and in 2016, he famously allowed host Jimmy Fallon to mess up his hair during an appearance on The Tonight Show.

The Independent has contacted the White House for comment.

When George W. Bush penned an essay this year about a president named George, he notably sidestepped any mention of Donald Trump.

This omission was mirrored by Barack Obama and Bill Clinton, who also contributed to the In Pursuit project. This 250th-anniversary series invited a roster of historians and authors to craft pieces on various presidents or first ladies.

While explicitly designed to rise above contemporary politics, some essays within the project nonetheless echo anxieties currently flaring in the era of President Donald Trump, particularly concerning the exercise of power, the health of democracy and the integrity of the presidency.

The initiative is curated by Colleen Shogan, the U.S. archivist who was fired without explanation by Trump last year. She instructed contributors to avoid partisan or ideological stances. "Everybody took those instructions and that guidance very seriously," Shogan told The Associated Press, emphasizing the goal for all Americans to "feel welcome to be able to read these lessons and essays and learn something from them."

open image in gallery The project is being curated by Colleen Shogan, the U.S. archivist who was fired without explanation by Trump last year ( Mandel Ngan/AFP via Getty Images )

The mission, Shogan said, “is to surface the lessons from the past 250 years of American history, so that we can learn from those lessons, from both our successes and our failures, so we can plan for the present and the future. It’s what has been described as debriefing the American story.”

The essays cover 43 presidents — all but Democrat Joe Biden and Republican Trump — and 30 first ladies. They are being published chronologically and weekly into December.

Trump and Biden were judged too fresh to be appraised by history, a call that may have also set aside passions of the moment.

Without naming Trump, Bush’s essay is difficult to read without thinking of Trump’s reluctance to cede power after his 2020 election defeat and his musings about a third term in defiance of the Constitution’s two-term limit.

Bush hails the heroism of humility

Bush's essay celebrates George Washington, the original “No Kings” guy. Bush, a Republican, hails a man whose legacy only grew larger because he modeled the limits of the presidency for centuries to come.

“Our first president could have remained all-powerful,” Bush writes, “but twice he chose not to. In so doing, he set a standard for all presidents to live up to.” First, Washington resigned as commander in chief of the Continental Army, then set the precedent of serving only two presidential terms before that limit was enshrined in the Constitution.

Bush went on: "George Washington’s humility in giving up power willingly remains among the most consequential decisions and important examples in American politics.” Bush's essay, released Presidents Day as the first in the series on Substack, drove heavy engagement.

Retired Gen. Stanley McChrystal, who led U.S. and international forces in the Afghanistan War, sized up a fellow general, Ulysses S. Grant, in another essay that drew much attention for its parallels with today.

open image in gallery Bush, a Republican, hails a man whose legacy only grew larger because he modeled the limits of the presidency for centuries to come ( Melina Mara / POOL / AFP via Getty Images )

History offers lessons on ‘law over loyalty’

McChrystal presents the Union general and post-Civil War president as a leader who displayed “an absolute commitment to principles larger than personal ambition" and who, before his presidency, resisted pressure on military leaders to “align with political factions and be loyal to a person rather than the Constitution.”

The emphasis on personal loyalty resonates in a time when Trump has repeatedly demanded fealty from officials in his administration.

The “temptation to bend institutions toward personal power is not unique to Grant’s era,” McChrystal writes. “Our future still depends on whether our leaders choose law over loyalty.”

This month, in the latest In Pursuit installment, Democrat Clinton writes about Theodore Roosevelt, focusing on that president's drive to expand the universe of “we the people” at the expense of powerful corporate interests, while also emphasizing Roosevelt's exclusionary views on Black and Indigenous people.

The essays frequently address presidents’ failures alongside their accomplishments, a contrast with Trump’s calls for federal cultural institutions to stick to patriotic interpretations of American history.

Presidents, the chief justice and first ladies contribute

Among the In Pursuit contributors are Chief Justice John Roberts (writing about William Howard Taft, the only president who also served on the Supreme Court); Hillary Clinton ( Eleanor Roosevelt ); Michelle Obama ( Jacqueline Kennedy ); GOP operative Karl Rove ( William McKinley ); documentarian Ken Burns ( Franklin D. Roosevelt ); and historian Michael Beschloss ( Lyndon Johnson ). Democrat Barack Obama presents Abraham Lincoln.

The project is being staged by More Perfect, a nonpartisan alliance of dozens of presidential centers along with academics and organizations dedicated to advancing democracy. It is where Shogan now practices her archivist craft that Trump shut down by firing her in February 2025.

open image in gallery Hillary Clinton is also among the In Pursuit contributors ( Charly Triballeau/ AFP via Getty Images )

She still has not been told why. Nor has Congress apparently been notified of the reason. The law requires Congress to be told but does not specify a deadline. The National Archives is the central repository of federal documents both precious and routine, and its leader has discretion over which records to preserve and display, and how.

“That is a position that used to be a nonpartisan position, much like the Librarian of Congress, the secretary of the Smithsonian,” she said. “And I took that very seriously and acted the entire time when I was archivist in a nonpartisan way.”

The White House did not respond when asked why Trump fired the archivist and whether the administration will tell Congress the reason.

Trump has long begrudged the archives for notifying the Department of Justice of his alleged mishandling of classified documents after he left office following his first term, though Shogan was not working for the agency then.

Shogan sees hunger for history without a slant

Shogan said she has been overwhelmed with the public response to the series so far and figures that speaks to a hunger for history shorn of partisanship. The essays have received more than 1 million cumulative views on Substack and her podcast of the same name registered 160,000 audio downloads and nearly 64,000 YouTube views at last count. A documentary about the series is scheduled to air on PBS in October.

In the essays, readers learn something new not just about the giants, but about presidents such as Millard Fillmore — “a historic punchline — best remembered, ironically, for being so forgotten,” in the words of his essayist, former New York congressman Steve Israel.

Then there was Franklin Pierce, presented by his essayist as a pro-slavery president and “permanent victim” of Washington's alcohol-soaked culture.

Yale history professor David W. Blight recounts how Pierce won the presidency for the Democrats in 1852 despite vicious trolling by the Whigs. Fielding Mexican War veteran Gen. Winfield Scott in that election, they labeled Pierce, who also served in the war, the “hero of many a well-fought bottle.”

A pair of baby giraffes that vanished last year from a notorious roadside zoo in Virginia were hidden from authorities with the help of a federal informant who allegedly double-crossed investigators by sharing sensitive intel about the investigation with one of the prime suspects, according to a search warrant application obtained by The Independent.

The 35-page affidavit reveals a slew of previously unreported details about the desperate search for the newborns, which went missing from the Natural Bridge Zoo in April 2025 and prompted actress and animal welfare advocate Alicia Silverstone to offer a $50,000 reward for their return.

In the affidavit, a special agent with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service describes trying to track down the two giraffe calves while Patrick Robinson, a Tennessee animal handler turned government snitch, purportedly helped undermine the investigation he was supposed to be supporting.

The feds say Robinson hamstrung agents looking for the giraffes when he broke a written agreement not to divulge any information he gleaned about cases he was asked to collaborate on, allegedly telling a Natural Bridge Zoo insider about planned operations by law enforcement that involved the missing animals. He also shared private messages between him and his FWS contact, and participated in at least one conversation about moving the giraffes in secret to keep from being found.

Reached by phone on Wednesday, Robinson confirmed his involvement in the case and told The Independent, “I was a confidential informant, so I don't know how that goes with my agreement with them. I was in it from the ground up, but I don't know what I can comment on and what I can’t comment on.”

Robinson’s work as a federal informant began in 2022, according to the affidavit, Robinson approached FWS agents in Texas with “information related to” the Big Cat Public Safety Act, a federal law enacted that same year restricting private ownership and the public display of lions, tigers, leopards, jaguars, cougars and cheetahs.

open image in gallery The two baby giraffes that disappeared last year from the Natural Bridge Zoo in Virginia, following their successful recovery in June. A federal informant is now under investigation for allegedly helping impede the search by sharing confidential information with a suspect ( Office of the Attorney General, Commonwealth of Virginia )

The following year, FWS Special Agent LaGesse was assigned to be the main point of contact for Robinson, who the affidavit says “claimed to be knowledgeable on individuals who were violating the Lacey Act and the Animal Welfare Act.”

The Lacey Act is a federal conservation law passed in 1900 that restricts the sale and transport of protected wildlife and plants.

“My initial discussions with Robinson focused on individuals who were illegally transferring primates throughout the United States,” La Gesse wrote in the affidavit.

On September 11, 2023, Robinson signed a “Cooperating Private Individual Agreement” with FWS, according to the affidavit, which was filed under seal last February. In the agreement, Robinson swore to “always provide truthful and complete information,” and promised not to “divulge orally or in writing any information related to this investigation unless authorized to do so.”

Around this time, the Natural Bridge Zoo was coming under scrutiny amid a state-level investigation into filthy conditions and animal neglect. On December 6, 2023, the Virginia Attorney General’s Office seized nearly 100 animals from the zoo, including four adult giraffes, one male and three female. But, the affidavit says, the AG’s office didn’t have the specialized equipment necessary to transport the giraffes, so they remained at the zoo until proper arrangements could be made.

That October, after a period of legal wrangling, a final court order was entered allowing the county to retrieve the three giraffes, two of which were now pregnant.

Since the duo had entered their third trimester of pregnancy, the affidavit says the county’s experts and veterinarians recommended they not be moved until they birthed their calves. On April 8. 2025, a criminal investigator with the AG’s office, a Virginia state trooper, and a veterinarian paid an unannounced visit to Natural Bridge Zoo, and discovered that both giraffes had already given birth. However, the affidavit states, the two newborns were nowhere to be found.

open image in gallery An unsealed search warrant application reveals a slew of new details regarding the year-long search for a pair of baby giraffes that vanished from the Natural Bridge Zoo ( Google Maps )

Shortly after the baby giraffes disappeared, LaGesse met with Robinson in the parking lot of a Morrison, Tennessee, barbecue restaurant to check in and renew their cooperation agreement, according to the affidavit.

“I then proceeded to discuss various ongoing investigations with Robinson and potential next steps,” it continues. “Notably, I asked Robinson if he had any new information regarding the pair of giraffes missing from the Natural Bridge Zoo. Robinson inquired, ‘Have y’all still not found them?’ and then stated he did not have any new information.”

Robinson had already told LaGesse that he had been contacted by Sondra Scott, a paralegal, U.S. Army veteran, and “self-described advisor” to the Natural Bridge Zoo who runs an organization called Two By Two 4U, which touts its “track record of unparalleled success in navigating challenges posed by the USDA and animal rights activists.” and showed him limited screenshots of a text chain during which she asked if he had “a place for giraffes,” according to the affidavit.

However, it alleges, when LaGesse asked to take a look at the rest of the messages, Robinson’s tone seemed to shift.

“I asked Robinson if I could see his phone to review the conversation, which was a routine practice that Robinson had agreed to on previous occasions,” the affidavit states. “... Robinson agreed and opened his phone to find the conversation.”

Robinson typed the word “giraffe” in the search bar of his iMessage app, located the pertinent text messages, and handed the phone to LaGesse, according to the affidavit.

“As I was reviewing the phone, Robinson frequently interrupted me and asked, ‘What's that a picture of? What are you looking at?’” the affidavit alleges. “After repeated inquiries, I asked Robinson what the problem was, and [he] stated, ‘There’s stuff on there I don’t want you to see.’”

open image in gallery The US Fish and Wildlife Service became involved in a state-level investigation into a pair of missing baby giraffes after a confidential informant shared limited information abut their whereabouts, according to a newly unsealed search warrant application ( Getty Images )

Robinson told LaGesse that Scott “had sent him sexually explicit photographs,” the affidavit states. The agent responded that he “was not concerned with his personal life,” but that he was “just trying to get more context regarding the giraffes.”

LaGesse kept reading, until a series of screenshots that Robinson had sent to Scott caught his eye, according to the affidavit.

“The first image was a screenshot of a text message conversation with the contact listed as ‘USF&W,’” it says. “I then recognized the text as one I had previously sent Robinson.”

In the message string, Robinson asked LaGesse about funding for upcoming operations, and if he should make contact with Scott when he saw her at an upcoming exotic animal sale in Madison, Florida. LaGesse responded that his budget was limited at the moment, but told Robinson to “definitely talk to [Scott] next week so we can get a plan together,” the affidavit states.

“When I asked Robinson why he shared our conversation with Scott,” the affidavit says he “got upset, grabbed his phone from my hand, and exited the vehicle.”

Scott at the time was an “active target” of multiple wildlife trafficking cases, and, according to the affidavit, LaGesse feared he had exposed “detailed potential investigative steps specific to Scott and numerous other targets.”

Anything that Robinson may have divulged “severely undermines, obstructs, and impedes those investigations,” while helping Scott “avoid detection and prosecution” for Lacey Act violations, according to the affidavit.

Scott had already raised eyebrows during litigation involving Natural Bridge Zoo and accusations of animal mistreatment, encouraging supporters to “stalk” family members of the team that removed the animals on behalf of the state and “engag[ing] in name calling and made false allegations directed towards the court” on social media, the affidavit says.

open image in gallery Natural Bridge Zoo owner Gretchen Mogensen, seen here after her arrest on contempt of court charges for refusing to reveal where the missing giraffes were located ( Rockbridge Regional Jail )

On April 28, 2025, a judge granted LaGesse access to Robinson’s phone records and iCloud account, in a search for “evidence of wildlife trafficking, ongoing criminal investigations, impersonating a government official, and conspiracy,” according to the affidavit.

In a photo folder, LaGesse found screenshots of a “fabricated conversation” between Robinson and LaGesse’s boss at FWS, which the affidavit says made it appear as though Robinson, while posing as an FWS higher-up, had been bribing FWS brass. LaGesse also discovered a voicemail from Scott to Robinson, saying, “Hey, um… we need to go ahead and get a plan in action to move the baby G’s… so call me when you can.”

Months went by, and the baby giraffes remained missing. In November 2025, Natural Bridge Zoo Owner Gretchen Mogensen, 42, was jailed for 100 days after refusing to divulge the location of the giraffes or hand them over. (Scott at one point also faced a contempt charge, which was later dropped.)

As February 2026 rolled around, Mogensen and her parents – who co-owned the zoo – along with a veterinarian and an elephant trainer who worked there, were charged with a total of 55 misdemeanor counts of torturing, overdriving or cruelty to animals, and eight felony counts of forgery of a public record.

On June 15, after searching for more than a year, the Virginia AG’s Office announced the two baby giraffes had finally been located and rehomed at a safari park in Georgia. It remains unclear where they had been, or how they were finally found.

In a press release, the AG’s office said, “Due to the ongoing criminal investigation, no further details can be released at this time.”

Robinson has not been charged with a crime, according to a review of federal court records. On Wednesday, a spokesperson for prosecutors overseeing the investigation told The Independent, “It is a policy of the U.S. Attorney’s Office to neither confirm, nor deny, nor discuss the status of any pending investigation.”

The Mogensens’ trial, the first of three, is set to begin in February 2027.
