Apple TV+ hit Ted Lasso is finally back on our screens – although fans will have noticed that a number of its stars haven’t returned for the new series.

The comedy-drama’s fourth season sees Jason Sudeikis’s endlessly optimistic football coach return to the UK to lead Richmond’s Women’s Football Club with the help of Roy Kent (Brett Goldstein), owner Rebecca Welton (Hannah Waddingham), coach Willis Beard (Brendan Hunt) and Keeley Jones (Juno Temple).

However, with the series’ new focus being the women’s team, the likes of Phil Dunster – who played midfielder Jamie Tartt – as well as Toheeb Jimoh, Kola Bokinni, Cristo Fernández and other stars who played footballers have not reprised their roles.

Now, actor and co-showrunner Hunt has shed more light on why they weren’t invited back.

open image in gallery Phil Dunster as Jamie Tartt in 'Ted Lasso' ( Apple )

In an interview with Variety, Hunt said that Dunster couldn’t make filming work with his schedule, adding that it also would not have made narrative sense for the Richmond FC Men’s team to still be kicking about. Dunster currently stars in Steve Carrell comedy Rooster, another show from Ted Lasso creator Bill Lawrence.

“Phil was going to be busy, but also, it would have strained credulity a bit further than we wanted to if all the old team were still on Richmond,” Hunt said.

“If this team is doing so well, then the best players would be gone. They’d be bought by bigger clubs.”

Hunt also revealed that it took Sudeikis a while to consider whether Ted Lasso should come back after season three, which he previously had said was its final outing.

“There would be one sort of baby-step text message of intrigue, like every three months,” he said. “I never got my hopes up. I really wanted to do it, but I wanted him to want to do it. I didn’t want to be among the people who were pushing him or pressuring him. So I never brought it up.

“Anytime he brought it up, I’d be like, ‘Sounds good,’ and then wait and see if it ever came up again. When, finally, I got the word of, ‘It’s happening, we’re going to do that women’s team thing that I’ve been thinking about,’ it was like ‘Great! Now I can get on with my life! Let’s go!’”

open image in gallery Jason Sudeikis with new star Tanya Reynolds in 'Ted Lasso' season four ( PA )

Sudeikis previously spoke about having to tell the former Ted Lasso stars that he had written them out of the show, revealing last month that he had “very difficult” individual phone calls with them.

“Because I didn’t want them to hear it on the internet,” the Saturday Night Live alum told the outlet. “And because I love those guys and we all went through something together.”

However, the show appeared to pay tribute to its old cast in the series four premiere, with Ted looking at a wall of AFC Richmond memorabilia, which include a picture of the entire men’s team and a photo of former assistant coach-turned-viral-West Ham United coach Nathan Shelley (played by Nick Mohammed) jumping into Ted’s arms. The scene also includes a newspaper clipping announcing Jamie Tartt’s departure from the team, written by fictional The Independent journalist Trent Crimm (James Lance).

News.title: Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount
News.content:
Manchester United 1 Paris St-Germain 1

Manchester United’s pre-season went up a level against Paris St-Germain, but injury worries over Mason Mount and Tom Heaton clouded a good performance in Gothenburg.

A well-worked Bryan Mbuemo goal just after the half-hour mark cancelled out Ibrahim Mbaye’s second-minute opener, in a match that United had the better chances and looked the more-polished outfit.

Chances fell to Bruno Fernandes, the returning captain, and Shea Lacey either side of Mbuemo forcing a great one-handed save from Matvey Safonov in a second-half that Michael Carrick’s men controlled.

But while the performance would have pleased the manager, a first-half knock for Mount and second-half injury for Heaton were negatives on an otherwise good day for United. The foot injury to Mount, who has impressed during pre-season will be one that Carrick will especially want to find out is nothing too serious.

United’s pre-season sees them next take on Leeds in Dublin on Wednesday, before they face AC Milan three days later.

Their Premier League season gets under way against newly promoted Hull on August 22.

News.title: Joao Pedro double and Caicedo stunner give Chelsea win over AC Milan
News.content:
Chelsea 3 AC Milan 0

Chelsea cruised to a 3-0 victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head intothe break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

The London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto. Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Chelsea had further chances to extend their lead in a dominant second-half performance but were unable to add to their three goals.

Chelsea conclude their tour of the Far East with a game against Johor Darul Ta’zim on Sunday in Malaysia before returning home.

Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge before beginning their Premier League campaign at Fulham.

AC Milan take on Amorim’s former club Manchester United next Saturday before they kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

News.title: Gomes scores for Aston Villa in defeat by Bayern Munich in Hong Kong
News.content:
Aston Villa 1 Bayern Munich 2

Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side showed some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

Aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

News.title: Suspected Ebola case on packed Congo river boat sparks testing rush
News.content:
Congolese health authorities have intercepted and detained a river boat on its way to the capital after a suspected Ebola case onboard.

Authorities have set up a mobile clinic to test more than 200 passengers after one of them disembarked and died earlier on the voyage.

The boat travelling from the northeastern commercial hub of Kisangani was stopped and held in Maluku, some 40 miles from Kinshasa.

Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is dealing with its worst ever outbreak of the viral haemorrhagic fever, which has seen nearly 4,000 cases and killed around 1,801 people according to the latest government figures.

Samuel Roger Kamba, the health minister, said a 32-year-old man had disembarked in Pimu in Mongala province, before developing ‌suspected Ebola symptoms and dying.

“We did not say it was Ebola. We said there was a suspected case for which we are being cautious,” the health minister told a press conference, according to MediaCongo, a local news site.

He said there had been no other reports of deaths among travellers.

The virus has so far spread to five provinces, though more than 90 per cent of cases have been recorded in the north eastern Ituri region.

News.title: The best luxury hotels in the Cotswolds
News.content:
From gracious old farmsteads and magnificent manor houses to an ancient coaching inn creaking with Tudor character, the top luxury hotels in the Cotswolds combine a wonderful sense of history with contemporary style and outstanding modern British cuisine. Whether near picturesque Broadway in the north of the region or close to Bath in the south, location is a key attribute to them all: some offer serene escapes in acres of their own rolling parkland; others sit amid superb gardens; and several take over classic honey-stone villages that look as if they have been beamed in from a halcyon era of the past.

They all excel in providing creature comforts, whether crackling fires by kick-back sofas, canopy beds with soft throws, or suites with terraces and hot tubs. Facilities are top-notch too, ranging from beautiful bars and quiet terraces to blissful spas with inviting pools and even an opportunity for equine adventures. Read on to discover our pick of the best luxury hotels in the Cotswolds.

News.title: El Nino could cause explosion of rabid seals, animal health experts warn
News.content:
This year’s El Nino weather event risks propelling an outbreak of rabid seals around the world, the world’s animal health body has warned.

Countries in South America and Australasia are being urged to look for signs the deadly infectious disease has reached their waters, only two years after it was first confirmed in South Africa.

The 2024 discovery of rabies in South Africa’s Cape fur seals was the first significant outbreak ever found in marine mammals and has been described as a “significant shift in rabies ecology”.

More than 100 cases have been confirmed in South Africa and Namibia since then, raising fears that aggressive rabid seals could infect humans, pets and other wildlife.

Changing patterns in fish stocks caused by the El Nino phenomenon now potentially risk widening the spread, as uninfected seal populations migrate for food and come into contact with rabid colleagues.

Scientists believe warming sea temperatures off Antarctica could send seal populations northwards into Southern African waters, where they could be exposed to rabies.

They could then return to their home waters, taking the virus with them and infecting other seal populations.

News.title: ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality
News.content:
Arsenal 1 Real Betis 3

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he said: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

No Saliba a concern

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

News.title: Ebola outbreak outpacing containment effort, WHO chief warns
News.content:
Caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which there are no vaccines or treatments, it has been extremely difficult to contain, according to experts on the ground.

“The outbreak is spreading faster than our scale-up of the response, with new cases doubling in some hotspots over the past week alone,” Dr Tedros said on X.

Part of the difficulty is that the virus was circulating undetected for weeks before the outbreak was formally declared in mid-May, leaving health officials even now racing to catch up with the spread.

Prof Placide Mbala, director of research, clinical trials and innovation at Africa CDC, told the Telegraph: “It’s mostly the fact we arrived a bit late. It took us some time before we detected this virus outbreak. And when we detected the outbreak, we already had a total of I can say more than 200 suspected cases. It’s been difficult to catch up. That’s where we are.”

While the DRC has a wealth of experience in tackling haemorrhagic fever outbreaks, the effects of that initial delay are still being felt.

Prof Mbala said: “We have some experience dealing with the cases, the labs, the communication, the infection prevention and control.

“We have some experience... But my observation is that we were very slow, and it’s why we’re in this situation.

“We are slow detecting the people, slow responding, we are slow deploying people, we are slow to recruit the community healthcare workers to improve contact tracing, we are slow to deploy the safe burials.”

DRC’s largest outbreak had previously been from 2018 to 2020, when 3,481 cases were recorded.

The West Africa outbreak recorded 28,616 cases and 11,310 deaths according to the WHO.

Prof Mbala said insecurity was also severely hampering attempts to curb the virus. The outbreak epicentre is in Ituri province, which has been wracked by ethnic strife for decades and is also home to militias competing to control mining.

He said: “There are many, many mining groups controlling most of the mining places. We have a big issue with those places, because they are places where the response team cannot go.”

Medics and aid workers have also been undermined by violent public distrust of their efforts.

Locals in the area have either doubted the existence of the virus, or have accused health teams of deliberately spreading the infection, or somehow benefiting from it.

More than a dozen health facilities have been set alight and several health workers have been killed.

Prof Mbala said: “The local people, they also sometimes are very upset, because they believe that it’s a kind of a business, and people who are coming here, they are getting a lot of money, [so] don’t want this disease to stop.”

He said he hoped that immunity was starting to rise in some areas and this would start to curb transmission.

However there was also a risk that people fleeing the outbreak would spread the virus further afield.

He said: “The second scenario is the fact we are seeing people moving from the affected area to new areas, to run away from the response team because they do not want to go to the treatment centre.

“And in complicity with their family members living in other areas, they are now the ones who are spreading the disease to new areas

“So we’ll see new places affected because people are moving around from the affected zone to the non-affected zone.”

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford pictured partying with bikini-clad women on luxury boat as he shares £270 a bottle champagne & sips beer
Sports.content:
FOOTBALLER Marcus Rashford becomes Flash Rash on holiday as he throws his cash around for a group of girls on a luxury boat.

The England star shared a £270 bottle of Armand de Brignac Brut Gold champagne with pals.



He also wore an expensive pair of Louis Vuitton trainers, a chunky silver chain with a pendant that reads “Home is where the heart is” and a £23,000 black Hublot Square Bang Unico watch.

The 28-year-old, said to be paid £325,000 a week, enjoyed his post-World Cup break on a hired boat on the French Riviera with ten female pals — but with no sign of his girlfriend Lucia Loi.



A witness said: “The England lads played so well at the World Cup and deserve some downtime after a heroic third-place finish.

“It was kind of Marcus to share his time off with a group of stunning women on the ocean waves. He’s really living the dream.”





After a year-long loan to Spanish La Liga side Barcelona, Rashford is set for a return to boyhood club Manchester United for the new Premier League season, which starts later this month.

He is due to re-join Michael Carrick’s outfit next week, but has also been linked with an £80million transfer to clubs including Arsenal and Spurs.

Rashford made his debut for the club aged 18 in 2016 and went on to make 426 appearances in all competitions.

But he has not pulled on a United shirt since the Europa League tie against Czech side Viktoria Plzen in December 2024 and fell out with former Red Devils boss Ruben Amorim.

When Amorim left him out of the team for an 11th successive game, the manager said he would rather play his 63-year-old goalkeeping coach Jorge Vital than Rashford.



Amorim was in a stand-off with the England international, who previously declared he wanted a “new challenge” away from the club he spent more than a decade representing.



United sacked Amorim on January 5, 2026, after 14 months in charge, following a 1–1 draw against Leeds United and growing tensions with the club hierarchy.

Rashford could make his return in a pre-season friendly against Leeds in Dublin on Wednesday.

Then on Saturday, United play AC Milan — where Amorim is now the manager.

Sports.title: Man Utd forced to field unknown keeper who last played in non-league FOUR YEARS ago after injury crisis in PSG friendly
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED were forced to turn to little-known goalkeeper Dermot Mee after their injury crisis deepened against Paris Saint-Germain.

The 24-year-old was thrown into the action during United’s 1-1 pre-season draw with the Champions League winners in Gothenburg after Tom Heaton pulled up injured.



Heaton raced from his goal to make a clearance early in the second half before immediately grabbing the back of his right hamstring.

The veteran stopper was unable to continue, leaving United with little choice but to call upon academy graduate Mee.



And incredibly, Mee’s only senior competitive appearances came FOUR YEARS ago during a loan spell with non-league Altrincham in the National League.

The Birmingham-born keeper, who has represented Northern Ireland at youth level, has been on United’s books since the age of 11.

He has become a regular presence around the first-team training set-up in recent years while also representing the Red Devils at Under-21 level.

United clearly value Mee’s contribution behind the scenes, with the stopper recently signing a new two-year contract at Old Trafford.

But he would hardly have expected to be called upon against the kings of Europe.

Number one Senne Lammens was rested after returning early from holiday and Altay Bayındır joined Celta Vigo on loan, leaving United’s goalkeeping options threadbare when Tom Heaton went off.



And the goalkeeper headache was just one of several injury and disciplinary concerns to emerge from the 1-1 draw.

Mason Mount was forced off with an injury scare barely 20 minutes into the friendly after being named in Michael Carrick’s starting XI.

The former Chelsea star trudged from the field before holding a lengthy conversation with members of United’s medical staff and eventually heading down the tunnel.

It was another worrying sight for the injury-plagued midfielder, whose Old Trafford career has been repeatedly interrupted by fitness problems since his £60million move from Chelsea in 2023.

Young defender Ayden Heaven also found himself at the centre of controversy following a reckless challenge on PSG winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.



Desperate to make amends, Heaven flew into the tackle with his foot high off the ground and went over the ball.

A furious Kvaratskhelia was left needing treatment following the challenge, but Heaven escaped with only a yellow card.

The chaotic afternoon eventually finished 1-1 as United continued their preparations for the new campaign – but Carrick will be hoping his growing list of fitness concerns does not overshadow the rest of pre-season.

Sports.title: Manchester United boss Michael Carrick gives Mason Mount update and breaks silence on Marcus Rashford return
Sports.content:
MICHAEL CARRICK has downplayed concerns over Manchester United midfielder Mason Mount’s latest injury.

Mount was substituted after 20 minutes in United‘s 1-1 draw with Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg but jogged off the pitch.



The 27-year-old was walking freely when he made his way to the team coach after United’s fourth pre-season friendly and Carrick confirmed his withdrawal was a precaution.

“He got kicked,” Carrick said. “We just wanted to be careful and look after him.



“We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.”

Mount has played 72 times in three years for United, averaging only 24 appearances per season.



The former Chelsea player has been used in central midfield by Carrick during pre-season after he ended last season in a deeper role.

United are still lacking an available defensive midfielder, despite bolstering the area with summer signings Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.

Carrick also confirmed Marcus Rashford’s imminent reunion with United after an 18-month absence from the first team squad.

Rashford is scheduled to travel to Dublin for United’s training camp that coincides with their penultimate friendly against Leeds United at Croke Park.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Barcelona passed on the option to sign Rashford for £26million and the England international is United’s highest earner on £325,000 a week.

Rashford has not played for United since a Europa League tie away to Viktoria Plzen in December 12 2024 and has spent spells on loan at Barca and Aston Villa, but he could be in line for a return for his parent club.

Carrick was the United captain when Rashford made his debut against Midtjylland in February 2016 and also coached and managed the 28-year-old.

“I’ve played with him,” Carrick added. “I played in the game he made his debut, so we have a history.

“We have a full squad next week in Dublin. We fly straight there and meet Leeds on Wednesday.



“We have a few days in Dublin where we have the whole squad, including Marcus, Kobbie (Mainoo) and Lisandro (Martinez).”

Sports.title: Kind-hearted Xavi Simons hosts family of young footballer who tragically died in car crash at Tottenham friendly
Sports.content:
KIND-HEARTED Xavi Simons hosted the family of a young footballer who tragically died in a car crash last month at Tottenham’s behind-closed-doors friendly against Getafe.

Aspiring player George Dennis lost his life at the heartbreaking age of 11 following a road-traffic accident in North London on July 10.



Spurs star Simons learnt about the youngster’s sad passing via a post on X, from Grassroots, the UK’S No1 Grassroots Football Organisation.

The post explained what happened to George, who played for youth side Ongar Juniors and was nicknamed “Twinkle Toes”, and appealed for donations to support his family following their unimaginable loss.



Simons, 23, replied to the post by writing: “George’s family is welcome to join my family and I at any upcoming Spurs game. Sending all my love.”

The Dutchman, who is currently recovering from an anterior cruciate ligament injury, made good on his promise at Saturday’s 1-1 draw with Getafe.



He hosted George’s mother, father, sister and cousin for the 70-minute exhibition at the club’s Hotspur Way training complex, to which no other fans or any media were permitted to attend.

Simons watched the game with them and took the family on a tour of the training ground, as well as giving the children kits and boots, and flowers for George’s parents.

Tottenham signed the promising Simons from German side RB Leipzig after he burst onto the scene, beating off competition from Chelsea, who were also keen on securing his signature.

In a difficult first season, Simons showed glimpses of his quality, but with Spurs flirting with relegation, it was a challenging environment for him to showcase his full potential.



Just as he began to find his rhythm, he suffered an ACL injury that ruled him out of the final few games of last season.

However, he has been working his way back to fitness and is now hoping to put the struggles of last season behind him and help Spurs challenge for a Champions League spot this coming campaign.

Sports.title: Chelsea flop Alvaro Morata ‘set for immediate shock transfer exit less than two MONTHS after latest top-flight move’
Sports.content:
CHELSEA flop Alvaro Morata could be set to leave Europe just TWO MONTHS after joining a new club.

Reports coming out of Italy suggest the Spanish striker is on his way to the MLS, despite only signing for Como on a permanent deal this summer.



Italian outlet Di Marzio report that Atlanta United hold an interest in the Spanish striker.

The news comes despite Como exercising their obligation to buy Morata from AC Milan this summer.



The MLS club have reportedly turned their attention to the ex-Real Madrid, Chelsea, Atletico Madrid and Juventus star, after giving up on pursuing another former Chelsea striker in Romelu Lukaku.

The Belgian reportedly wants to stay in Europe.



Embracing the football scene in America might suit Morata, who failed to score a Serie A goal for Como last season, despite making 26 appearances.

He captained world champions Spain to Euros glory just two years ago, as they defeated Gareth Southgate‘s England 2-1.

Following his dream summer on the international stage, the Chelsea flop earned a move to AC Milan.

However, halfway through the campaign he was shipped out to Turkish giants Galatasaray for a loan spell.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

After a decent second-half of the season, in which he scored five goals in eleven league appearances, Morata returned to Serie A, joining Cesc Fabregas‘ Como on loan with a buy obligation.

However, playing under his former Chelsea team-mate didn’t seem to spark the connection they had back in 2018/19.

He managed ZERO goals in 26 Serie A appearances, with his only joy in a Como shirt coming in the Coppa Italia.

Despite his below-par performances, Como were forced to activate Morata’s buy option and signed him permanently.



However, they might not be overly keen on keeping the Spanish veteran who turns 34 in October.

But whether Morata fancies a switch to the USA is a whole different question.

Sports.title: Frank Lampard’s Coventry ‘make move for ex-Man Utd midfielder Angel Gomes with England international keen on transfer’
Sports.content:
FRANK LAMPARD’S newly-promoted Coventry are keen on former Manchester United midfielder Angel Gomes.

The Sky Blues have reportedly sounded out Marseille over a potential deal for the England international, who is keen to return to the Premier League this summer.



According to L’Equipe, Coventry are among the clubs to have made enquiries about Gomes’ situation.

Marseille are prepared to let the 25-year-old leave before the transfer window shuts if a suitable offer arrives.



Gomes has featured regularly during Marseille’s pre-season preparations and was deployed in his preferred No10 role during Wednesday’s 3-0 friendly win over Al Shahania.

But despite being involved in Bruno Genesio’s plans, the midfielder’s priority is understood to be a return to England.



Gomes came through Manchester United‘s academy and made his senior debut for the club as a teenager.

He eventually left Old Trafford in 2020 to join Lille, where he established himself as an important player before moving to Marseille on a free transfer last summer.

The midfielder spent the second half of last season on loan at Wolves but his time at Molineux proved difficult.

That has not dampened his desire to make another attempt at establishing himself in the Premier League.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

And Coventry could now provide Gomes with the opportunity he is looking for.

Lampard’s side secured promotion to the top flight this summer and are preparing for their return to the Premier League.

A move to the Sky Blues would give Gomes the chance to play regular top-flight football and rebuild his reputation in England.

Marseille, meanwhile, are willing to listen to offers.



Gomes joined the French club on a free transfer in the summer of 2025 and is understood to be among their higher earners.

OM are looking to reduce their wage bill and his departure would help free up funds for further additions.

Genesio is also keen to strengthen his midfield and is reportedly a big admirer of Feyenoord star Quinten Timber.

That could further increase the chances of Gomes leaving the Stade Velodrome before the window closes.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

For Gomes, the message is clear, he wants another shot at the Premier League.

And Lampard’s Coventry could now offer the former Manchester United wonderkid the route back home he has been waiting for.

Sports.title: Chelsea fire major warning to Arsenal as ‘rockstar’ coach Austin MacPhee inspires Blues to TWO set-piece goals vs Milan
Sports.content:
LOOK OUT Arsenal, there is a new Set Piece FC in town.

Chelsea showcased their newest lethal weapon to the world today, scoring twice from corners to stroll to a commanding 3-0 victory over Ruben Amorim’s dismal AC Milan in Jakarta.



That new weapon comes in the form of their high-profile recruitment from Aston Villa – not Morgan Rogers, but set-piece guru Austin MacPhee.

It is no secret the last Premier League season was defined by set-pieces.



And with Arsenal laying down the blueprint, it turns out improving your coaching staff in that department might genuinely be the smartest, cheapest way to spend your way to the Premier League title.

Chelsea’s new long-haired Scot might look like he should be playing drums for a metal band, but he is the latest set-piece rockstar ready to launch Xabi Alonso’s Blues right to the top of the table.

Or the set-piece table, at least.

The Blues paid an undisclosed release clause to snap him up from Villa after severely struggling to defend dead-ball situations last term.

But on today’s evidence, he is already making a staggering difference at the other end of the pitch.

It shouldn’t come as a surprise, given Villa fans spent last season chanting “Austin MacPhee, Ole, Ole” after winning the Europa League thanks to a decisive goal carved straight from one of his training-ground routines.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

During a chaotic campaign under three different head coaches, Chelsea finished as the eleventh-best team for set-piece goals, scoring eleven fewer than their table-topping London rivals and five fewer than MacPhee’s clever Villa, who ranked third best.

If today’s display is anything to go by, those numbers are about to skyrocket.

Moises Caicedo was the provider for Joao Pedro’s opener, whipping in a corner that completely bypassed Milan’s front-post ‘blockers’ – a technique used often by MacPhee at Villa last season.

The ball landed on the head of the Brazilian striker, who made no mistake by heading firmly into the ground and up into the roof of the net.



Pedro tapped in again from close range early in the second half, before another stroke of dead-ball genius sealed the third.

This time, MacPhee concocted an entirely different routine from the sideline alongside Alonso.

Romeo Lavia lofted a corner directly onto the outside of Caicedo’s right boot, and the midfielder’s terrific volley carried just enough backspin to take one bite on the turf and bend out of reach of Lorenzo Torriani in the Milan goal.

Of course, the heavy lifting for MacPhee lies in tightening up the backline.

Alonso’s side were barely troubled by Amorim’s toothless side in Indonesia, with Robert Sanchez not being forced into a single save all match, facing just two corners across the entire ninety minutes.

Last season, Chelsea ranked a lowly 12th in the top flight for defending set plays.

They also conceded eleven more goals from dead balls than Arsenal, and three more than MacPhee’s defensively resolute Villa setup.

That is where the most obvious improvement must happen.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Fortunately, with Chelsea missing out on European competition this year, MacPhee will enjoy precious extra time on the Cobham training pitch to drill his methods into the squad – far more time than former coach Bernardo Cueva ever had at his disposal.



If he does manage to get his methods working at both ends, we could soon be hearing “Set piece again, ole, ole” coming from the south west of London, as opposed to the north.

Sports.title: Man Utd player ratings: Bryan Mbeumo stakes claim to starting spot up front while Harry Maguire imposes himself vs PSG
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED stepped up their pre-season preparations as they took on Paris Saint-Germain in Sweden.

Michael Carrick was able to run the rule over his side against the reigning champions of Europe, albeit missing some of their biggest stars.



The match got off to a disastrous start for the Red Devils, with Ibrahim Mbaye firing PSG into the lead within the first two minutes.

Mason Mount was then forced off injured in a further blow for Carrick and Co.



United did regroup, however, with Bryan Mbeumo‘s leveller earning them a creditable 1-1 draw.

SunSport’s Samuel Luckhurst rates each United performer from Gothenburg.



Tom Heaton – 6

Had to make a double save shortly after conceding to Ibrahim Mbaye. Provided authority in goal amid the absence of numbers one and two, Senne Lammens and Karl Darlow. Went off injured early in the second half.

Noussair Mazraoui – 5

Caught out early on for Mbaye’s goal in what was his first appearance since the World Cup quarter-final. Started at right-back as competition between Mazraoui and Diogo Dalot resumed.

Harry Maguire – 7

Off the pace for Mbaye’s goal but grew in confidence and deceived Khvicha Kvaratskhelia a couple of times. Saw out the game and started to impose himself more, having a speculative strike.

Ayden Heaven – 4

Gearing up to start the season but may have thrown away his place. Caught ball-watching for the goal, he recklessly fouled Kvaratskhelia after a poor pass and was booked. A liability.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Luke Shaw – 6

With no Achraf Hakimi in the PSG side, United had some joy down PSG’s right-hand side and Shaw ably supported Patrick Dorgu. Also suffered a knock and was taken off at the same time as others.

Andrey Santos – 6

Having to settle into a defensive-minded role out of necessity and he was disciplined with his deep positioning. It would have been more useful had PSG pitted Santos against Joao Neves and Vitinha.

Mason Mount – 5

Forced off after 20 minutes with yet another injury. Time will tell how severe it is but it is another blow for a player who has averaged 24 games per season in his three years at United.

Amad Diallo – 6

An unsurprising improvement on his mixed performance against Atletico Madrid in Stockholm. After getting 45 minutes under his belt in the Swedish capital, Amad was more urgent and a greater goal threat.



Shea Lacey – 5

Quieter than on his influential showing against Atletico and struggled to impose himself in the No10 role. Not a memorable performance but more valuable experience.

Patrick Dorgu – 5

Much more urgent after an unconvincing afternoon against Atletico. Showed some versatility by occasionally switching to the right and his pace had PSG on the back foot. Faded in the second-half.

Bryan Mbeumo – 8

Another goal for Mbeumo as the centre forward. Aside from his fine strike, he tested goalkeeper Matvei Safonov with a couple of free kicks and a piledrive. Every chance he starts the season up front.



Substitutes

Tyler Fletcher – 6

An early arrival for the injured Mount, Fletcher acquitted himself confidently again in another substitute role. 6

Leny Yoro – 6

Replaced Heaven at half-time and it feels like those two are now competing to start alongside Maguire at Hull in two weeks. Involved in a tangle with Heaton that led to the goalie’s injury. 6

Diogo Dalot



Came on at the interval as Carrick introduced some added competition at right back. United’s final two friendlies against Leeds United and AC Milan will likely determine who starts at Hull.

Jack Fletcher – 6

Played on the right wing again.



Bruno Fernandes – 6

Endeavoured to make something happen on his return to the side.

Youri Tielemans – 6

Made his maiden United appearance alongside Tyler Fletcher.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Joshua Zirkzee – 6



Hurt by Matvey Safonov when he tried to get onto a through ball.

Sports.title: Mbeumo scores in encouraging Man Utd draw with PSG
Sports.content:
Bryan Mbeumo earned Man Utd a 1-1 draw with Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg, a pre-season friendly which left boss Michael Carrick encouraged by the "good signs" from his side.

A slow start, which saw Liverpool-linked Ibrahim Mbaye tuck in a PSG opener after just two minutes and the European champions - despite missing many of their star names - stretch United, was overcome and fears of an injury to Mason Mount were also allayed, with the midfielder later seen walking freely after being forced off during the first half.

The standout Amad Diallo was key to United shifting the momentum. He won the ball back high up the pitch to tee up Mbeumo for a fine finish for United's equaliser and proved too hot to handle for the PSG defence into the half-time break.

Mbeumo would have added to his tally had PSG's Matvey Safonov not been in such sharp form, although the goalkeeper left the pitch to jeers after escaping punishment for clattering Joshua Zirkzee way outside of his area.

Image: Youri Tielemans made his first appearance for Man Utd against PSG

At the other end, United goalkeeper Tom Heaton suffered a hamstring issue and had to be replaced. It was a problem which appears more significant than the injury Mount seemingly got to his left foot, which Carrick later suggested was just a kick. With Altay Bayindir loaned to Celta Vigo and Radek Vitek sold to Middlesbrough, 23-year-old Dermot Mee came on for his debut.

There were late chances for Tyler Fletcher, Shea Lacey and captain Bruno Fernandes - who linked up excitingly with new signing Youri Tielemans. United weren't able to find a winner but this was a performance to be positive about.

Man Utd team news: Tielemans on for debut as Bruno returns Youri Tielemans came on as a second-half sub to make his Man Utd debut in Sweden. Captain Bruno Fernandes also entered the action for his first minutes of pre-season.



Michael Carrick had made just one change from the side which started the win over Atletico Madrid last weekend, with Noussair Mazraoui coming in for Leny Yoro.



PSG were without their France stars Ousmane Dembele, Desire Doue or Bradley Barcola.

The key moments from Gothenberg...

2: GOAL! Ibrahim Mbaye tucks in the opener at the back post from Dro Fernandez's cross after Ayden Heaven is unable to cut it out.

4: SHOT! PSG threaten again with Khvicha Kvaratskhelia denied from distance by Tom Heaton.

16: BLOCK! Andrey Santos slides in to block Mbaye's shot over the bar with United stretched.

20: INJURY! Mason Mount is forced off injured with an apparent foot injury.

32: GOAL! Amad Diallo wins the ball back high up the pitch and feeds Bryan Mbeumo who cracks an equaliser across goal and into the bottom corner.

Man Utd on the front foot Man Utd had 24 touches in the opposition box. PSG managed just seven.

36: NO PENALTY! Amad's appeals are waved away when Willian Pacho nudges him as he goes for a header.

38: SAVE! For the second time in the match Mbeumo tests PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov with a free-kick shot.

48: INJURY! Heaton injures his right hamstring making a clearance and Dermot Mee comes on in his place.

54: SAVE! Stunning stop from Safonov to deny Mbeumo's shot towards the top corner from outside the box.

72: DRAMA! Safonov rushes out of his box and clatters Zirkzee with his shoulder as United try to counter no foul is given and after Jack Fletcher declines a long-range shot at the unguarded goal, Shea Lacey's effort is blocked behind.

87: CHANCES! Dalot's cross is met by Tyler Fletcher but he twice has efforts blocked before Lacey lashes over from a tight angle

89: CLOSE! Fernandes whips a shot just wide of the far post with a bouncing shot from outside the box.

Carrick 'enjoyed' PSG draw: 'We should have scored more goals'

Man Utd head coach Michael Carrick to MUTV:

"I enjoyed it. Good challenge. Slightly different with the way they play. We should've scored more goals.

"Very different to what we've played against, the boys adapted really well, so there were a lot of positives from the game. The things we were trying to get out of the game, a lot of it was there.

"It's good for the boys sometimes to have to problem solve and find their own way and I thought we did that. That prepares them for the season as well. In that respect there were a lot of things that maybe people don't always see that we were quite happy with. There were some good signs there."

Attacking positives for Man Utd in PSG draw

Sky Sports' Peter Smith:

"Man Utd's attack caught the eye on Saturday, with Bryan Mbeumo and Amad Diallo looking sharp and the connection between Youri Tielemans and Bruno Fernandes already clicking.

"Amad played a big part in shifting the momentum United's way after PSG's fast start. In the final third he won the ball back and passed it more than any other player on the pitch.

"That impact with and without the ball was clear when he found Mbeumo for the equaliser - and the striker's finish was excellent.

"Mbeumo could easily have scored more but for some good goalkeeping, landing four shots on target. No other player managed more than one.

"Debutant Tielemans and returning captain Fernandes could not be expected to be so sharp making their first minutes of pre-season - but still they produced some nice link-up play and signs they will be a big influence in this coming campaign.

"Tielemans' passing from deep was classy; Fernandes was immediately a threat around the edge of the box.

"As Michael Carrick said afterwards, 'good signs' for the season ahead."

Sports.title: Huddersfield Giants to leave home for Dewsbury amid major investment
Sports.content:
Betfred Super League side Huddersfield Giants have announced they are to leave the town and move to Dewsbury for the 2027 season onwards.

The Giants' intention is to move into Dewsbury's Flair Stadium, subject to RFL board approval, investing a projected £10m-plus in developing the ground.

The investment will deliver a transformational upgrade of the venue, including the construction of a new stand that will increase capacity from 5,000 to around 8,000 spectators, creating a viewing area on all four sides of the pitch.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Huddersfield Giants director of rugby Andy Kelly reflects on what he's described as the 'most challenging' period of time in charge of the club

The redevelopment will also feature refurbishment of the fan concourses, significant upgrades to existing and new hospitality suites, new bars and food areas, both male and female player dressing rooms, and press facilities elevating the stadium to Super League standards.

An agreement has been reached following extensive and amicable negotiations with Betfred Championship team, Dewsbury Rams, and a strong partnership between the two clubs has been forged. The Flair will continue to host the Rams in the newly-upgraded and dual-branded facility.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Huddersfield Giants prop Tom Burgess joins Jenna, Jon and Sam Tomkins on The Bench

This comes following a period of uncertainty for the Giants after seeking a permanent location in the Huddersfield area.

Owner of the club, Ken Davy OBE, has explored several alternative sites, including The Shay Stadium in Halifax.

Speaking of the decision, Davy said: "It's no secret that as a club, we have fought to find a home in Huddersfield. We had to move from Fartown, from Leeds Road, and now from the Accu Stadium. But the Huddersfield Giants will not retreat. We will not compromise or quietly shuffle into the shadows.

"While we remain the Huddersfield Giants, I am proud to announce that our stage for the 2027 season and beyond is Dewsbury.

"The Flair Stadium is the perfect location for us, it will have the right capacity and facilities for the Giants and its fans to thrive while we continue the search for our permanent home. Our one giant future starts now.

"My overriding aim is to create a purpose-built stadium within Huddersfield for the Giants to call home. My commitment on that has not wavered. However, that was not feasible for the 2027 season."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Huddersfield Giants against Hull FC from the Super League

Ralph Rimmer OBE, executive chairman of the Huddersfield Giants, added: "The Giants' future is bright, and we are excited to lead the club into this new era.

"For fans, the matchday experience will be our focus. A smaller, more intimate ground means the crowd is closer to the action, letting the atmosphere grow and support the team out on the pitch.

"The Flair Stadium offers everything that supporters need from parking and accessibility to corporate hospitality and function rooms.

"We can't wait to welcome you for the 2027 season and beyond to be a part of the Giant future we have in store."

Jackson: Dewsbury not yet Super Lsague ready

Huddersfield Giants non-executive director Rebecca Jackson:

"[Dewsbury flair stadium] is not quite Super League ready yet, so we definitely need to bring it up to standard.

"We'll be spending around £10m - a huge investment - to ensure that it can actually be the place where the Huddersfield Giants can play, and really have the atmosphere for both the fans and our partners - and that means building a new stand too, which is very exciting.

"This is just a medium-term plan. We are still looking to build our own stadium within Huddersfield, which has been something that we've worked on for a really long time.

"We've just unfortunately not been able to secure a site quite yet with the local authorities, but a lot of discussion has been happening.

"We're hoping that this is going to be able to be a bit of a stop gap for us - a medium-term solution - to then be able to get back into Huddersfield long term."

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+.

Sports.title: Moore helps GB and Ireland to Shergar Cup crown
Sports.content:
Ryan Moore bagged a Shergar Cup double on his return to the competition following a 20-year absence to help his Great Britain and Ireland team win the team event while he was also crowned leading rider over the six races.

Winner of the Silver Saddle on his last appearance at the team-based meeting in 2006, Moore has usually been required to ride on a Group One card in Ireland.

But with that meeting put back 24 hours he was free to attend and delighted the Ascot crowd.

Team Great Britain and Ireland topped the standings on 81 points from Team Hong Kong in second on 62, with Moore's individual haul of 47 enough to take the Silver Saddle.

He first struck on Dylan Cunha's Asgard's Captain (13-2) who stuck to his task gamely to win the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Challenge by a length and a quarter from Yutake Take on Sportingsilvermine for the Rest of the World.

Moore said: "Dylan did say he could be a little bit lazy, but he has an uncomplicated attitude and to just help him through it and it was straightforward, really.

"It's great to get Dylan a winner here today and the owners will be delighted as they were all looking forward to it, so it's a good job the horse has performed today."

In the penultimate Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Classic, he gave Marco Botti's Archers Bay (5-2) a textbook ride coming home three-and-a-quarter lengths clear of Christophe Lemaire on King Of Berkshire for Team Europe.

Having run in the Italian Derby earlier in the season, he looked the class act and so it proved.

In the closing Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Mile, Moore finished third on Ozat behind the Frida Valle Skar-ridden Crown Board (10-1), but her Team Europe were not in contention for top honours by then.

Saffie Osborne thrives in the team environment and got her name on the scoresheet when Tim Easterby's Red Spells Danger justified 2-1 favouritism in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Sprint.

Osborne was leading rider in the Racing League on three occasions and is captaining Moore and Dylan Browne McMonagle in Team Great Britain and Ireland.

She said: "I heard a few people knocking this horse today but I thought the track would really suit and it has. I'm just glad I pulled my finger out.

"Looking at the standard of jockeys here today, it's amazing - look at our team with Ryan Moore and Ireland's champion jockey.

"The win for me today is that I made Ryan laugh a couple of times, so I'm quite happy with that!"

Team Hong Kong had earlier set the pace winning the first two races.

Jerry Chau gave them the perfect start when partnering Tuco Salamanca to a clear-cut victory in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Dash.

Representing a team making its Shergar Cup debut, Chau, 26, gave Ollie Sangster's four-year-old the perfect ride, taking a lead into the final furlong before a gap opened up seamlessly.

Tuco Salamanca (4-1) quickened impressively to beat Gold Star Hero, ridden by Chau's team-mate Vincent Ho, by a length and a half.

Fandom and Suraj Narredu were third for the Rest of the World.

Chau told Sky Sports Racing: "It felt amazing when I hit the line.

"No words can describe riding a winner at Ascot. I grew up watching Ryan Moore on YouTube. I watched him as much as I could."

Luke Ferraris did not have to wait long to play his part for Team Hong Kong as after an opening race one-two from his team-mates, he drove home Dancing In Paris to win the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Stayers.

Riding the Ian Williams-trained 17-2 shot, Ferraris came with a late run to collar Moore on Andrew Balding's Shrimp Shady to win by a length.

Mountain Road was third for Yutake Take and the Rest of the World.

Ferraris said: "That's phenomenal, he's a lot fitter than me! He was turned out in great order.

"He didn't settle as good as he should have, but he still produced a great turn of foot.

"I think I've only ridden in one two-mile race in recent years, so it was a bit of a change.

"We've a good group of young riders representing Hong Kong, so let's hope it continues."

Sports.title: Nicholls pays tribute as Big Buck's dies aged 23
Sports.content:
Big Buck’s, one of the greatest staying hurdlers of all time, has died at the age of 23.

Owned by the late Andy Stewart, he was part of a golden age for trainer Paul Nicholls as he counted Kauto Star, Denman, Master Minded and Neptune Collonges among his stablemates.

Big Buck's had always been viewed by connections as a potential top-class chaser, however, a fall at the final fence in the 2008 Hennessy Gold Cup saw him revert back to hurdles and he never looked back.

He won what is now the Stayers' Hurdle a record four times, the Liverpool Hurdle four times and three times he came home in front in the Long Walk Hurdle.

Big Buck's, who struck up a great relationship with Ruby Walsh, was a fan favourite as he would often hit a flat spot in his races before powering to victory.

Nicholls told the Press Association: "Ability-wise he was probably as good as anything I've ever trained, it's just a shame he couldn't jump a chase fence.

"He was a wonderful horse for a wonderful owner who deserved to own a great horse like that. Andy enjoyed the whole journey and shared it with everybody.

"The horse had a brilliant life and had a great time with us and then a great time with Mike and Lucy Felton in retirement, but sadly time caught up with him.

"I was very lucky to have him at the same time as Kauto Star, Neptune Collonges, Master Minded and Denman. He was definitely as good as any of them."

Image: Big Buck's and Ruby Walsh formed a formidable partnership

One of the last surviving members of that halcyon period for the Ditcheat handler, Big Buck's would go on to pass Sir Ken and win a then record 18 straight National Hunt races when reverting to hurdles, an achievement only eclipsed by Altior since.

However, for Nicholls there will always be the question of how high he could have climbed if remaining over the larger obstacles.

"He won the Graded race at Aintree over fences, jumped 18 fences and jumped them 18 different ways and still won," said Nicholls.

"It made me think he was a certainty in the Hennessy and he was unlucky that day, but he just wasn't a natural jumper of a fence.

"If Kauto Star hadn't been about at that time then we probably would persevered over fences and he had the ability to win a Gold Cup. If he had won the Hennessy that day it would have definitely given us a headache and it would have been interesting where he would have ended up.

"But over hurdles he was invincible. Andy said I was bonkers, but going back over hurdles was the best thing we ever did. History tells you how good he was and Cheltenham, Aintree, Newbury, Ascot - if there was a big staying hurdle race, he won them all - all those Grade Ones on the trot, what a horse."

Big Bucks would become a standing dish on Thursdays at the Cheltenham Festival, with his famous flat spot often sparking nervous gasps from supporters before hitting top gear and surging up the Cheltenham hill under Walsh.

When asked to nominate just one race in Big Bucks' decorated career littered with so many great triumphs it was his fourth-straight success in the day three feature, when seeing off arguably the deepest field he met, edging out Irish raider Voler La Vedette, that Nicholls remembers most fondly.

"His fourth World Hurdle was the one that sticks out as being very special," said Nicholls.

"But we had so many great days with such a brilliant horse and we were all very lucky to be associated with him."

Sports.title: Burnley edge win on penalties, West Ham through in Carabao Cup first round
Sports.content:
Kyle Walker struck the winning penalty as Burnley edged out Notts County 4-3 in a shoot-out to reach the Carabao Cup second round after a 1-1 draw at Turf Moor.

Newly-promoted County, League Two play-off final winners over Salford in May, led through Callum Roberts at half-time before Zian Flemming equalised early in the second period for the Clarets.

Walker struck the winning penalty after Burnley goalkeeper Max Weiss had saved efforts from Notts pair Emile Acquah and Jacob Bedeau in the shoot-out.

West Ham came from behind to beat Portsmouth 3-1 at the London Stadium in their first match following relegation from the Premier League.

The Hammers fell behind to Adrian Segecic’s first-half opener, but turned it round before the break with Taty Castellanos and Jarrod Bowen on target, before the former notched his second in the second half.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Carabao Cup first round match between West Ham United and Portsmouth.

Substitute Jamal Lowe struck the only goal as Sheffield Wednesday beat 10-man Bolton 1-0 at Hillsborough.

Lowe scored midway through the second half after Bolton's Xavier Simons was sent off for punching Owls' on-loan Leeds striker Harry Gray in retaliation having been pulled back.

Millwall goalkeeper Lukas Jensen saved all four of QPR's penalties as the Lions won 2-0 in a shoot-out at Loftus Road after the game ended 1-1 after 90 minutes.

Luke Cundle had given Millwall a second-half lead before the Hoops hit back through a late own goal from Mark Sykes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Norwich City's clash with MK Dons in the first round of the Carabao Cup.

Norwich debutant Andre Brooks was on target as the Canaries cruised to a 4-1 win against MK Dons at Carrow Road.

Cardiff substitute Jack Moylan also scored on his debut, firing the winner as the Bluebirds won 3-2 against Swindon, for whom James Debayo was sent off for two yellow cards in the final six minutes.

August Priske's first-half finish sealed Birmingham a 1-0 win at Swansea and Marc Bola's stunning long-range strike deep in added time clinched Watford victory over Crawley by the same score.

Late goals from substitutes Andri Gudjohnsen and Jayden Fevrier secured Blackburn a 2-1 win at Burton.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Carabao Cup first round tie between Derby and Lincoln.

Newly-promoted Lincoln picked up where they left off last season, winning 2-1 at Derby thanks to first-half goals from Ben House and Dom Jefferies before Sammie Szmodics pulled one back for the Rams.

Ollie Norburn's own goal and Robert Bozenik's late effort secured Stoke a 2-0 win against Oldham at the bet365 Stadium and Bradford pair Will Swan and Aden Baldwin earned their side a 2-0 home win against Rochdale.

Fleetwood captain Ched Evans' first-half effort sealed his side a 1-0 home win against Chesterfield and Cambridge hit back to beat Barnet 2-1 through second-half goals from Ben Knight and Isaac Heath.

AFC Wimbledon, Barnsley and Reading progressed after winning on penalties against Newport, Wigan and Bromley respectively, while Preston, Shrewsbury and Doncaster came through respective shoot-outs against Huddersfield, Salford and Stockport.

Luca Moore's late goal sealed Crewe a 2-1 victory against Accrington at Gresty Road and late goals from Demetri Mitchell and Idris El Mizouni secured Leyton Orient a 2-0 home win against Oxford.

Peterborough, Luton and Blackpool all won on the road, at Bristol Rovers, Gillingham and Grimsby respectively, and Caleb Okoli's header secured Leicester a 1-0 home win against Northampton.

In the evening kick-offs, there was a 2-0 victory for Southampton as Cyle Larin and Romeo Akachukwu scored their goals at Colchester.

While West Brom won 4-1 at Rotherham and Charlton secured a 3-1 victory at Cheltenham.

When is the second round draw?

The draw for the second round of the 2026/27 Carabao Cup will be made live on Sky Sports Football on Monday August 10, during the build-up to the tie between Plymouth and Exeter.

The draw will feature all first-round winners, as well as the 11 Premier League clubs not participating in European competition.
