Sports.title: Fifa president Gianni Infantino denies claims Uefa paid off alleged ‘lover’
Sports.content:
Uefa has confirmed a “departure payment” was made to a female employee who is alleged to have been in a relationship with Gianni Infantino while he was the organisation’s general secretary, allegations Fifa has dismissed as “categorically untrue”.

The Daily Telegraph reported on Friday night that the woman received a six-figure sum following the alleged relationship with Infantino. In a statement, Uefa confirmed a payment was made along with covering the fees for an MBA course, which it said was “in line” with regulations at the time.

However, Fifa has responded to the reports. “Fifa president Gianni Infantino strongly denies these allegations, and they are categorically untrue. Any insinuation of inappropriate conduct or violation of statutes or regulations is defamatory,” a Fifa spokesman told the Telegraph. “No employee at Uefa and Fifa has ever raised a complaint regarding Mr Infantino’s behaviour because there never was an incident where he was involved.”

The report comes as pressure mounts on Infantino following his plan to seek private investment in a company which would run Fifa’s competitions, including the men’s and women’s World Cups. Infantino worked at Uefa for 16 years and was its general secretary from 2009 before being elected as Fifa president in February 2016.

A Uefa spokesperson said: “We are aware of the allegations and can confirm a departure payment was made to the individual in question, coupled with the payment of fees for a MBA course at a local business school.”

The payment was in line with the regulations that existed for departing staff at the time. “Such regulations have been tightened since 2016 and the current staff regulations – which apply to all Uefa employees at whatever level – reflect those found in a modern, high-profile organisation.”

Infantino has found himself at the centre of a storm for two weeks following his controversial plan to sell stakes to private investors in a company to run the World Cup. The plan was rejected by Uefa and two other continental confederations. On Wednesday, Infantino was backed by Fifa’s management board following a meeting in Morocco and issued an apology over the process.

Uefa’s threat for its 55 member countries to boycott Fifa competitions until the plan was scrapped remains, with the European confederation saying on Thursday that Wednesday’s announcement “changes nothing”.

Sports.title: West Ham sink Pompey in Carabao Cup as Sullivan ignores advice to stay away
Sports.content:
In an unseasonable black bomber jacket, with heavy duty company beside him, David Sullivan took his seat. Against the advice of the stadium’s operators, unbowed by serious allegations placed against his name and the weight of public opinion, West Ham’s major shareholder, the former co-chair, sat with arms crossed, always conspicuous by his presence.

By beating Portsmouth in relative comfort, West Ham, the club where Sullivan’s name is no longer above the door, had secured a heartening Carabao Cup passage to the second round. There, they will be reunited with their former Premier League peers. The serious Championship business begins next Sunday at Burnley. Whether Sullivan travels north for that remains to be seen. It cannot be ruled out.

“Neither me nor the players,” said Nuno Espírito Santo when asked about the effect of the uninvited guest’s presence. “We’ll focus on the pitch. The noise that comes from outside cannot distract at all; we’re going to find a lot of noise. We focus on the game, they do their job, they did it well.”

Before kick-off, the London Stadium big screen showed a “countdown to walkout”, referring to the players’ arrival rather than to fans deserting the scene in protest. This being West Ham in 2026, any confusion would be understandable. Taking previous mutinies into account, and despite a summer of intrigue and anger, there were surprisingly few audible or visible signs of insurrection as season 2026-27 began, and an extended 90 minutes was played out.

Even with Sullivan’s arrival expected, the gate to the directors’ car park did not stage a welcoming committee, the lanes around the London Stadium quiet. Protests there have been a regular sight, targeting Sullivan and his departed associate Karren Brady.

Even once Sullivan’s presence was confirmed there was nothing resembling the barracking of last season. Instead, the loudest boos of the first half came at a hydration break at its midway point, with an odd choice of 90s rave musical accompaniment. The legacy of a North American World Cup continues to darken.

View image in fullscreen David Sullivan takes his seat at the London Stadium just after kick-off. Photograph: Richard Pelham/Getty Images

Perhaps still-searing temperatures and a dose of early optimism had doused the fires raging when the Hammers’ drop was confirmed in May. Time-served Irons know plenty about relegation; their club has dropped down each decade since the 1970s; West Ham heritage indeed.

The kick-off chorus of I’m Forever Blowing Bubbles drowned out the Pompey Chimes ringing out from 9,000 away fans. As is usual at the London Stadium, the visiting contingent decried their surroundings and the Faustian pact struck for West Ham’s tenancy.

Football has rarely been in focus during West Ham’s summer of tumult, boardroom battles after Sullivan’s defenestration. So what of football? Carabao Cup Saturday served as a decent dry run for their attempt at a promotion campaign. The new West Ham closely resembled the former West Ham, though shorn of the £151m worth of player sales that took in Mateus Fernandes, Crysencio Summerville and Freddie Potts. Joël Veltman, the sole summer signing so far, came on with three minutes left.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

In midfield, Edson Álvarez, who spent last season on loan to Fenerbahce, lined up alongside Lewis Orford, a 20-year-old it is hoped can follow the path of Frank Lampard, Michael Carrick and Mark Noble, the latter a mentor, into becoming a first-team regular. His was a successful introduction into the first team.

“The energy of the young players is really really important for us,” said Nuno. “It’s up to us to develop the young academy players. That’s the vision for the future.”

The torpor of a first 30 minutes of little footballing consequence was broken by a Portsmouth goal, scored by Adrian Segecic, via a deflection off Maximilian Kilman, an expensive purchase far too regularly on the crime scene.

It took 10 minutes for West Ham to awaken before Mohamadou Kanté’s pirouetting feint laid up Taty Castellanos to equalise. Mere moments later, Jarrod Bowen, the club captain staying on to lead his club back up, a rare adult in the room last season, lashed in their second. “Jarrod shows us every day his commitment,” said Nuno.

The goals evidenced a quality that ought to guide the club back to the Premier League with some comfort, though nothing should be taken for granted. “If you give them a slight opening they’re going to take it,” said the Portsmouth manager, John Mousinho.

Sullivan kept any celebrations to himself and returned for a second half that began with Castellanos nodding in Bowen’s cross. An afternoon that might have descended into a familiar seething pit of rage and resentment now offered grounds for optimism. Though just beyond the hour, a chorus of “Stand up if you hate the board”.

If Sullivan is no longer a board member he was its undoubted target. He has turned many a deaf ear down the years and continues to do so.

Sports.title: Carabao Cup: Millwall keeper saves four penalties, Preston prevail in Goodison home game
Sports.content:
Alex Neil felt Lukas Jensen deserved his moment of glory after the fit-again goalkeeper saved all four QPR penalties to take Millwall through to the second round of the Carabao Cup.

After a 1-1 draw, with a late Mark Sykes own goal bringing Rangers level after Luke Cundle’s opener, Millwall won 2-0 in a shootout which included six missed spot-kicks. Jensen, back after a long injury lay-off, kept out penalties from Ilias Chair, Harvey Vale, Koki Saito and Kwame Poku.

The Millwall manager said: “To save four penalties is really, really rare. And to put in the context behind that, Lukas has been missing for 15 months – he had a bad injury and then came back and had a setback. I think he would have been dreaming about that moment for 15 months – making four penalty saves and being the reason we’re through to the next round. And I’m absolutely delighted for him because he’s a great professional and a good lad, so fair play to him.”

View image in fullscreen Lukas Jensen saves from Harvey Vale during Millwall’s shootout victory. Photograph: Andrew Fosker/Shutterstock

Burnley prevailed 4-3 in a shootout to book their place in the second round after the Championship club had been held to a 1-1 draw by League One Notts County at Turf Moor. Veteran defender Kyle Walker held his nerve with the winning kick after Clarets goalkeeper Max Weiss had saved from Emile Acquah and Jacob Bedeau.

Russell Martin celebrated his first competitive game in charge of Leicester with a 1-0 victory over Northampton thanks to Caleb Okoli’s first-half goal. The former Southampton and Rangers manager has been tasked with leading Leicester’s recovery following relegation to League One and overcame a spirited showing from League Two opponents at the King Power Stadium.

Andre Brooks scored on his debut as Norwich cruised to a 4-1 victory over visitors MK Dons. The Canaries made a blistering start at Carrow Road, pouncing on some sloppy defending to grab an early two-goal advantage. Mohamed Touré was put clean through by Kenny McLean after the Dons had made a hash of their first attempt to play out from the back and blasted home with just 40 seconds on the clock.

The hosts then made it 2-0 after seven minutes as Touré picked out Anis Ben Slimane who calmly found the corner. Norwich effectively settled the issue on 43 minutes when Brooks’ shot found the net via a deflection off Ben Chrisene, who was credited with the goal. The Dons pulled one back on 56 minutes through Ryan Wintle, but Brooks made it four just before the hour.

Tony Mowbray wants to see more cutting edge from his Blackburn side after his return to the club began with a comeback 2-1 win at League One Burton. Substitutes Andri Gudjohnsen and Jayden Fevrier netted late goals to secure victory after Zac Scutt’s opener. “We got there in the end.” Mowbray said. “We said at half-time that we should have scored four or five goals. Not could have. Should have.”

View image in fullscreen Jayden Fevrier celebrates scoring Blackburn’s second at Burton. Photograph: Andrew Kearns/CameraSport/Getty Images

Delano Burgzorg scored the winning penalty in the shootout after Jusef Erabi equalised in stoppage time for 10-man Preston to knock out Huddersfield. The game took place at Goodison Park, the former Everton men’s ground, due to Preston’s Deepdale pitch not being ready. Daniel Iversen saved two penalties, after a thrilling end to normal time that ended 1-1 when Erabi cancelled out Radinio Balker’s strike. Preston played 69 minutes without Lewis Gibson who was shown a red card.

Sheffield Wednesday’s manager, Henrik Pedersen, praised his team’s performance after they beat Championship side Bolton 1-0. Substitute Jamal Lowe scored in the 70th minute. Bolton had Xavier Simons sent off in the 56th minute when he received a red card after clashing with Harry Gray.

Pedersen said: “I saw a lot of steps in the right direction for our aggressive pressing, for our quick transition, more players higher up when we won the ball, more forward mindset. We keep on going, and they keep on working as a group. It means everything in this situation where we are.”

View image in fullscreen Players confront each other before Bolton’s Xavier Simons is shown a red card. Photograph: Lee Parker/CameraSport/Getty Images

Arkell Jude-Boyd scored the decisive spot-kick as Shrewsbury beat Salford 4-3 on penalties after a 1-1 draw. Both goalkeepers starred in a remarkable shootout which saw nine penalties missed before Jude-Boyd fired into the top corner.

An unlucky own goal from Ollie Norburn and a late strike from Robert Bozenik gave Stoke a 2-0 win over Oldham, while Birmingham booked their place in round two with a narrow 1-0 win at Championship rivals Swansea. August Priske’s goal a minute before the break proved decisive at the Swansea.com Stadium, with the big Danish striker steering the ball into the far corner after Carlos Vincente had sent a cross back across goal following a long free-kick into the box.

Fleetwood’s manager, Matt Lawlor, described the only goal in his side’s victory over Chesterfield as “Ched Evans in a nutshell”. New captain Evans struck 14 minutes in to seal the Cod Army’s place in the second round. Lawlor said: “He was brilliant. He sets standards at 37, while also challenging the young lads. We can use him as a reference point. That’s how you prepare for a game of football, whatever he does, replicate it.”

Reading beat League One new boys Bromley on penalties as they sunk five flawless spot-kicks to go through to the second round after a 1-1 draw. Goalkeeper Joel Pereira proved the match winner, saving Ethon Archer’s spot-kick to claim a 5-4 victory.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Derby crashed out after a 2-1 home defeat to Championship new boys Lincoln, who deserved their victory in the sunshine at Pride Park and could have won by a bigger margin. It took the Championship newcomers less than three minutes to go ahead when Ben House steered in a corner via a deflection off Matt Clarke. Lincoln were playing with confidence and a superb pass from Freddie Draper released Dom Jefferies to fire into the bottom right corner in the 23rd minute. Derby offered little until first-half stoppage time when Sam Szmodics struck from 25 yards.

View image in fullscreen Lincoln’s Ben House, centre, celebrates scoring their opener against Derby. Photograph: Chris Vaughan/Getty Images

The new Watford head coach, Alessio Dionisi, admitted he was relieved after his first game in charge needed a dramatic 99th-minute winner to sink League Two Crawley 1-0 at Vicarage Road. Dionisi, the Hornets’ 15th full-time appointment in seven years, watched his side squander a string of chances until Marc Bola’s 25-yard rocket.

The Italian said: “In the first half we played good, in the second only so-so. It is true we had a lot of shots and I agree it is better to win 1-0, but after 90 minutes it was 0-0 and to win football matches you have to score.”

Cambridge mounted a speedy comeback to beat Barnet 2-1. The visitors went ahead soon after half-time, but the Us hit back through Ben Knight and Isaac Heath to lead only eight minutes later. Leyton Orient struck late to seal a 2-0 win over Oxford at Brisbane Road, with both goals coming from crosses by Charlie Wellens, the son of manager Richie, who only came on after 84 minutes. AFC Wimbledon scored a late equaliser before beating League Two Newport County 5-4 on penalties.

Luca Moore’s late header earned Crewe a 2-1 victory over Accrington. The tie appeared destined to end in spot-kicks, but there was late drama five minutes from the end of normal time when Moore pounced just as John Doolan’s side seemed to be gathering momentum. Doncaster advanced into the second round with a 5-4 penalty shootout win over Stockport after the game had finished 1-1 over 90 minutes. Rovers’ keeper Tommy Simkin proved the hero, keeping out efforts from Ben Osborn and Eoghan O’Connell.

Charlton progressed with a 3-1 win at League Two Cheltenham. Nathan Jones’ side opened up a three-goal lead before half-time, with Matty Godden, Sonny Carey and Tyreece Campbell on target.

Substitutes Cyle Larin and Romeo Akachukwu scored inside the last 18 minutes to give Southampton a 2-0 victory at Colchester, while West Brom coasted into the second round with a 4-1 win over Rotherham. The damage was done early on with goals coming from debutant Jimmy Jay-Morgan and Harry Whitwell to make it 2-0 at the break. Albion then doubled their lead in a dominant second half.

Barnsley beat Wigan on penalties after the tie had finished 1-1 in normal time. The first 10 spot-kicks were scored before Jon Mellish’s effort was saved by the knee of Rogan Ravenhill and Josh Earl scored to make it 6-5. Jack Moylan scored the winner on his Cardiff debut as the Championship new boys squeezed into the second round with a 3-2 win over League Two Swindon. Moylan – who joined Cardiff in midweek from Lincoln – curled in the winner in the 77th minute.

View image in fullscreen Cardiff’s Jack Moylan celebrates with Joel Colwill after scoring their third against Swindon. Photograph: Gareth Everett/Huw Evans/Shutterstock

League One Luton cruised to a comfortable 3-0 victory over League Two Gillingham. Goals from Nahki Wells, Benny Benagr and Gideon Kodua made sure Jack Wilshere’s side impressed at the Priestfield Stadium. Blackpool secured progression with a 3-1 victory over Grimsby at Blundell Park, while League One Bradford eased their way into the second round with a 2-0 win over Rochdale.

Harry Leonard ensured Bristol Rovers’ Carabao Cup hoodoo continued as his penalty secured Peterborough a 1-0 win at the Memorial Stadium. Leonard’s first-half spot-kick for the League One outfit meant Rovers have exited the competition at the first hurdle for seven consecutive seasons.

Sports.title: Bruno Guimarães completes £75m Arsenal move: ‘I needed a new challenge’
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimarães says he “needed a new challenge in my life” after joining Arsenal from Newcastle for £75m and has targeted winning trophies. Guimarães is understood to have signed a four-year contract that contains a further one-year option after Newcastle reluctantly agreed to sell their captain.

The 28-year-old, who captained Newcastle to their first trophy since 1955 when they won the Carabao Cup last year, had made it clear that he wanted to join the Premier League champions after meeting the club’s new manager, Matthias Jaissle, this week.

Arsenal have previously shown an interest in signing Guimarães on two occasions – in 2020 when he was playing for Athletico Paranaense in Brazil and then 18 months later when he was at Lyon and went on to move to the north-east. But the Brazil midfielder said he wanted to join Arsenal after his first meeting with Mikel Arerta and the sporting director, Andrea Berta.

“I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a new challenge in my life and to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life,” he told Arsenal’s website. “After playing two World Cups, I’m at the point of my life, I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I’m in the right place to do it.

“I’m so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season, so the squad is going to be very, very important and I’m hopeful we can achieve our dreams.”

The arrival of Guimarães significantly boosts the midfield options available to Arteta, who now has a formidable squad that contains Declan Rice, Martin Ødegaard, Martin Zubimendi, Mikel Merino and Myles Lewis-Skelly.

“We are further strengthening the heart of our team,” said Berta. “As we have all seen, Bruno can play as a defensive midfielder and as a box-to-box player. He combines quality with quantity and has provided goals and assists for his team every year. Bruno will allow Mikel to further develop our playing style and will also increase our internal competitiveness, which is essential for maintaining the standards required when we are aiming to win major trophies.”

Guimarães revealed he has already received a message from Rice welcoming him to Arsenal that said “come here and please no more fights, now we’re friends”. “I was happy he messaged me, but the midfield we have here, is one of the best in Europe,” said Guimarães. “Everyone is an amazing player. I’m so excited to start chatting and play, and know the players very, very well,”

View image in fullscreen Bruno Guimarães said leaving Tyneside was ‘one of the toughest decisions of my life’. Photograph: David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty Images

Guimarães also released a statement to Newcastle. He said: “I fell in love with this place. I really mean that. From my first day, the supporters, my teammates, Eddie [Howe] and the staff, and everyone connected with the club made me and my family feel at home.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“This is one of the toughest decisions of my life. When I arrived, the club was in a challenging position and I am incredibly proud of what we achieved together. I thank PIF, our chair, Yasir Al-Rumayyan, and Jamie Reuben for everything they have done for me and for this football club. I also want to say thank you to David [Hopkinson, the Newcastle CEO] and Ross [Wilson, Newcastle’s sporting director] for the huge respect to me throughout this process. They did everything they could to keep me at Newcastle, and I am very grateful for our time together.”

On Friday, Wilson said they had no option but to allow Guimarães to leave. “What we had to weigh up was, very respectfully from Bruno with his behaviour towards us, very emotionally as well, he effectively told us he wanted to leave,” he said.

“That doesn’t mean he can go, but it certainly plays a part in what our thinking is when we hit a certain range of number. There’s no part in saying it was part of our strategy and was in our thinking this summer – it wasn’t. But we have got to be flexible and react to things that happen.”

Sports.title: Jorge Messi, father and agent of Argentina great, dies aged 68
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi’s father and agent, Jorge, has died aged 68 at a medical clinic in the ⁠Argentinian city of ⁠Rosario after ​a long illness, the family have announced. Jorge Messi spent his final months ⁠alternating between a medical centre in Rosario and his home, accompanied by his wife, Celia, and his ⁠children Rodrigo, Matías and María Sol.

Lionel Messi ​spent time with his ‌father after the World ‌Cup before rejoining his club, Inter Miami, for whom he ‌returned to action a week ago. Inter Miami are due to play Monterrey on Saturday at home in the 2026 Leagues Cup, but the MLS club have yet to announce whether he will feature.

Newell’s Old Boys announced the death in a social media post that said he had undergone treatment in recent months for an unspecified illness. The post described him as “the pillar and the person who, with vision, rigour and affection, supported the career of the best player of all time, alongside his wife, Celia Cuccittini”. The Argentinian FA also expressed its ⁠condolences in a statement, saying: “From here, we stand in solidarity ​with the entire family ​during this difficult time and send ​the most heartfelt, warm, and affectionate embrace. Strength to you all.”

View image in fullscreen Lionel Messi poses with his brother Rodrigo, sister María Sol, father Jorge, mother Celia, nephew Tomás and brother Matías in Rosario, Argentina, in 2003. Photograph: El Grafico/Getty Images

At the World Cup, Lionel Messi said after Argentina’s 3-0 victory over Algeria – when he broke down in ​tears while celebrating ​his first goal in the team’s opening match – that he was going through a difficult personal situation. Later, he explained his tears ​were due ‌to “something unrelated to ​football” after ​going through “a few difficult, complicated days”.

There was speculation that the player’s emotional reaction to Argentina’s last-16 victory over Egypt was due in part to his father’s deteriorating condition. A few days later, the family issued a statement regarding Jorge Messi’s “health situation”, informing the public that he was undergoing medical treatment.

Jorge Messi closely accompanied his son throughout his career, beginning with his early years at Barcelona. He acted as a crucial pillar of support and, for several years, served as his representative. “I always ‌needed my dad’s approval, ever since I was a kid. After every match, I’d ask him ​what he thought of how I played,” said Lionel Messi.

Sports.title: Liverpool agree to sign Barcelona’s Ronald Araújo on loan as Jacquet cover
Sports.content:
Liverpool have agreed to sign Ronald Araújo on a season-long loan from Barcelona after Andoni Iraola was faced with lack of defensive options for the start of the new season.

Concerns over Jérémy Jacquet – the France Under -21 defender who arrived last season for more than £50m – and injuries to Joe Gomez and Giovanni Leoni have left Liverpool short of options at the back after the departure of Ibrahima Konaté on a free transfer to Real Madrid.

Araújo, who was part of the Barça side that won La Liga last season, will add much-needed cover in the short-term. The Uruguay defender is expected to complete his medical on Sunday.

The deal for the 27-year-old is believed to contain an option to buy at the end of the season. Araújo has made more than 200 appearances for Barcelona, but only made 11 league starts last season.

Liverpool have shown an interest in Aston Villa’s Ezri Konsa, but were put off by the £60m valuation of the England defender. Arsenal have had an initial approach for Konsa rejected.

Jacquet, who signed from Rennes in February, has not made a competitive appearance after picking up a serious shoulder injury last season and did not feature during Liverpool’s three-match tour of the United States. Iraola said last week that he has been feeling “some discomfort, so we don’t want to rush him”.

The Liverpool manager added: “He comes from a lot of months without playing. And obviously I would like to try with him with Virgil [van Dijk] when he recovers, because with the injury of Joe we’ve been without senior centre-backs. But we have to be careful with Jeremy.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Liverpool have held talks with Paris Saint-Germain over a move for Bradley Barcola, although the European champions value him at around £145m. PSG are expected to make a move for Spain’s World Cup final hero Ferran Torres, who has one year left on his contract at the Camp Nou.

Sports.title: Why Super Furry Animals joined music’s dash to cross over football’s vinyl frontier | Emma John
Sports.content:
As someone born on the cusp of the gen X-millennial divide, I am the perfect target for today’s 90s nostalgia. I played my modest, teenage part in the Battle of Britpop (verbal skirmisher, Blur division); I fervently sang – and, God help me, believed – that Things Can Only Get Better. Super Furry Animals were a band I knew only distantly, via the transgressive thrill of that song they had with all the swearing in. And yet the news they’ll be shirt sponsor for a Welsh football club this season has managed to whisk me straight back to a time when things seemed simpler, kinder and more hopeful.

Nearly three decades have passed since Super Furry Animals last had their logo on a football kit. Back in 1999, their frontman Gruff Rhys and bassist Guto Pryce, both Cardiff City fans, persuaded their Bangor-born bandmates to lay down their north Wales allegiances for the duration of the Bluebirds’ Welsh Cup run – which was, incidentally, all they could afford. The cup shirts cost them £2,000 and were, according to Rhys, knock-offs made for ice hockey. This year’s beneficiaries are a more modest outfit: Cwmbran Celtic, just relegated from Wales’s second tier. Cwmbran is the town where the band send their stage props for repair, and given the props in question are giant inflatable bears, you wonder whether they could get one installed in goal.

Super Furry Animals aren’t the only 90s band involved: Scottish post-rockers Mogwai have sponsored the men’s away strip, with 10% of the profits from all shirt sales going to a grassroots music charity.

There has traditionally been an element of patronage when famous musicians do football, from Elton John’s time as chair of Watford, to Robbie Williams’s 2024 elevation to Port Vale club president. The pattern is a repeating one: local lads (they’re usually lads) make good, and want to give back to the team they’ve followed since they were little. Wet Wet Wet were the first to go down the shirt-sponsorship route with Clydebank in 1993. The team’s shirts turned out to be a more timeless design than the loud, oversized suits that Marti Pellow’s crew wore the day they unveiled them.

Slapping your logo on your home side’s shirt was a charitable endeavour, rather than an investment. Nothing underscored this point better than Fatboy Slim’s relationship with Brighton & Hove Albion. The DJ’s record label first sponsored their shirts in the late 90s, back when the team’s financial straits had left them flirting with extinction, and Tony Bloom’s billions were still waiting to be won. It was particularly appropriate back then that Micky Adams’s men should run out on to the field with their chests declaring them SKINT.

View image in fullscreen Bobby Zamora in Brighton’s home kit sponsored by Fatboy Slim. Photograph: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images

Musical match-ups have tended, therefore, towards the endearing, not the cool. Jake Bugg sponsored Notts County not to market his own music, but to evangelise the Midlands team on his global tours. And it’s even cuter when bands have sponsored kids’ teams. The late Lemmy of Motörhead was tickled by the thought of a Lincolnshire under-10s team sporting his Snaggletooth skull mascot on their fronts; unfortunately the resultant all-black kit too closely resembled referees’ uniforms and the children were banned from wearing it in league matches. Still, the idea had an enduring appeal: the Prodigy, Biffy Clyro, Sleaford Mods and Franz Ferdinand have all paid for youth kits.

In the last couple of years, though, the relationship between bands and football teams has turned serious. The move to monetise the “adjacent audiences” of pop and sporting fandom means shirt sponsorship is no longer a way of artists showing their support, but a marketing and merchandising opportunity in its own right.

Spotify’s deal with Barcelona got the ball rolling, with Coldplay, Karol G, Rosalía and Travis Scott each briefly appearing on the shirtfront, and limited-edition replicas costing more than £340 a pop. The footie-kit-as-streetwear trend means bands aren’t “sponsors” any more, they’re “collaborators”. Hence Manchester United’s pre-match shirts don’t bear the name of the Stone Roses, just their album artwork. And while that may have baffled a few younger fans – the club’s website ran a post explaining who the Madchester group were for the gen Z-ers – it still reflects a genuine connection. Ian Brown is a lifelong Red, and the team has walked out to This Is the One since Gary Neville first requested it two decades ago.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Coldplay show off their Barcelona shirts. Photograph: Fc Barcelona Handout/EPA

Whereas a year ago, if you’d been asked at a pub quiz what Paris Saint-Germain had in common with a K-pop band, or what Pink Floyd had to do with a Serie A team, you’d have been within your rights to say “nothing”. The answer, now, is clothing ranges – PSG teamed up with the girl group Blackpink to optimise fan engagement in Asia, while Inter marked the 50th anniversary of the album release of Wish You Were Here.

All this can be confusing for the simple-minded sports lover like me. What is a culture-forward lifestyle capsule, anyway? It sounds like something Musk and Bezos want to blast to Mars in. Creating a sporting look now involves an advanced understanding of fashion arithmetic: at last year’s Euros it was Admiral x Spice Girls, now it’s the Rolling Stones x England Cricket x Castore. These are powerful equations, as when a 2025 Bohemian FC x Fontaines DC shirt (raised to the power of Greta Thunberg when she wore it on her flotilla to Gaza) = £££££ for charity. Maybe Ed Sheeran’s Mathematics tour top for Ipswich was an omen. Or perhaps this is a fad, and the music industry will soon move on to something new. GQ, which has declared “blokecore” over, says we’ll be wearing classic rugby tops by autumn/winter. Sounds delightfully 90s to me.

Sports.title: Will Lankshear starts off in style to see Middlesbrough past Wrexham
Sports.content:
Will Lankshear’s debut strike ensured Middlesbrough made a winning start to the season as they beat Wrexham 1-0 in the Carabao Cup first round. Lankshear, a £10m summer signing from Tottenham, scored the only goal of the game in the 61st minute as he hooked home an excellent first-time volley.

Middlesbrough almost claimed a seventh-minute opener but when Adilson Malanda prodded Sebastian Berhalter’s cross goalwards from close range, Danny Ward kept the ball out with a superb point-blank save.

Danny Imray wasted a decent chance for Wrexham when he failed to make a proper connection from Callum Doyle’s cross and the visitors went close again six minutes before the break when Sam Smith fired a low shot into the legs of Sol Brynn after he was rolled into space by Nathan Broadhead.

Lankshear came close with an effort that was curled just over the bar at the start of the second half, but the 21-year-old did not have to wait too much longer for his first goal in a Boro shirt. Leo Castledine headed Jeremy Sarmiento’s cross into Lankshear’s path, and the striker swivelled neatly before hooking a superb first-time volley into the far corner.

Boro almost doubled their lead with three minutes remaining but Morgan Whittaker’s low strike rebounded off the post.

After the match the Middlesbrough manager, Kim Hellberg, expressed his delight with the instant impact Will Lankshear has made since joining the club. “He was very impressive and the most impressive thing has been seeing how well he has worked on the training ground,” Hellberg said. “How hard he works on the training ground and how much he wants to learn.

“It’s a joy to watch and when you add the person he is to the quality he has as a footballer on the pitch, you have a very good striker. I’m happy to have him here.”

Wrexham’s manager, Phil Parkinson, felt his side had given a decent account of themselves just four days after returning from a pre-season tour of the US. Parkinson said: “I thought we had enough half-chances, particularly in the first half, to have progressed in the competition. The game really separated from one quality finish from their lad. We had some good build-up play, but just didn’t quite have that clinical edge.

“It was a big ask in terms of coming back from America on Monday and you’ve got to give the lads credit for going close. There were a lot of positives in the performance.”

Sports.title: Sandro Tonali sparks mid-game scuffle during ‘heated’ Tottenham pre-season clash
Sports.content:
A frustrated Sandro Tonali sparked an angry scuffle during what was a not-so-friendly friendly between Tottenham and Getafe.

Tonali, who joined Spurs from Newcastle for £100m earlier this summer, was angered by a challenge from Mario Martin.

4 Tonali was not happy with a kick he received from Getafe's Martin

After the Italian midfielder pushed Martin over when winning back possession, the latter reacted with a late dig.

As the Getafe star looked to regain the ball, he left a leg in as Tonali passed the ball forward, catching his opponent.

And that left Tonali furious as he then pushed Martin back and lost focus on the game, having all eyes on his rival.

He chased him and grabbed Martin's shoulder to turn him around, pushing him again multiple times, with one of them to the neck.

That caused a melee in the centre of the pitch, as players from both teams swamped around the two players.

Ben Davies rushed over to defend Tonali, with Archie Gray, Jan Paul van Hecke and Andy Robertson all jumping in too.

Robertson also had a quick pushing match with a Getafe player before things eventually calmed down in the 'friendly'.

Tonali and Martin avoided a booking for the incident.

'If you get kicked, you're going to react'

Post-match, Tonali was defended for his reaction that sparked the scrap, as Getafe took things too far in pre-season.

Van Hecke admitted that things got a bit too aggressive in the friendly that was being played behind closed doors.

4 Tonali won the ball back but then got caught by a late challenge from his opponent

4 The Italian then ran after Martin and pushed him multiple times

“Sometimes it’s good [to have a physical game]," he admitted.

“I thought today was a bit too much. A bit from their side, sometimes it’s not necessary, especially in a friendly.

“I think in a normal game maybe they have two or three red cards.

"But that’s also maybe the way they play. We knew beforehand that they can do it.

“But then it’s a friendly, so sometimes you think maybe a bit less, but on the other side we also need to be at our top then because if you don’t put in your foot then they are going to win it.

“If that’s what the game asks, you also need to put your foot in and battle with them, otherwise they win the battles.

4 Spurs and Getafe players swarmed around Tonali and Martin as things got heated

"That’s what you don’t want, that’s the first thing in football you need to win.

“You saw sometimes it got a bit heated, but that’s because of the reaction, if you get kicked, then you’re going to react.”

Tottenham drew with Getafe in the feisty affair on Saturday as Conor Gallagher netted following Alberto Risco's opener.

They now only have one more pre-season game to play before the Premier League campaign kicks off on August 22.

Spurs take on Hoffenheim at 3pm on Saturday, August 15 next.

Sports.title: Joao Palhinha in talks over return to the Premier League after Tottenham exit
Sports.content:
Joao Palhinha in talks over return to the Premier League after Tottenham exit

Aston Villa are in talks over a deal for Joao Palhinha, their director of football has confirmed.

The midfielder is one of three players that Bayern Munich are willing to sell this summer.

2 Palhinha could be set for another season in the Premier League at a new club Credit: Getty

Palhinha joined Bayern from Fulham in 2024 and he spent last season on loan at Tottenham Hotspur.

His move to north London included a £26million option to buy, but it expired and he has returned to Germany.

With the Portuguese international not in Bayern's plans, he looks set to leave just two seasons after he signed.

A return to the Premier League appears to be on the cards as Damian Vidagany told BILD that Villa are working on a move.

"We need a midfielder because Amadou Onana is out for the entire season - Joao Palhinha is a very good player who would fit our plans," Vidagany said.

"We are in talks, but there is currently no agreement. I believe Aston Villa would be a great club for him."

That was as much as Vidagany was willing to give away, as he refused to comment on further details due to the 'great respect' all at Villa have for Bayern.

Palhinha has made 101 appearances in the Premier League across his stints at Fulham and Spurs.

A move to Villa would present him with an opportunity to play in the Champions League during the new season.

Newcastle United, who have lost Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal, have also been linked with Palhinha.

Midfield moves

2 Palhinha impressed at Spurs, but they chose not to pursue a permanent deal Credit: Getty

Villa have already completed two signings in central midfield so far this summer.

Johan Manzambi was brought in from SC Freiburg in a £52million deal that made him their club-record signing.

Villa have also signed Joao Gomes from West Midlands rivals Wolves for £35m.

Ross Barkley, John McGinn, Boubacar Kamara and Lamare Bogarde are listed as central midfielders on Villa's website.

However, Youri Tielemans has departed for Manchester United, whilst Enzo Barrenechea is back at Benfica after a loan spell.

Villa begin their season on Wednesday night when they take on Paris Saint-Germain in the Super Cup, live on talkSPORT.

Their first Premier League fixture comes four days later on August 23 with a trip to Brighton.

Sports.title: New EFL signing immediately forced to clarify ‘stepping stone’ comment amid backlash
Sports.content:
Middlesbrough signing Radek Vitek has been forced to explain a comment made during his first interview after his transfer.

Vitek signed for Boro from Manchester United on Saturday, but he said that the move was a 'new stepping stone' for him.



2 New Middlesbrough goalkeeper Vitek received backlash for his first interview Credit: Getty

His wording led to some backlash from fans online, as they questioned his mentality regarding the switch.

Typically, the phrase 'a stepping stone' relates to a player using a smaller club solely as a route to join a bigger team in the future, rather than planning to stay for a long time.

After Middlesbrough posted a video of Vitek's first interview as their new signing, supporters flooded the replies.



One Boro supporter replied on X: "Don’t love how he has just called us a stepping stone."

Another questioned: "Did he just say stepping stone..."

"Lad really said ‘new stepping stone’ Jesus. Welcome to the club, I guess," a third Boro fan posted.



But some fans jumped to Vitek's defence and pointed out a language barrier that could have impacted the Czech star.

"I think he means 'next step in my career' having listened to it a few times," another Middlesbrough supporter said. "Easy to mix up sayings when it's someone's second language."



'Not meant in any negative way'

And just a few hours after Vitek's first interview was posted and he faced some backlash, he spoke out on the matter.

"I wanted to clarify what I meant by 'stepping stone'," the goalkeeper wrote, explaining his words on his X account.

What did Radek Vitek say in his interview? In the video posted by Middlesbrough on Saturday, Vitek could be heard saying: "A new challenge for me. "A new stepping stone in my career, a permanent move. "So I'm really excited. I hope everyone is as excited as me for the season ahead and I hope we can go for the goal we all want."

"I just want to assure everyone that I have not meant that in any negative way.

"The point of this comment was that this is a very important step in my career going forward.



"I can’t wait to get started."

Off to a controversial start

Vitek won't have wanted any controversy to begin his time as a Middlesbrough player, but he has now cleared things up.

The 22-year-old has joined the club from Man United after spending the last six years with the Red Devils.

He spent last season on loan at Bristol City in the Championship, following other loans in the EFL and Austria.

2 Vitek spent pre-season with Man United after a loan at Bristol City last term Credit: Getty



Vitek was named Bristol City's Player of the Year after an impressive campaign - and now he's back in the second tier.

Away from his 'stepping stone' comments in his first interview as a Boro player, he also said: “It feels great to be here.

“This is a new challenge for me and I’m really excited to be a Boro player.

“The project here is very impressive, because you can clearly see the ambition and where the club wants to go.



“I’m delighted to now be part of that.”

Sports.title: South Korean FA apologises after headquarters raided over sexual services for refs allegations
Sports.content:
South Korean FA apologises after headquarters raided over sexual services for refs allegations

South Korea’s FA has issued an apology following reports that it had provided 'sexual services' to foreign referees.

The country’s broadcaster JTBC reported earlier this week that the Korea Football Association (KFA) had offered the services to officials that were in the country for international matches.

3 The South Korean FA is under the microscope yet again Credit: AFP

The allegations date back more than a decade ago with referees offered services on multiple occasions in 2011 and 2012.

It is alleged that further indiscretions occurred prior to qualifying matches for the 2014 World Cup and the 2012 London Olympics.

In a statement, the KFA profusely apologised for the details of the report.

KFA's statement on shock allegations

It read: “We deeply apologise for causing concern over various issues involving the association, which emerged from a parliamentary hearing and an unprecedented search and seizure, and from reports about events from more than a decade ago, that even many within the organisation were unaware of.'”

The news report published on Thursday revealed how a sports ministry investigation back in 2016 found the KFA had provided inappropriate entertainment to foreign referees.

It claimed that it happened on seven separate occasions between March 2011 and March 2012.

The services included trips to massage parlours with the fees inclusive of the costs of sexual services.

“The association makes clear that inappropriate conduct of this kind, or the use of corporate cards for such purposes, is absolutely not currently taking place,” the KFA added in its statement.

The allegations come after a period of instability on and off the pitch in South Korean football.

A review into an issue involving the appointment of former national team coach Hong Myung-bo is ongoing.

3 Hong Myung-bo's appointment as South Korea head coach is under investigation

Seoul police raided the KFA’s offices on Thursday as part of their inquiries into Hong’s selection.

The investigation began shortly after Hong’s appointment but to a halt this summer after nearly two years without answers.

However, public anger surrounding South Korea’s disappointing World Cup group-stage exit brought about renewed attention.

Ex-KFA technical director Lee Lim-saeng is accused of offering Hong the job at a bakery near the coach’s home.

South Korea’s sports ministry said in 2024 that Lee’s meeting with Hong was not a formal interview and that the KFA had breached its own hiring rules.

However, the ministry found no evidence of foul play.

3 South Korea endured a hugely disappointing World Cup campaign this summer Credit: AFP

“When I received the offer, I thought they had all taken the proper steps,” Hong said at the parliamentary hearing.

“People may think things were not so transparent, but I never once asked for any special treatment.”

Sports.title: Mason Mount sparks new injury fears by limping out of Man United pre-season game
Sports.content:
Mason Mount sparks new injury fears by limping out of Man United pre-season game

Mason Mount was forced off with an injury scare during Manchester United's pre-season clash with Paris Saint-Germain.

The 27-year-old has been blighted by fitness issues since his move to Old Trafford in 2023, but was named in Michael Carrick's starting XI as they took on the European champions in Gothenburg.



4 Mount was in conversation with Man United's medical team after lasting less than 20 minutes against PSG Credit: X: @samuelluckhurst

4 The Englishman headed straight down the tunnel after his afternoon was cut short Credit: X: @samuelluckhurst

But there was no let-up for Mount in the pre-season fixture, as he pulled up early on and was unable to continue.

The 27-year-old then had to be replaced by Tyler Fletcher in yet more concerning scenes.



After exiting the field, Mount could be seen deep in conversation with members of United’s medical staff.

He then made his way down the tunnel, in a familiar sight for Red Devils supporters.



Man United were 1-0 down to a youthful PSG side when Mount was forced off, with Liverpool target Ibrahim Mbaye putting the Champions League winners in front within two minutes.

But Carrick's side responded soon after, as Bryan Mbeumo equalised shortly after the half-hour mark.



In the wars

Injuries have plagued Mount's Man United career, preventing him from reaching the standards he set at previous club Chelsea.

The Cobham academy graduate joined the Red Devils in a £60million deal in 2023.

However, since then he has spent a staggering 394 days on the sidelines, causing him to miss both Euro 2024 and this summer's World Cup with England.

Mount has made just 72 appearances for United, but made his most appearances in a Premier League campaign for the club last term.



4 Mount was in Sweden for Man Utd’s latest pre-season clash Credit: Getty

The England midfielder featured 23 times in the league, scoring three goals, although he was mainly used by former boss Ruben Amorim in the first half of the season.

This has led to rumours he could join Amorim at new club AC Milan, although Mount has been part of United's pre-season group so far.

Make or break?

Mount's latest setback against PSG come after talkSPORT's Shebahn Aherne suggested that the upcoming season was make-or-break for him in his career.



“He needs to have a strong season,” Aherne said of Mount.

“Luke Shaw played every game last season and really got his season back on track, sorted out the injury issues and he was brilliant.

“But Mason Mount, you always hear that he’s the perfect pupil. He’s a very smart and intelligent player and when he’s on his game. He’s brilliant.

4 Mount has scored just seven goals in his injury-hit Man United career Credit: Getty

“You just hope that this season he will come good.”

talkSPORT's Tony Cascarino was also hopeful the 27-year-old could find his level again and highlighted one of his key attributes.



He said: “They paid £55m for him. He was injured at Chelsea before he got to Old Trafford and he was a terrific player for Chelsea.

“He can play in that floating position like [Florian] Wirtz and he can get a goal.

“Manchester United need a really fit Mason Mount, if not to start, then to challenge for other player’s spots in the team.

“He’s a good finisher, get him in goalscoring positions and he will finish. It would be like a new signing.”

Sports.title: Are hydration breaks now part of English football? Carabao Cup stoppages roundly booed
Sports.content:
If there was one thing that English football fans did not want to see introduced to the game this season, it was hydration breaks.

So, why did some fixtures in the Carabao Cup first round on Saturday see a pause in play called by the referee for a drink?

2 Hydration breaks caused plenty of fan backlash at the World Cup Credit: Getty

It appeared to take some supporters by shock as the largely condemned World Cup rule appeared to be used in England.

Halfway through each half in multiple ties across the country, including at West Ham's London Stadium and Leicester City's King Power, a break was called for the teams to take on some fluid.

And as those in the stands realised what was happening, a chorus of boos and angry chants filled stadiums - a reaction that is not surprising.

Hydration breaks were one of the main talking points of the summer, as every World Cup game was split into four quarters.

Each half of each game at the tournament saw a pause in play that allowed players to have a drink, but the break ended up becoming a chance for a team talk with the manager and coaches too.

FIFA were slammed for including the breaks, which were added to the rules to help out players when playing in scorching heat.

There were also many questions raised over whether that was the sole reason, or whether they were introduced for extra commercial time on TV coverage in the United States.

But with the World Cup over and temperatures not reaching the heights of those in the US during the 3pm kick-offs in the Carabao Cup, why were the hydration breaks used on Saturday?

Are hydration breaks now in English football?

Fortunately for fans in England, despite some expecting the breaks to eventually become the norm, it is not a new rule.

The EFL has told talkSPORT that it is not a new competition policy in the Carabao Cup to have the hydration pauses.

2 The EFL have not made hydration breaks a new competition policy Credit: Getty

There were breaks in the play during the first round clashes purely down to the decision of the officials in charge.

The referees decide on an individual basis depending on the weather, which is the standard protocol in the EFL - with temperatures on Saturday reaching highs of 29 degrees Celsius.

So, thankfully, it is not expected that the official hydration break ruling will be introduced in English football anytime soon.
