Sports.title: David Sullivan publicly defies London Stadium recomendation in West Ham opener
Sports.content:
David Sullivan has defied advice to stay away from the London Stadium by attending West Ham's Carabao Cup tie against Portsmouth.

The 77-year-old stepped down from his position as club chairman in June ahead of the release of a joint investigation by The Times and BBC Panorama accusing him of sexually-exploitative behaviour.



3 David Sullivan defied advice to keep away from the London Stadium in West Ham's first competitive game of the season Credit: Getty

Sullivan categorically denied the claims made against him in the investigation, which saw seven women come forward.

Despite stepping down from his role as chairman, the former adult industry kingpin remains West Ham's largest shareholder.

However, the London Stadium confirmed earlier this week that it had 'recommended' that Sullivan stay away from home fixtures this season.



This followed an internal investigation which deemed there was not an ongoing safeguarding risk associated with him attending matches.

The club asked for advance notice of any planned visits by Sullivan - who retains a 38.8 per cent stake in the Irons - in order to implement additional safety and operational measures.



Staying put

West Ham's Carabao Cup clash with Portsmouth on Saturday saw them kick off their first competitive game of the season.

And Sullivan appeared to ignore advice from the London Stadium, as he was spotted in the stands for the Hammers' 2026/27 opener in east London.



However, there did not appear to be any problems inside the stadium before and shortly after kick-off.

This marks the first competitive fixture the Hammers have played since the allegations against him were first reported.

It also saw the club begin their campaign following relegation from the Premier League to the Championship last season.

3 Sullivan appeared to go unnoticed by fans as he took his seat at the London Stadium Credit: Getty



As well as being advised to stay away from the London Stadium, the investigation into Sullivan also revealed he had been banned by the FA from having contact with West Ham’s women's and youth teams since 2023.

His suspension from doing so came after allegations and a safeguarding investigation, and meant he was unable to attend matches involving either side.

Changing landscape

Sullivan bought a 50 per cent stake in West Ham alongside David Gold 16 years ago and currently holds a 38.8 per cent share.

While he currently remains the club's largest single shareholder, a change in boardroom at the London Stadium looks increasingly likely.



There is an ongoing tussle for shares in the Hammers between a consortium led by Amanda Staveley and current second-largest shareholder Daniel Kretinsky.

The Czech billionaire is attempting to stop Staveley from purchasing the Gold family's 25.1 per cent stake in a £150million deal.

3 Jarrod Bowen marked the news that he will remain at West Ham this season with a goal against Portsmouth Credit: Getty

While West Ham continue to navigate a summer of upheaval on and off the pitch, they focused on the task in hand against Portsmouth.



After falling behind to Adrian Segecic's deflected effort in the first half, the east Londoners fought back to turn the game on its head.

After Taty Castellanos' equaliser, captain Jarrod Bowen then fired the Hammers in front on the stroke of half-time.

This was Bowen's first goal since penning a new deal to stay at the club for the upcoming season, and West Ham's lead was soon doubled as Castellanos grabbed another on 50 minutes.

West Ham will then begin their Championship campaign away to Burnley on Sunday, August 16.

Sports.title: Arsenal sign Bruno Guimaraes: Gunners complete £75m deal for Brazilian midfielder as ANOTHER Newcastle star leaves St James' Park
Sports.content:
Arsenal have completed the £75million signing of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle.

The Brazilian becomes their fourth arrival of the transfer window after they made Piero Hincapie's loan permanent and signed Christos Tzolis and Illan Meslier.

Guimaraes has signed a four-year deal with the option of a further 12 months.

Guimaraes said: 'I feel good, I feel amazing. I'm glad for the opportunity. Since the first time I spoke to (Andrea) Berta and Mikel (Arteta), I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a new challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

'Well I think, after playing two World Cups, I think I'm at the point of my life, I think I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I'm in the right place to do it. I'm so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season, so the squad is going to be very, very important and I'm hopeful we can achieve our dreams.

'Big Gabi (Gabriel) was very excited. Every time he sent me the message, "We’ll wait for you, when will you come?" I'm so excited to join them, not only the Brazilians, we have an amazing squad here.

'(Declan) Rice sent me a message: "Come here and please no more fights, now we're friends". I was happy he messaged me, but the midfield we have here, in my point of view, is one of the best in Europe. Everyone is an amazing player, I'm so excited to start chatting and play, and know the players very, very well, but we have an amazing midfield.'

Arsenal have completed the £75million signing of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United

Mikel Arteta hugs his new arrival after the Premier League champions bolster their midfield

Sporting director Andrea Berta said: 'We are delighted to welcome Bruno Guimaraes to our club.

'Bruno is a player with a great mentality and great quality, who will bring strong leadership to our squad.

'With Bruno joining us, we are further strengthening the heart of our team. As we have all seen, Bruno can play as a defensive midfielder and as a box-to-box player. He combines quality with quantity, and has provided goals and assists for his team every year.

'Bruno will allow Mikel to further develop our playing style and will also increase our internal competitiveness, which is essential for maintaining the standards required when we are aiming to win major trophies.'

His arrival at the Emirates takes their summer spend to around £145m as they look to build on last season's Premier League title and Champions League final.

But the move is another complication for Newcastle, who had already sold Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali this window before Eddie Howe stepped down as manager.

Guimaraes has been an important player for the Magpies ever since joining for £40m in 2022.

But the 28-year-old told them in July that he wants to join Arsenal.

Daily Mail Sport revealed on June 25 that the Magpies were braced for an offer from the Gunners after leading agents were instructed to explore the Brazilian's options.

The World Cup star had two years remaining on his contract at St James' Park, plus the option of an extra year, hence Newcastle were able to command a strong fee.

Mikel Arteta has been keen to strengthen his central midfield options despite already having Declan Rice, Martin Zubimendi, Mikel Merino, Eberechi Eze and Fabio Vieira.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso deploys a back three for the first time as Blues boss and why adding a set-piece coach has proved a masterstroke: Chelsea 3-0 AC Milan
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso can take plenty of encouragement from deploying a back three for the first time at Chelsea - conclusively beating AC Milan 3-0.

The display was a far cry from Chelsea’s leaky defensive performances in pre-season so far, as they kept their first clean sheet since Alonso took charge.

Chelsea were dominant throughout, helped by having consistent personnel on the pitch - making only two changes before 80 minutes, whereas AC Milan made wholesale substitutions at half-time.

But it was the defensive structure Alonso utilised so effectively at Bayer Leverkusen that enabled a comfortable performance.

Summer signing Marco Palestra was deployed at left wing-back, with Pedro Neto on the opposite side. In possession, though, they may as well have been wingers.

When Chelsea attacked, Neto ran beyond Palmer - who started on the right of Danny Welbeck - offering a penetrating threat to stretch play. Palestra acted the same way on the opposite side as his perpetual movement shone.

Not only did the set-up allow Chelsea to threaten all over the pitch with significant offensive threats occupying both wide and narrow areas, but the front three demonstrated their fluidity.

Joao Pedro, Cole Palmer and Welbeck often rotated. At times, there were two up top with one behind. The main formation, though, was a 3-4-2-1.

Welbeck led the line with Palmer and Pedro either side of him. But that was not a strict rule, as the attackers were given the freedom to roam.

A link-up between Pedro and Neto earned Chelsea their second less than a minute after half-time. Neto found Pedro’s run with a dinked cross into the box from the right.

Neto had very few defensive responsibilities as the right wing-back, allowing him to focus on being a nuisance.

That right side could prove deadly during the season, with full-backs forced to deal with the menacing Palmer inside while also keeping tabs on the threat Neto poses out wide.

Pedro, meanwhile, flourished in the system. Encouraged to float around, the technical Brazilian demonstrated his versatility as a number 10 who can also play out wide and up front.

Joao Pedro has been on fire during pre-season, scoring five times, and Xabi Alonso’s back three seemed to bring out the best in him

Four shots, two goals, a big chance missed and the most touches in the AC Milan box - Pedro, thanks to the set-up, was extremely active and took his pre-season tally to five goals.

Josh Acheampong was also a beneficiary of the system, exuding confidence both on and off the ball. The centre-back recovered brilliantly to make a last-ditch challenge on Rafael Leao in the first half, strong in the tackle - putting his mistake behind him.

With the likes of Reece James, Maxence Lacroix, Enzo Fernandez, Malo Gusto and Morgan Rogers to report for the remainder of pre-season next week, Alonso has every right to be excited about this Chelsea side.

At 70 per cent strength, Chelsea looked cohesive and controlled, with four games now under their belt and an encouraging understanding of what is required in a back three.

As even more quality is added to the group next week, the back three looks an appealing option to open their Premier League campaign against Fulham.

MacPhee's immediate impact

New set-piece coach Austin MacPhee has already started to earn his money.

Chelsea paid a release clause just shy of £1million to get him out of his contract at Aston Villa and bring him to Stamford Bridge. Minuscule in the context of player spend, but significant for a member of the backroom staff.

Yet he could prove to be Chelsea’s most important signing of the summer.

Chelsea had an appalling record from set-pieces last season, with a negative goal difference from them - conceding 17 and scoring 14. It is no wonder Alonso was so keen to add one of the world's best dead-ball coaches to his coaching staff.

Having joined Chelsea just this week - flying to Asia to unite with his new side on their pre-season tour - MacPhee made a blazing impact, with Chelsea scoring twice from corners against AC Milan.

Chelsea scored twice from set-pieces against AC Milan, with Moises Caicedo finding the back of the net from outside of the area

The first was pretty basic. Moises Caicedo’s pinpoint cross found Pedro’s intelligent movement. Pedro, unmarked, glanced his header into the far corner. It was a goal you will see many times this season.

The second, however, was certainly a move crafted on the training ground as MacPhee's expertise emerged.

Romeo Lavia floated a cross to the edge of the area where Caicedo was waiting. The midfielder coolly came onto the ball and ingeniously guided it into the bottom corner with the outside of his boot. He made a tough finish appear straightforward - it was anything but.

A move executed with individual brilliance, but one crafted by Chelsea’s new master in the dugout. If this is just a glimpse of MacPhee’s capabilities, Chelsea certainly have plenty to look forward to.

Lavia provides timely reminder of his quality

Lavia completed his first full 90 minutes for Chelsea since joining from Southampton for £53m in 2023, taking another step towards building up his fitness.

The 22-year-old midfielder has endured injury after injury since arriving in West London, but made significant progress on Saturday, having played 25 minutes against Juventus just three days earlier.

There have never been any questions about his ability. Lavia has the talent to become one of the Premier League’s best midfielders - the biggest question is whether his body will allow him to fulfil that potential.

Romeo Lavia played 90 minutes for the first time in a Chelsea shirt

That is his challenge: staying fit. He has two more opportunities to build up substantial minutes before Chelsea’s season opener, and a steady pre-season would give him the ideal platform to build on in the campaign ahead.

Lavia was lively alongside Caicedo in midfield, providing an assist from a corner, rarely giving the ball away and making eight recoveries.

Completing a game will boost his confidence and provide a platform for greater stability.

Sports.title: Unlucky Man United star's injury concern will force Michael Carrick into a transfer rethink, hungry Amad Diallo is set to hit the ground running  - and why Bryan Mbeumo's new role bodes well for the season
Sports.content:
Manchester United have plenty of reasons to smile after holding European champions Paris Saint-Germain to a 1-1 draw in Gothenburg.

Similarly to the win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm, United made the worst possible start when PSG went ahead through Ibrahim Mbaye 101 seconds following a fast-break that totally caught Michael Carrick's side on their heels.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia stung the palms of Tom Heaton, who was later forced off with a hamstring problem, moments later but was denied, before United put their foot on the accelerator to prove themselves as the better side.

That was rewarded when Bryan Mbeumo, teed up by Amad Diallo, again impressing in what is a crucial campaign for the Ivorian, finished low and hard into the corner to equalise, notching his third goal in two games.

But the injury to Mason Mount, however precautionary, left pause for thought on a day where the midfield rebuild came back into sharp focus, the lack of left back depth came to the fore, and the Mbeumo striker experiment may well be here to stay. Daily Mail Sport takes a look at the key talking points.

Manchester United impressed in a 1-1 draw against Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg

A MOUNT-ING PROBLEM

Heading into this summer, after closing out the season well down at Brighton, the question around Mount was whether he could be anything more than Bruno Fernandes' understudy.

Mount played deeper at Brighton and yet all indications coming out of Old Trafford were that yes, three midfield signings would be on the agenda. What that meant for Mount, who pitched up from Chelsea in a £60million move back in 2023, remained to be seen.

Then pre-season started. Mount started well, playing deeper alongside Andrey Santos, himself joining from Chelsea, arriving for £50m this summer. The duo impressed. Internally the stance around a third midfielder looked to have softened of late, such was Mount's form.

Mount is a very popular member of United's squad; a leader for many and a player that so many in the building are willing on to do great things.

After the 5-0 win over Rosenborg in Trondheim earlier this summer, Mount was full of glee when he spoke about how well he feels.

'I was ready and raring to get back and get training again and get back into the flow of it,' he said.

'As players that's what you want. I feel strong and ready to go. I know we've got a few weeks more games left and a few more weeks to really work at stuff but I feel good.'

But here was the reminder of how fallible it can all be.

Reliability matters. Inside 20 minutes here, clutching his foot, Mount had to go off, withdrawn and was replaced by academy product Tyler Fletcher.

Mount jogged off unassisted, sought advice from three members of United's medical team before heading down the tunnel. It looked precautionary ahead of two final pre-season games against Leeds United in Dublin and AC Milan in Wroclaw.

But it is also a warning that United cannot allow the next three weeks and a couple of days to pass between now and the transfer deadline without another midfielder signing walking through the door. That prospect has to now be inexplicable.

United's recruitment in that area of the pitch has been good, too, this summer. Santos has been the star of pre-season and Youri Tielemans, who got 25 minutes on debut off the bench, could prove the steal of the summer at £35m.

Taking a big swing, the biggest of the lot most likely, should be a pressure Ineos and the bosses at United must relish, not be afraid of.

DORGU IS NO DEFENDER

Speaking of recruitment, let's talk left backs. Patrick Dorgu isn't one, if that wasn't abundantly clear already.

Ironically, the Dane is consistently listed as a defender on any United squad list but Carrick has never played him there. Not once. Much like Darren Fletcher, who took interim charge between Carrick succeeding Ruben Amorim, Dorgu is seen as a winger.

In Gothenburg he again started on the left wing, occasionally drifting out to the right in a bid to confuse PSG's makeshift backline – in what was a heavily rotated squad from the one we saw lift the Champions League title against Arsenal.

Dorgu is raw and that is both a blessing and a curse. His ceiling feels sky high but getting to the consistency required is going to take patience.

What won't deliver that is shifting him to left back and evidently United's coaching team agree, which leaves Luke Shaw and… exactly.

So, again, United simply have to deliver Carrick a left back between now and 11pm on September 1.

Luke Shaw appears to be United's only orthodox and viable left back option for this season

Shaw was steady here, nothing extremely good nor extremely bad. Defensively sound is the best summation.

And yes, he started every Premier League game last season and deserves credit for that. But depth at left back matters and it's an issue United haven't been able to fix.

Top target is Lewis Hall, who Newcastle United have made plain they have zero appetite to sell this summer after two approaches from Old Trafford's hierarchy.

There's Harry Amass, an impressive youngster that has come through United's academy in recent years, and, truthfully he should be an option. But he has been told his best chance of minutes will come elsewhere.

United played just 40 games in all competitions last season, their fewest in a single season since 1914-15, while others such as Chelsea (59 matches) and Tottenham Hotspur (52 matches) played considerably more.

Back into European and cup runs expected – no repeats of the debacle at Grimsby Town ideally – depth is going to be as vital as having the requisite quality. One injury to Shaw post transfer deadline and United are firmly on the back foot. The warning is staring them in the face.

A-MAD WORLD

Back to how United out-performed this makeshift PSG side – playing only their second pre-season game compared to United's fourth – and hats off to Amad.

Significant questions were asked of the Ivorian to the point where sources at United were eager to privately stress that he was never at risk of being moved on and remains an integral part of the group.

After a promising 45 minutes in Stockholm against Atletico Madrid, this was another big step in the right direction by Amad.

It was his tenacity that stood out, the pressure he put on PSG's defenders and that was the origin of United's equalising goal when he closed down the ball, recovered possession and was decisive in playing in Mbeumo, who slotted away.

Amad can do a lot well that won't show up on the stats sheet but he is under no illusion that goals and assists have to improve. Prior to this assist for Mbeumo, Amad had just one United assist to his name in this calendar year, simply nowhere near a player of his ability should be.

'For me it's been good,' he said of pre-season after the PSG draw.

'We need to keep building fitness because we have a big season ahead of us and we need to keep going. It's a good game. We know how tough PSG are to beat and we draw, we now look to the next game.

'We have two more games and we need to keep building fitness, that's the most important thing. We have a big season coming and I hope we can win trophies this season.'

If United are to hit the heights Amad wants, he will need to be at his very best. There were flashes here to suggest the 24-year-old absolutely has the bit between his teeth.

Amad Diallo showcased another really promising outing as he faces a crucial campaign

HIGH RISK, HIGH REWARD

One of the most encouraging signs across United's pre-season is actually the bravery out of possession, rather than in it.

PSG, no matter how many players were rotated, are so well drilled and have so many great players on the periphery that avoiding defeat against them is no mean feat.

So to see Carrick setting his side up with such an aggressive high press, at times showing six players in the final third to press, will inject plenty of belief into supporters.

Other times we saw a zonal press in a 4-4-2 with Shea Lacey, making a third straight start, again as a No10, right up alongside Mbeumo.

Pre-season and competitive Premier League action are naturally different – but the signs are there. Be brave, and you'll get success. Now it's over to United's hierarchy to show that same aggression in the transfer market.

Sports.title: West Ham and Tottenham agree £5m fee for Manor Solomon, Barcelona to table new bid for Man City's Rodri - and Southampton eye move for Man United youngster: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
West Ham and Tottenham agree £5m fee for Manor Solomon, Barcelona to table new bid for Man City's Rodri - and Southampton eye move for Man United youngster: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Everton and Palace discuss McNeil-Johnson swap

Everton and Crystal Palace are in discussions over a potential swap deal between Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson.

McNeil was left upset after a move to Palace fell through in January while Johnson has been struggling to find his form since joining in a £35million deal from Tottenham also in the winter window.

The 25-year-old hasn't managed a single goal in his 18 appearances since joining the Eagles.

Everton and Crystal Palace are in discussions over a potential swap deal between Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson

He has also failed to earn a starting berth, and a trial as a right-wing back under former manager Oliver Glasner failed to trigger improvement. However, David Moyes is a long-term admirer.

McNeil rediscovered form after February but wants more regular starts.

Solomon fee agreed

West Ham and Tottenham have agreed a deal for Manor Solomon at £5million plus add-ons for the 27-year-old winger.

He is expected to undergo his medical over the next 48 hours.

Loan star Ronald Araujo to check in at Liverpool

Ronald Araujo will have a medical at Liverpool on Sunday ahead of completing his loan with option to buy from Barcelona.

Ronald Araujo will have a medical at Liverpool on Sunday ahead of a loan with option to buy

The fee on the option to buy for the 27-year-old defender is £47million.

Araujo is preparing to travel to link up with Liverpool ahead of signing his contract and meeting his new teammates tomorrow.

The Uruguay international gives Liverpool experience and vital defensive cover as he is able to play at centre-back and right-back.

Araujo wanted to go because after talks with coach Hansi Flick it was apparent he would not be guaranteed regular starts and he believes he will find greater opportunity to do so under Andoni Iraola at Liverpool.

The Spanish champions are working to offload a number of players as they look to upgrade their squad. They are focused on signing Rodri from Manchester City and still want to strengthen their own centre-back options and at striker.

Araujo will say farewell to Barcelona teammates today prior to heading for Merseyside on Sunday.

Liverpool remain in talks for Paris Saint-Germain pair Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye.

Full story

Forest on cusp of £36m Diomande move

Nottingham Forest are closing on a £36million deal for Sporting Lisbon centre-back Ousmane Diomande.

The proposed transfer looked to be off last week but a series of conversations have ironed out differences and the 22-year-old Ivory Coast international is due to travel over tomorrow ahead of undergoing a medical.

Forest have a five-year contract in place for the defender.

Forest centre-back Nikola Milenkovic is an option being considered by Juventus while Murillo also has interest from other clubs.

Nottingham Forest are closing on a £36m deal for Sporting centre back Ousmane Diomande

Barca set to table new Rodri bid

Barcelona are preparing a new bid for Manchester City midfielder Rodri after their initial £38million offer plus bonuses was dismissed.

City want £68million for the 30-year-old Spain captain.

Barca are looking to find moves for a number of players including Marc Casado, Roony Bardghji, Hector Fort, Alvaro Cortes, Tommy Marques, Ferran Torres, who is bound for Paris St Germain and Ronald Araujo who is off to Liverpool.

Hammers re-enter Solomon talks

West Ham have revived talks with Tottenham over a deal for winger Manor Solomon.

Talks initially broke down over bonuses due if West Ham were promoted which the Championship side thought were unreasonable but the clubs are working towards a £10million agreement.

Saints eye Man United youngster Kamason

Manchester United full-back Jaydan Kamason is wanted by Southampton.

The Championship side would like the 19-year-old England youth international on a permanent transfer and he is also receiving enquiries from others wanting him on loan.

Preston North End, Blackburn Rovers, Bristol City and Sheffield Wednesday have shown interest in the right-back while there are clubs abroad keen to take him.

Kamason though has a lot of admirers at Old Trafford. He was one of the academy players who excelled in the opening games of United's pre-season, particularly in the 5-0 win over Rosenborg.

He was the first player to sign scholarship forms at United after coming through the club's Emerging Talent Programme, which he joined at 10, while playing for grassroots team Stockport Vikings.

United have yet to decide on plans for his development but he looks likely to stay around Michael Carrick's squad until January.

Goalkeeper Radek Vítek has completed his move to Middlesbrough on a permanent transfer from United in a deal worth up to £14million.

Jaydan Kamason has excelled in pre-season games for United and has plenty of admirers

Geronimo Rulli medical at Man City

Marseille goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli is due to undergo a medical at Manchester City on Monday after the clubs agreed a £1.75million deal.

Rulli, who is set to sign a two-year deal at the Etihad, joins as a replacement for James Trafford, who completed a club-record move to Leeds for £45million.

Rulli has been identified by City as the man to provide backup to Gianluigi Donnarumma next season.

Atletico's Ruggeri to join Villa for £16million

Atletico Madrid left-back Matteo Ruggeri has agreed to join Aston Villa. The 24-year-old Italian will cost £16million plus add-ons.

His transfer will help pave the way for Atletico to bid for Tottenham captain Cristian Romero.

The Argentine centre-back is also among names being considered by Barcelona but Atletico coach Diego Simeone hopes to convince his compatriot if they can agree on terms.

Matteo Ruggeri's move should pave the way for Cristian Romero to join Atletico Madrid

Facundo Buonanotte leaves Brighton for Elche

Brighton midfielder Facundo Buonanotte has joined La Liga side Elche on a season-long loan.

The 21-year-old was on loan at two different Premier League clubs last season, spending the first half with Chelsea before joining Leeds in the second half of the campaign.

Sheffield Wednesday chase Liverpool star Scanlon

Liverpool left-back Calum Scanlon is wanted on loan by Sheffield Wednesday.

The 21-year-old spent the second half of last season on loan at Cardiff City and they are keen to take him back too.

Scanlon has impressed on Liverpool's pre-season and is attracting a number of enquiries but League One Wednesday, who play Bolton in the Carabao Cup today, are making a concerted effort to take the England U20 international to Hillsborough.

Sports.title: Why wasteful Spurs' behind-closed-doors draw with Getafe proves Roberto De Zerbi is right that they need a 'bomba' signing - and the summer arrival who will be key to their attacking exploits
Sports.content:
Why wasteful Spurs' behind-closed-doors draw with Getafe proves Roberto De Zerbi is right that they need a 'bomba' signing - and the summer arrival who will be key to their attacking exploits

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Roberto De Zerbi’s fears about Tottenham’s lack of firepower will be reinforced by his team’s latest preparation game.

Conor Gallagher scored the equaliser as Spurs came from behind in a fractious 1-1 draw against Getafe over 70 minutes behind closed doors at the club’s training centre in Enfield.

Positives included an instant response after going behind and more minutes in the tank, working through the stifling heat with two weeks to go before the Premier League season begins.

Roberto De Zerbi's concerns about a lack of firepower will be reinforced after their draw with Getafe

Lacking quality in front of goal

Spurs backed De Zerbi’s desire to strengthen midfield and bring experience into the back four, but he wants more options up front with the club interested in Savinho and Cody Gakpo among others and it’s not difficult to see why.

Richarlison led the line against Getafe, flanked in the front line by Mathys Tel and Mikey Moore, but the Brazilian who has strengths and was Spurs’ top scorer in the Premier League last season with 11 goals, issued a reminder that he does not have the instinct of a clinical predator.

Two terrific chances came his way in the second half, both in the air and both saved by goalkeeper David Soria. One in the first half was headed wide. Ben Davies headed the best chance of the first half straight at Soria from a free kick, delivered by Andy Robertson.

Moore chances slipping by

If this was Moore’s final opportunity to change De Zerbi’s thinking before a proposed loan move to Cologne, he might want to start packing for Germany.

The teenage winger, deployed against Getafe on the right, has found it difficult to recapture the sparkle of his early performances in Spurs colours.

He returned with a decent end-of-term report from a season at Rangers and is still very young, he will be 19 on Tuesday, but here he was again unable to impose his unquestionable talent on the game.

Low crosses from Tel on the left fizzed past him at the back post and he could not find the target with a looping header in the second half. Tel offered little in the first half but was more effective in the second and showed hints of developing an understanding with Robertson, who adds the balance of a natural left footer often missing last season.

Mikey Moore was unable to sparkle and looks set to make a season long loan to Cologne

Gallagher on target

If the strikers are misfiring Gallagher can be an alternative source of goals. Playing at his best, he will weigh in from midfield as he did against Getafe, driving forward onto a loose ball spilling out of a challenge on Richarlison, taking a touch and applying a firm low finish.

Gallagher, signed for £35million from Atletico Madrid in January, started to show glimpses of form towards the end of last season and should benefit further when De Zerbi imposes his high intensity style.

Against Getafe, they did not control possession as the Italian boss would want. There were flashes of Sandro Tonali, although the £100million midfielder was also easily distracted by a niggling late challenge.

Conor on target against Getafe 🎯 pic.twitter.com/HE48SGxuBn — Tottenham Hotspur (@SpursOfficial) August 8, 2026

Van Hecke passing range

There were signs on display of what De Zerbi will demand from £54m centre-half Jan Paul van Hecke, who got on the ball and sought to spark attacking patterns from the back with early passes forward through the lines.

His passing range is impressive. Although the Getafe goal came through his channel. Lucas Bergvall, in midfield beside Tonali, lost track of Alberto Risco.

Van Hecke came out of the back four to try and avert the danger but Risco was too quick for him, played a one-two and beat Antonin Kinsky with a crisp shot.

Jan Paul van Hecke will be key to Tottenham's build-up with passes through the lines

Absent stars making hearts grow fonder

De Zerbi made no changes through the 70 minutes played with barely a break at half time, with lots of senior players involved in another training game played at the training ground on Saturday. Six young subs were named plus goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario. None were used.

HOW THEY LINED UP Tottenham (4-2-3-1): Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Davies, Robertson; Tonali, Bergvall; Moore, Gallagher, Tel; Richarlison. Subs not used: Vicario, Takai, Donley, Scarlett, Yang, Hardy, Byrne.

Among those not involved against Getafe who are firmly back in the swing of preseason were Martin Dubravka, Kevin Danso, Micky van de Ven, Destiny Udogie, Rodrigo Bentancur, Pape Matar Sarr, Mateus Fernandes, James Maddison and Dominic Solanke.

De Zerbi did not appear too concerned as he reclined on the touchline. He will file it away as another valuable training exercise and look to strengthen the forward department before the deadline.

Xavi's touching gesture

Xavi Simons hosted the family of George Dennis, an 11-year-old Spurs fan killed by a lorry in Chipping Ongar in Essex in July, for the preseason friendly against Getafe on Saturday. Simons, who is out with a long-term knee injury, made the offer via social media after reading about the tragedy.

The Netherlands international gave the family, including George's cousin who witnessed the crash, a tour of the training ground and presented the children with Spurs shirts and boots and the parents with flowers before they all watched the 1-1 draw played behind closed doors.

Sports.title: Defiant David Sullivan attends West Ham's Carabao Cup victory over Portsmouth after claiming he was being 'bullied' into not watching it amid sexual misconduct allegations
Sports.content:
David Sullivan emerged to take his seat, cloaked in a thick black bomber jacket. Hardly attire befitting the 28-degree sunshine blazing down on the London Stadium but, as Sullivan has made clear of late, he’s not too interested in reading the room.

The stadiums operators told West Ham they didn’t want him here because they were worried about fan unrest. The club’s own fan advisory board said his presence would cause ‘offence and upset’.

Sullivan remains the club’s largest shareholder but resigned as co-chair in June amid allegations of sexual misconduct, which he strongly denies, and no longer controls the day-to-day running of the club.

This is, after all, supposed to be the fresh start that West Ham need. It’s taken relegation to the Championship and boardroom scandal for them to get it but after years of rotten decline this was, at long last, meant to be it and a gentle stroll into the second round of the Carabao Cup under the afternoon sun should be the ideal way to begin.

Everyone should be talking about how Jarrod Bowen, the loyal captain who stuck with the club, scored one and set up another for Taty Castellanos and showed the kind of quality that will see them as one of the favourites to go back up regardless of how clumsily they played in the first half. Or of the impressive displays of youngsters Lewis Orford and especially Mohamadou Kante in a 3-1 win over Portsmouth.

And yet how can the club make a clean break when the man so many supporters hold responsible for their plight, and against whose ownership they have long protested, was so keen to ignore all that advice.

David Sullivan takes his seat at the London Stadium for West Ham's game with Portsmouth

West Ham came from behind to beat Portsmouth 3-1 in the Carabao Cup first round

Daily Mail Sport revealed on Friday that Sullivan felt he was being ‘bullied’ by ‘keyboard warriors’ into staying away. He was concerned about the lack of transfer activity, now that he’s no longer the man signing the cheques.

The club have so far turned the loan signing of youngster Keiber Lamadrid permanent and snapped up Joel Veltman, who came on for his debut, on a free from Brighton despite selling Mateus Fernandes and Crysencio Summerville for a combined £150million. Why should anyone be able to tell him he can’t watch the club he supports?

Not one for reading the room.

Many behind the scenes at West Ham were shocked he planned to attend. Daily Mail Sport knew of one staff member who decided not to come due to the ‘circus’ of it all.

For Nuno Espirito Santo, at least, it was business as usual. ‘We are focused on what happens on the pitch,’ he said. ‘The noise that comes from outside cannot distract us at all. We are going to find a lot of noise. We focus on the game, do their job, and they did it well.’

The last time Sullivan was here, the final game of the season against Leeds when West Ham’s relegation to the Championship was confirmed, he did not stay until the end. Fans pelted him with abuse and he left before full-time.

He made it all the way this time. For all the worries that his attendance might turn the place toxic, he sat there unperturbed and unpestered. The first boos of the afternoon were not even in his direction but at a hydration break during the first half while the PA system played The Bouncer by Kicks Like a Mule. The burly bloke sat next to Sullivan throughout the game looked like he just might.

If anything, the fans acted as if he wasn’t even there. Daily Mail Sport was outside the directors' entrance in September when thousands gathered outside to protest against Sullivan’s ownership. Even though his expected attendance had been well-publicised, none bothered this time.

The only chant came on 63 minutes when, coasting at 3-1 up, the fans rose in unison to the chant of: ‘Stand up if you hate the board’. Sullivan, to be fair, is not even on it these days. He remains the leading shareholder, although former Newcastle co-owner Amanda Staveley would like to change that.

West Ham fans largely acted as though Sullivan was not there as they looked to make a fresh start after the club's relegation

Sullivan, with Karren Brady in 1993, resigned as West Ham's co-chair in June ahead of the airing of an investigation in which seven women accused Sullivan of predatory behaviour

The fans were too busy trying to make that fresh start. Before kick-off, a clock on the big screen displayed a ‘countdown to walkout’. It meant the players, of course, but this place has seen more than its fair share of exoduses in recent years.

Not this time. For the first round of the League Cup, the London Stadium was impressively full. Forever Blowing Bubbles echoed so loudly around the place that a West Ham-supporting member of the press pack turned and grinned: ‘Not bad for a Championship side’.

In fact, it was the travelling Portsmouth fans who took it upon themselves to make the first move. ‘You sold your soul for this s***hole,’ erupted from the away end after four minutes.

If there was going to be a moment when it turned foul, it was when Adrian Segecic long-range effort deflected off the perennially unfortunate Max Kilman to give Portsmouth a deserved lead.

Nuno Espirito Santo’s side, to their credit, didn’t need long to turn it around. Kante produced some marvellous skill down the left before crossing to an unmarked Castellanos for the equaliser before Bowen curled a beauty from outside the box to put West Ham in front.

Sullivan remained in his seat and clapped. He did so again after half-time when Castellanos nodded in Bowen’s cross and, once more, at full-time. As the whistle blew, he stood up, grabbed his jacket, and left the room. Regardless of the advice, you suspect he’ll be back.

Sports.title: Man United handed major injury blow just two weeks before the start of the season as Mason Mount hobbles off after only 20 minutes against PSG
Sports.content:
Man United handed major injury blow just two weeks before the start of the season as Mason Mount hobbles off after only 20 minutes against PSG

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Mason Mount was forced off with an injury during Manchester United's friendly against Paris Saint-Germain.

The midfielder has been one of United's standout performers in pre-season, but his latest appearance was cut short after he was substituted just 20 minutes into the match in Gothenburg and replaced by Tyler Fletcher.

Mount spoke to three members of the medical staff before heading down the tunnel and appeared to be experiencing a problem with his foot. The 27-year-old was able to jog off when his number was shown, suggesting the decision may have been precautionary.

Even so, Michael Carrick is unlikely to take any risks with the start of the new campaign rapidly approaching.

United, who qualified for the Champions League with their third-place finish last term, begin their season away at newly-promoted Hull in two weeks. They then host Ipswich and travel to Everton before Old Trafford stages the Manchester derby on September 13.

The midfielder has been one of United's standout performers in pre-season, but his latest appearance was cut short after he was substituted just 20 minutes into the match

Mount, who joined United from Chelsea in a £60million deal in 2023, has struggled with injuries during his time at the club, making 72 appearances across three seasons.

Of the three seasons he has been at United, he made the most top-flight appearances last term with 23, averaging just 44 minutes per game.

In Sweden, United drew 1-1 to United fell behind in the second minute when 18-year-old striker Ibrahim Mbaye buried his chance at the far post.

Bryan Mbeumo then levelled the scoring half an hour later. Amad Diallo won the ball and carried it forward before feeding Mbeumo to the left of the box, with the Cameroonian burying his shot into the far corner.

Neither side could find a winner after the break as the match finished 1-1.

Sports.title: Fiji rugby player, 26, dies from suspected heatstroke after training session in Japan
Sports.content:
Fiji rugby player, 26, dies from suspected heatstroke after training session in Japan

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Fijian rugby player Saimoni Vunilagi has died of suspected heatstroke following a training session in Japan.

Vunilagi, who was 26, played for Japanese second division team Kyushu KV.

Kyushu KV announced Vunilagi had died on Friday morning in a hospital in Fukuoka City, after being hospitalised earlier in the week due to severe heatstroke.

'After team practice on Monday, August 3, 2026, Saimoni displayed symptoms consistent with severe heatstroke,' a team statement read.

'He was transported to a medical facility for treatment, but despite the best efforts of the medical team, he sadly passed away.

'The players, staff, and all team associates are devastated by this sudden news.

Fijian rugby player Saimoni Vunilagi has died aged 26 from suspected heatstroke after a training session in Japan

'Although Saimoni had only recently joined Kyushu KV, his generous spirit and powerful style of play had raised high hopes for his contributions in the upcoming season.

'We humbly pray for the repose of his soul and extend our heartfelt condolences to his bereaved family.

'At this time of profound grief, we respectfully ask the family be granted space and privacy.'

Temperatures in Fukuoka had reportedly reached around 35 degrees Celsius on Monday, the day Vunilagi was hospitalised.

The back rower had only joined the team last month, having previously played for top-flight team Tokyo Sungoliath.

'We are deeply saddened to learn of the passing of Saimoni Vunirangi, a wrestler belonging to Kyushu Electric Power's Kyuden Voltex,' a Japan Rugby League One statement read.

'We extend our heartfelt condolences to his family and all those involved.'

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
