World.title: Ukraine denies targeting Bulgaria as drone explodes near pipeline
World.content:
Ukraine President, Zelensky

Ukraine on Saturday denied targeting Bulgaria after a drone exploded close to the strategic Trans-Balkan gas pipeline linking Turkey to Ukraine near the Romanian border.

Bulgaria’s defence ministry said the drone was of a type “widely used by the Ukrainian military”, and the foreign minister summoned the Ukrainian ambassador for a meeting on Monday in response, her office told AFP.

Kyiv said it was “in close contact with the Bulgarian side to clarify the circumstances” of the incident, the latest case of a drone straying into NATO airspace as Ukraine fights off Russia’s invasion.

“We can say with certainty that the Ukrainian Armed Forces did not intentionally direct any assets toward Bulgaria,” Ukraine’s foreign ministry spokesman Georgiy Tykhyi said, blaming Russia’s invasion for the incident.

While the explosion caused no casualties, Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said the amount of explosives it was carrying was “significant”.

“The drone exploded in the immediate vicinity of the Kardam border-crossing with Romania,” near the Black Sea in the country’s northeast, “1,000 metres from the Trans-Balkan gas pipeline’s compressor station,” he said in a video released by the government.

After analysing the debris from the crash, Bulgaria’s defence ministry however said that “currently, nothing suggests that this was a deliberate incident”.

The drone eventually crashed into a sunflower field, Radev said.

– A ‘loud explosion’ –

Romania border police recorded the sound of the drone, then a Bulgarian border police patrol spotted “a loud explosion accompanied by black smoke”, Radev added, speaking after an extraordinary meeting of his cabinet’s security council.

“One thing is certain: the drone was carrying a significant amount of explosives, given that it could be heard from a distance and produced such black smoke,” he said.

The drone had not been detected by either of the two neighbouring countries, he said, adding: “As you know, identifying and neutralising these drones poses a major challenge.”

Incidents involving drones have become increasingly frequent in recent months across eastern European countries that are NATO members and supporters of Ukraine in its conflict with Russia.

Romania has faced frequent drone incursions since the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 — — including some crashes on its territory. It ordered the expulsion of a Russian embassy staff member in late July.

Radev said that, following the latest incident, Bulgaria had boosted its surveillance and would redeploy troops and soldiers to the borders to detect drones and employ anti-drone measures.

– Several recent incidents –

Bulgaria, Romania and Turkey all front onto the Black Sea, an arena of drone combat by both Ukraine and Russia.

Turkish officials on Tuesday said a drone attack the previous day on two civilian vessels in the Black Sea had injured crew members. Turkey’s foreign ministry said it was “deeply concerned about the escalating conflict” in the body of water.

Bulgaria in June halted its military aid to Ukraine. Radev said the country did not belong in the coalition of Kyiv’s allies supplying arms and that he preferred to see diplomatic efforts to end the war.

Further west, a German military operational command spokesman told AFP on Saturday that drones were detected this week above an army installation in western Germany known to house a large underground depot.

Among other armaments, the Mechernich special site is home to parts for US-made Patriot air-defence systems long coveted by Kyiv.

Those sightings came days after an explosives-laden drone was found near a Ukrainian cargo plane at Leipzig-Halle airport, which plays a key role in the transport of military goods by the German military and NATO allies.

AFP

World.title: Police quiz Osun Commissioner over gunshots at APC rally
World.content:
One of the injured.

By Shina Abubakar, OSOGBO

The Police have arrested Osun State Commissioner for Environment, Mr Mayowa Asejoorin, in connection with gunshots fired at the All Progressives Congress, APC, holds rally in Ilesa on Saturday.

Four persons were reportedly injured in the incident.

It was gathered that the APC supporters, during the rally in Ilesa metropolis, were attacked by some Accord chieftains, during which sporadic gunshots heard.

As a result, people sustained different degrees of injury, including a 14-year-old Ilesanmi.

As at press time, no casualty has been recorded. But the injured victims have been taken to the hospital for treatment.

An eyewitness, Kola Adeoti disclosed that the boy was at his mother’s shop when he was hit by a stray bullet on his thigh.

He added personnel of a security outfit based in the state, who escorted the Accord chieftains shot directly at the APC members which led to protest in Ilesa.

Contacted, the Osun State Police Command spokesperson DSP Abiodun Ojelabi confirmed the report.

He said the Commissioner for Environment, Mr Mayowa Asejoorin was arrested in connection with the incident.

“Immediately the incident was reported, our personnel moved to the scene, cordoned off the area before some exhibit were recovered, which included expanded cartridges, Amotekun personnel caps.

“Also, Mr Adejoorin was arrested the scene and has been taken to the command for questioning as part of the investigation process,” he added.

Vanguard News

World.title: US slams Chinese actions in South China Sea
World.content:
China’s President Xi Jinping (Photo by Maxim Shemetov / POOL / AFP)

The United States on Saturday accused China of “destabilizing” activity near the disputed Scarborough Shoal in the South China Sea, saying it is using “dubious” environmental explanations to advance its territorial claims.

Scarborough Shoal is a fish-rich reef formation 240 kilometers (124 miles) from the main Philippine island of Luzon and hundreds of kilometers away from mainland China. Both Beijing and Manila claim the flashpoint coral atoll.

“The United States rejects China’s ongoing attempts to enforce its destabilizing ‘national nature reserve’ at Scarborough Reef and deny Filipino fishermen access to their traditional fishing ground,” State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott said.

“This is yet another unilateral attempt by China to use dubious environmental and legal pretexts, backed by coercion, to advance its sweeping territorial and maritime claims in the South China Sea at the expense of its neighbors,” Pigott said in a statement.

China recently published new rules on the management of the nature reserve it unilaterally created last year around the shoal, which is controlled by Beijing.

Beijing claims most of the South China Sea, including the flashpoint shoal, despite an international ruling that its assertion lacks any legal basis.

China and the Philippines regularly clash over disputed territories. The most recent incidents took place last month.

AFP

World.title: UI removes admission quota barrier for distance learning candidates
World.content:
University of Ibadan

By Adeola Badru

The University of Ibadan (UI) has declared that limited admission quotas and inadequate physical space on campus should no longer prevent qualified candidates from obtaining admission into the institution, offering them an alternative route through its Open, Distance and eLearning (ODeL) programme.

The university said the initiative was designed to provide a second opportunity for candidates who participated in its Post-UTME screening exercise but could not secure admission through the conventional face-to-face mode because of limited admission quotas and physical space constraints.

The institution disclosed that the special application window for the 2025/2026 academic session would close on August 15, 2026, while classes for the special cohort are scheduled to commence on August 17, 2026.

The Director of the UI Distance Learning Centre (DLC), Prof. Olufade Onifade, stated this in a statement issued by the centre, urging eligible candidates to take advantage of the opportunity before the application deadline.

Onifade said candidates who sat for the University of Ibadan Post-UTME examination could switch from the conventional on-campus mode to the ODeL programme at no cost.

He said, “The UI-ODeL programme provides flexible virtual classes with mobile learning, interactive course materials and physical revision sessions. Courses are taught by the same faculty lecturers who handle conventional programmes, and learners graduate with the same prestigious University of Ibadan degree.”

According to him, the ODeL programme provides access to first-degree programmes across a wide range of disciplines, thereby enabling qualified candidates to pursue university education without being constrained by the limitations of physical classroom capacity.

Onifade listed some of the programmes available under the initiative as B.Sc. Computer Science, B.Sc. Statistics, B.Sc. Psychology, B.Sc. Economics, B.Sc. Political Science, B.Sc. Sociology, B.A. English, B.A. Communication and Language Arts, B.Ed. Educational Management and B.Sw. Social Work, among others.

He further explained that candidates who participated in the 2026 UI Post-UTME exercise were eligible for the free change-of-mode offer.

“Candidates who took the 2026 UI PUTME qualify for the free change-of-mode offer. Such candidates are required to visit the official change-of-mode application portal to switch their mode of study from the conventional on-campus option to the ODeL programme,” he said.

The DLC director added that other interested candidates who met the requirements could also submit fresh applications to join the special cohort.

He urged eligible applicants to act promptly, stressing that the August 15 deadline was fast approaching and available spaces could be taken up quickly.

“Other interested candidates who are qualified may submit a fresh application for the special cohort. With the August 15 deadline fast approaching, the university encourages qualified candidates to act immediately, as slots are expected to fill up quickly,” Onifade said.

The university maintained that the ODeL pathway offers candidates the opportunity to obtain a University of Ibadan degree while benefiting from flexible learning arrangements that combine virtual instruction, mobile learning, interactive academic materials and physical revision sessions.

World.title: Nigeria risks losing out on fresh $1.4bn US aid over ‘Christian persecution’
World.content:
By Nkiruka Nnorom

Nigeria may be excluded from a new $1.4 billion U.S health and humanitarian assistance package announced earlier this week if the Federal Government fails to take measurable actions to address violence against Christians, according to terms contained in a bilateral Memorandum of Understanding signed by both countries.

The MOU, signed on December 20, 2025 between the U.S Department of State and the Nigerian government under the America First Global Health Strategy, AFGHS, commits Washington to nearly $2.1 billion over five years to expand preventative and curative services for HIV, TB, malaria, maternal and child health and polio.

Under the MoU, Nigeria is also expected to increase its domestic health spending by nearly $3 billion during the term, an expenditure that has been described as the largest co-investment under AFGHS.

A significant portion of the U.S funding is earmarked for Nigeria’s 900 faith-based clinics and hospitals, which currently serve more than 30 percent of Nigerians.

However, the deal contains strict conditions. The MOU states that the agreement was “negotiated in connection with reforms the Nigerian government has made to prioritize protecting Christian populations from violence” and includes “significant dedicated funding” for Christian health facilities.

Crucially, it adds: “As with all foreign assistance, the President and Secretary of State retain the right to pause or terminate any programme which do not align with the national interest, and the Trump administration expects Nigeria to continue to make progress ensuring that it combats extremist religious violence against vulnerable Christian populations.”

The conditionality was reinforced by the U.S House of Representatives, which recently voted to tie Nigeria’s aid to verifiable steps on tackling Christian persecution.

The bill passed last month by the House of Rep tasked Abuja with taking concrete actions to ensure the return of internally displaced persons to their ancestral homes and ensuring protection for persecuted Christians in the Middle Belt region among others.

Meanwhile, in the fresh aid approved by Washington under its AFGHS, the U.S set aside $1.4 billion to support integrated health services through faith and community-based hospitals and clinics in more than 20 countries.

Out of it, $850 million will go through a Faith and Community Initiative Award to World Vision and local faith-based implementers to strengthen over 2,500 faith-based hospitals and clinics across 17 countries with more than 30,000 community health workers trained, paid, and equipped.

An additional $570 million will be channelled directly to faith-based and community hospitals through bilateral MOUs with governments, including Nigeria.

In humanitarian assistance, the State Department also announced $538 million for Samaritan’s Purse and a World Vision–Compassion International consortium to reach 7 million people across 16 humanitarian crises. Over $100 million will be made immediately available for disaster response in 23 disaster-prone countries.

The State Department said the combined $1.4 billion health announcement is the largest to faith-based organisations in over 20 years, with at least 80 percent of resources required to go directly to frontline services.

For Nigeria, the MOU specifically emphasised support for Christian faith-based health care providers, which are described in the agreement as “uniquely positioned” to complement public facilities.

With the U.S shifting more resources to faith-based delivery where such providers account for 40 per cent or more of health facilities in many aid-recipient countries, Nigeria’s access to the new funding will depend on how Abuja addresses concerns raised in Washington.

The State Department said partners like Samaritan’s Purse, World Vision and Compassion International were chosen for their record of rapid deployment in conflict zones and disaster areas without bureaucratic delay.

World.title: Nigerians abandoning plans to buy homes, cars, Atiku slams Tinubu for cost of living
World.content:
Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar

By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: Presidential Candidate of the African Democratic Congress ADC, Atiku Abubakar, has described the latest Central Bank of Nigeria CBN Household Expectations Survey as a damning verdict on President Bola Tinubu’s economic policies, saying an economy in which citizens are abandoning plans to buy homes, cars and basic household assets cannot credibly be advertised as one on the path to prosperity.

In a statement issued by his Senior Special Assistant on Public Communication, Phrank Shaibu, on Friday in Abuja, Atiku said the CBN’s own numbers have stripped the government’s economic propaganda of whatever credibility it had left.

According to the survey, buying conditions stood at just 28.7 points for motor vehicles, 28.9 for consumer durables and 30.0 for buildings and landed property. Even more disturbing, willingness to purchase vehicles fell to 18.7 points, while buildings and landed property stood at only 19.2 points.

“These are not figures manufactured by the opposition. They are the verdict of Nigerian households captured by the Central Bank under President Tinubu’s own government,” Atiku said, adding that the figures show Nigerians are being priced out of decent living, with a home “becoming a fantasy” and a car “becoming a luxury.”

He said families are exhausting their incomes on food, transportation, electricity, school fees and other necessities, leaving practically nothing for savings, investment or asset acquisition.

Citing the latest SBM Jollof Index, Atiku noted that the ingredients required to prepare a single pot of jollof rice for a family of five now cost an average of ₦29,578, meaning that for a worker earning the ₦70,000 minimum wage, one pot of jollof rice can swallow more than 40 per cent of an entire month’s salary, before rent, transportation, electricity, school fees and healthcare are considered.

“Tinubu has not merely made life more expensive; his policies are steadily pricing ordinary Nigerians out of food, comfort, asset ownership and the basic dignity of a decent life,” he said.

According to him, it was particularly insulting for the Tinubu administration to continue celebrating headline macroeconomic indicators while the personal economies of Nigerian families deteriorate.

“Government officials can celebrate GDP growth, foreign reserves and other statistics from air-conditioned conference rooms, but ordinary Nigerians have become unwilling economists, calculating every cup of rice, every litre of fuel and every transport fare before deciding what their families can afford,” he said, adding that “between official statistics and empty cooking pots, the cooking pots do not lie.”

He warned that the collapse in household purchasing power also threatens the wider economy, noting that when citizens cannot consume, businesses cannot sell; when businesses cannot sell, production falls; and when production falls, jobs and livelihoods disappear.

“An economy is not successful merely because government officials can quote favourable statistics. An economy succeeds when citizens can work, earn, eat, save, invest and progressively improve their standard of living,” Atiku said, insisting that “before there is GDP, there must be dinner. Before there is prosperity, there must be purchasing power.

“President Tinubu should stop governing Nigeria through PowerPoint economics. The real economy is the Nigerian family’s pocket, and that pocket is increasingly empty.

“Tinubu has not merely increased the cost of living. He has increased the cost of dreaming”, he said.

World.title: Every father would want a son like Seyi Tinubu – Showunmi
World.content:
Segun Showunmi has praised Seyi Tinubu for his leadership approach and commitment to inclusive politics after visiting the City Boy Movement office.

In a message shared on X and addressed to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Showunmi said no father could have a son like Seyi Tinubu and not be deeply thankful to God.

“There are many achievements a man may record in public life, but among the greatest blessings bestowed upon any father is to see his values reflected in his children,” Showunmi wrote. “In Seyi, I see a young man who is working hard to justify the confidence reposed in him and to earn his place through effort and commitment.”

Showunmi said he recently visited the City Boy Movement office, where Seyi Tinubu personally took him around the facility. He described what he saw as impressive, not because of the building itself, but because of the thinking behind it.

“It was a truly pan-Nigerian operation. Young Nigerians from different regions, backgrounds, and faiths were working together toward a common objective. The team was gender-balanced. Diversity and inclusivity were not slogans on a wall; they were visible in practice. Persons living with disabilities had their own space and representation. Every detail suggested careful planning and deliberate leadership,” he stated.

What struck him most, Showunmi said, was the culture within the organisation.

“I watched Seyi interact with his team. I saw him share snacks with members of his back-end staff. There was no air of superiority, no unnecessary distance. Respect flowed naturally. The people around him appeared motivated not merely because they worked with him, but because they felt valued by him,” he added.

He noted that leadership is often revealed in moments when cameras are absent and speeches are not being made, adding that character is found in the little things.

Addressing the President, Showunmi said: “Mr. President, I do not know what special favour from God has produced such a blessing, but I can say without reservation that you have a son worthy of admiration. As for me, I see in Seyi a younger brother whose dedication, energy, and commitment to service make me proud.”

He encouraged Seyi Tinubu to continue his work.

“ST, keep going. The seeds you are planting today will bear fruit tomorrow. The hours you spend, the sacrifices you make, and the bridges you are building across our national divides will not go unnoticed,” Showunmi said.

He expressed confidence that Seyi’s efforts would contribute meaningfully to the cause he believes in and demonstrate that political engagement can be organised, inclusive, respectful and purposeful.

“May the Almighty reward your labour, strengthen your resolve, and continue to guide your steps,” he added.

Showunmi concluded that every father desires a son who will add value to his legacy, and every nation needs young people prepared to work, unite others and serve with humility.

“From what I have seen, Seyi Tinubu is striving to be such a man. Character is what you do when no one is watching. Keep building, ST,” he said.

“May God bless you. May God bless your family. And may God bless the Federal Republic of Nigeria.”

World.title: PFIPC: Punishing ‘impostor’ won’t explain who opened govt doors — ADC
World.content:
ADC National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi

By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has dismissed the interim report of the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) on the alleged fake Presidential Foreign Intervention Promotion Council (PFIPC), saying it failed to explain how a fictitious agency gained access to the machinery of government.

For the opposition party, the bigger question is not simply how one man allegedly posed as a government official, but how the supposed fake agency got office space at the Federal Secretariat, civil servants, official vehicles, armed security and a N1.3 billion provision in the 2026 budget.

In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC said the ICPC report was predictable and appeared more interested in damage control and exonerating government officials than in answering the questions thrown up by the scandal.

“The ICPC report appeared to have given the impression that what happened was mere failure in government processes or procedures. This position is difficult to sustain in the light of publicly available evidence,” Abdullahi said.

The party said the alleged PFIPC was not created by Nigerian law or any legitimate executive approval, yet managed to secure the institutional backing required to operate as though it were a government agency.

It took particular exception to the ICPC’s recommendation that Adeyemi be prosecuted while suggesting that there could be other accomplices within government without identifying any.

“If all that the commission had to present was a preliminary report, why not simply present it as confidential brief to the President instead of making a public drama of it in a manner that potentially prejudiced the overall investigation and cast Adeyemi as the principal culprit?” the ADC asked.

The party said the N1.3 billion reportedly provided for PFIPC in the 2026 Appropriation Act was a key issue requiring explanation.

It said the National Assembly had already commenced an investigation into how the allocation found its way into the budget, insisting that the process should reveal who proposed the provision, who processed it and who verified the agency that was supposed to receive the money.

“Budgetary provisions do not materialise by accident. They leave records, submissions, approvals and an audit trail,” the ADC said.

The party also questioned how PFIPC secured accommodation within the Federal Secretariat and how civil servants were deployed to an organisation the Presidency now says never existed.

“To prosecute Mr. Adeyemi without answering these questions would be to punish the man who entered through the window while refusing to ask who left the doors open,” the ADC said.

It also raised the issue of a purported appointment letter bearing the signature of the Chief of Staff to the President, which investigators reportedly found to have been forged.

The ADC said establishing that the signature was forged only addressed the beginning of the alleged deception, not how the document passed through subsequent layers of government verification.

“A forgery may explain the first door that was opened. It cannot explain why every subsequent door appears to have opened as well,” the party stated.

The ADC said the reported discovery by the ICPC of two other fictitious organisations allegedly linked to Adeyemi should have expanded the investigation rather than narrowed its focus to one suspect.

It said the development raised questions about how the administration’s systems allowed such organisations to acquire what appeared to be official legitimacy.

The party recalled that when President Bola Tinubu directed the ICPC to investigate the matter, it had instead called for a full investigation by an independent panel, arguing that an agency of government could not adequately probe a scandal involving government institutions.

“What has happened is a national disgrace in the full glare of the entire world. No serious government should be satisfied with identifying one culprit for prosecution,” the ADC said.

It demanded the immediate publication of the full ICPC interim report and called for every public official whose actions or negligence enabled the alleged fictitious organisations to obtain official legitimacy to be identified and held accountable where wrongdoing is established.

The party said Nigerians were not asking the government to manufacture culprits, but to follow the evidence wherever it leads, warning that anything less would amount to an exercise aimed at containing the embarrassment rather than uncovering the truth.

World.title: Oath-taking Video: APC’s Desperate Attempt To Smear Adeleke Will Not Save Him From Defeat, Says Imole Campaign Council
World.content:
Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo

The Imole Campaign Council has described as laughable and defeatist the attempt by the Osun State All Progressives Congress (APC) Governorship Campaign Council to link Governor Ademola Adeleke to an alleged oath-taking video currently circulating on social media, stating emphatically that the governor has absolutely no connection whatsoever with any such activity.

In a statement issued yesterday by the Chairman, Media Committee, The Imole Campaign Council, Bamidele Salam, said the council is presently examining the authenticity, source and circumstances surrounding the video in question.

According to him, “It is important to state categorically that Governor Ademola Adeleke has neither authorised, participated in, directed nor endorsed the taking of any oath by anyone in relation to the August 15 governorship election or for any other political purpose.

“Governor Adeleke is a democrat who believes fundamentally in the freedom of citizens to make their political choices according to their conscience. He does not need oaths, threats, intimidation or any form of coercion to secure the support of the people of Osun State.”

He further said, “Indeed, the governor enjoys broad and demonstrable support across the state based on his record of performance and his personal connection with the people. His campaign is therefore anchored on his achievements, his vision for Osun and the confidence of the electorate, not on superstition, coercion or clandestine practices.

“The APC’s attempt to immediately attribute an unverified social media video to Governor Adeleke is therefore nothing but a hard-sell political manoeuvre by an opposition that is increasingly confronted with the reality of its rejection by the Osun electorate.

“The APC’s attempt to convert an unverified video into a campaign issue also exposes the poverty of its campaign strategy. Rather than engage Governor Adeleke’s administration on roads, healthcare, education, workers’ welfare, infrastructure, rural development and other measurable areas of governance, the opposition has resorted to allegations based on videos whose provenance remains unclear.

“But let there be no ambiguity: Governor Ademola Adeleke does not require anybody to swear an oath before supporting him. He does not require anyone to invoke a curse before voting for him. He does not require supernatural intervention to win an election. His strength is the people. His campaign is based on his record. His mandate belongs to the electorate.”

Salam noted that the APC should therefore stop looking for excuses in videos and begin preparing for the verdict of the Osun people on August 15.

“The people of Osun are not being asked to vote for Governor Adeleke because of any oath. They are being asked to vote for him because they have seen the difference between a government that works for the people and an opposition that has offered little beyond fear, propaganda and empty accusations.

“Governor Adeleke will face the people on August 15 with his record. Let the APC face the people with its own record.”

World.title: Benue ADC Guber Candidate Confident Atiku Will Win 2027 Presidential Election
World.content:
George Okoh in Makurdi

The governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Benue State, Herman Hembe, has declared that the ADC’s presidential candidate, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, will win the 2027 election.

Hembe disclosed this in Makurdi yesterday while unveiling his deputy, John Abba.

He had constituted a committee to select the party deputy governorship candidate a few days after he emerged as the party’s gubernatorial candidate.

According to Hembe, the selection of deputy governorship candidate which has the endorsement of the national chairman of the party, Senator David Mark, was transparent.

Hembe said, “Let me congratulate Abba on his selection as deputy governorship candidate of the party. We constituted a team to consult and get the deputy governorship candidate and our leader, David Mark ensured the process was transparent.”

Speaking on the permutations, Hembe stated that all things are working in favour of the party presidential candidate.

“Our permutations are that the votes from the Southern part of the country will be shared between Peter Obi and Bola Tinubu and we are very sure that none of Obi and Tinubu will be able to defeat Atiku in the three geo political zones in the North,” Hembe said.

While charging the party members to go all out to work for all the party candidates at the presidential election, Hembe assured that there will be band wagon effects on the second election.

“Our hardest job is to work and ensure that our party wins the presidential and National Assembly elections, then, we will just go and sleep because that victory will have a positive effect on our election.”

Hembe promised that he is only going to spend a term in office to complete the eight years of Jechira Zone and create history to hand over to the Benue South senatorial district, known as Zone C.

World.title: 2027: Kogi East APC Stakeholders Back Tinubu, Ododo, Demand Power Rotation
World.content:
• Say East will no longer be appendage to any political bloc

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

Ahead of the 2027 general election, critical stakeholders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kogi East Senatorial District have declared their total support for the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo, while demanding a fresh and equitable framework for political power rotation in Kogi State.

The stakeholders, who spoke through a communiqué issued at the end of their Strategic Leadership Conference in Abuja and made available to THISDAY on Saturday, said Kogi East would no longer accept a political arrangement that relegated the senatorial district to the status of an appendage of another political bloc.

They also called for direct negotiations with political stakeholders from Kogi Central and Kogi West on what they described as “distinct, transparent and equitable” terms to establish a predictable framework for power transition and inclusive development in the state.

The stakeholders said their immediate priority was to ensure victory for the APC in the January/February 2027 general election, particularly the re-election of Tinubu and the victory of all APC candidates contesting National and State Assembly seats.

They further pledged to mobilise support for Governor Ododo’s re-election for a second term in the November 2027 governorship election.

According to them, the political objective was not merely to win elections but to reposition Kogi East within the mainstream of state and national politics and secure what they described as the “deserved share of development” for the district.

The communiqué noted that Kogi East had recorded the highest bloc vote for President Tinubu among the three senatorial districts of Kogi State in the 2023 presidential election, stressing that the district was prepared to increase its contribution to the APC in 2027.

He said: “We look forward to increasing our electoral contributions to the APC and to strengthening our collaboration with our fellow compatriots from Kogi Central and Kogi West Senatorial Districts to return power to Kogi East.

“However, we are resolved to mobilise total support for the incumbent governor, Alhaji Ahmed Usman Ododo, and his re-election for his second term come

2027.”

The declaration came against the backdrop of what the stakeholders described as more than a decade of political fractures, disaffection and missed opportunities in Kogi State following the 2015 governorship election and the death of the late former governor, Prince Abubakar Audu.

They said attempts to achieve political realignment in 2019 and 2023 were not sustained, leaving ordinary citizens of Kogi East to bear the consequences of prolonged political disagreements.

The stakeholders insisted that the time had come to heal the wounds, rebuild trust among the three senatorial districts and establish a new political understanding based on equity, inclusion and mutual respect.

They said: “We refuse to allow old wounds to permanently damage the deep historical linkages between the people of the various sections of Kogi State.

“Our only path to reawaken the political strength of Kogi East is to encourage healthy collaboration with the other sections of the state and negotiate truthfully for all that our people deserve.

“We reject any attempt to make Kogi East an appendage of any group in the state.”

The stakeholders invoked the political legacy of Prince Audu, saying his philosophy was anchored on statewide unity, inclusion, dialogue and equitable distribution of development.

They recalled that during Audu’s administration, major projects were conceived and executed across the three senatorial districts, including the establishment of the state university in Anyigba and the Obajana Cement Project, as well as roads and other civic infrastructure.

They argued that the late governor’s political philosophy should be revived as the foundation for a new era of cooperation in Kogi State.

“That is the true political philosophy we must revive today: vision, selflessness, courage, fraternity, equity and shared purpose,” the communiqué stated.

The stakeholders also demanded an immediate shift towards a predictable political transition arrangement, arguing that sustainable development could not be achieved where political succession remained a source of tension.

According to them, “We assemble here today to lay a solid foundation for Kogi East to be part of a realistic, predictable and harmonious political transition in Kogi State.

“We call for an immediate shift towards building consensus, renegotiating power transfer and rotation, and establishing an inclusive, development-driven agenda that guarantees equitable access to the instruments of power.”

The group also sought national recognition for Audu, describing him as a statesman whose contribution to Nigeria’s democratic development should not be confined to his final years in politics.

It urged the Kogi State Government to present Audu’s contributions to the Federal Government for a “highly merited and long-overdue national honour”.

The stakeholders cited the 10th anniversary commemorative events held in Lokoja in October 2025, which brought together national political leaders, traditional rulers and former governors, as evidence of the late governor’s enduring national stature.

They also noted the naming of a major boulevard in Lokoja after Audu by Governor Ododo and the unveiling of the Prince Abubakar Audu Leadership Foundation by the representative of President Tinubu at the anniversary events.

The stakeholders called for the foundation to operate as a nationwide, non-partisan platform for preserving Audu’s memory and promoting his leadership philosophy.

They argued that restricting his legacy to one election cycle or the final period of his political career would amount to historical injustice.

“Prince Audu belonged to multiple eras of Nigeria’s democratic development, from his early public service to his trailblazing leadership as the first and second civilian executive governor.

He must be remembered as a statesman,” they said.

In their resolutions, the stakeholders pledged to unify APC grassroots structures across the nine local government areas of Kogi East behind Tinubu and all APC legislative candidates in the 2027 elections.

They also committed themselves to dialogue with political leaders in Kogi Central and Kogi West, stressing that such engagement must be conducted on mutually acceptable and equitable terms.

The stakeholders further resolved to align with the state government to promote peace, inclusivity and accelerated development across Kogi East.

They called on party leaders, youth leaders, elders and other members of the late Audu’s political family to put past grievances aside and work towards a united political front.

“Our goal is to reintegrate Kogi East into the mainstream of politics in Kogi State and the nation on terms that will assure us of our deserved share of development,” they declared.

World.title: Idris Deserves Second Term, Says Zuru, Urges Voters To Support Gov For Continuity
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent

The Special Adviser to the Kebbi State Governor on Media Strategy and Communication, Abdullahi Zuru, has declared that Governor Nasir Idris has performed credibly well and deserves to be re-elected for a second term in 2027.

Zuru made the declaration yesterday while responding to questions from journalists who paid him a courtesy visit. He said the assessment was based on the governor’s record of delivery across key sectors since assuming office in 2023.

“Since the creation of Kebbi State, we have never had it this good,” Zuru said. “The governor has touched every sector and the impact is visible to the people.”

According to him, the Idris administration has prioritised the economy, infrastructural development, education, health, workers’ welfare, and human capital development. He noted that the interventions were designed to directly improve the lives of ordinary citizens.

On infrastructure, the media aide said the government has embarked on road projects, urban renewal, and rural development programmes aimed at opening up communities and boosting commerce across the 21 local government areas of the state.

“In education and health, we have seen massive investments in schools, primary healthcare centres, and the welfare of teachers and health workers,” he added. “Workers’ salaries are paid as and when due, and their welfare is receiving serious attention.”

Zuru further stated that the governor’s approach to governance has restored public confidence in government. He said the administration runs an open-door policy that allows citizens to feel the presence of government at all levels.

Calling on voters in the state, he urged them to rally behind the governor ahead of the next election. “I encourage the good people of Kebbi State to support Governor Nasir Idris and ensure he returns for a second term so that the good work can continue,” he said.

The Special Adviser also took a swipe at some politicians in the state, saying they lacked the pedigree to challenge the governor’s record.

“Some of them have held positions at state and federal levels before, yet they have no track record to show for it,” Zuru stated. “Leadership is about results, and the results are there for everyone to see.”

He noted that with the current momentum, Kebbi is on the path of sustainable development, and continuity under Governor Idris remains the best option for the people of the state.

World.title: Beyond Interest: The Alternative Bank Charts New Path for Wealth Creation
World.content:
Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

The Alternative Bank has concluded plans to chart a new course for capital allocation in Nigeria as it hosted investors, policymakers and business leaders in Lagos under the theme, ‘Beyond Interest: Capital, Innovation, and the Future of Wealth’.

The event focused on non-interest finance and the need to deploy patient capital into the country’s productive sectors rather than extractive models that only generate short-term gains.

Opening the forum, Muhtar Bakare, Chairman of The Alternative Bank, said the economy must move away from capital that merely harvests value.

“Extractive capital treats the economy chiefly as a place from which value is harvested. It may reward its owner, but it rarely leaves the economy stronger. Productive capital invests in enterprises, assets and systems that grow over time. It creates income for workers, demand for suppliers, revenue for governments and sustainable returns for investors,” Bakare stated.

Delivering the keynote on behalf of Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, the Commissioner for Finance, Abayomi Oluyomi, said government has a critical role in de-risking investment through infrastructure and credible policy.

He cited the Blue and Red Line rail projects as examples of public investment expanding markets and reducing business costs.

“The future of finance will belong to capital that is more purposeful, innovative and closely connected to productive economic activity.

“The future of development finance will increasingly draw on instruments including green bonds, sukuk and other ethical and non-interest structures that connect capital to real assets, productive activity and measurable outcomes. Investors do not invest in government promises. They invest in credible systems,” he said.

Also speaking, former Lagos State Governor and former Minister of Works and Housing, Babatunde Raji Fashola, urged financial institutions to prioritise investments tied to tangible assets and community well-being over those chasing immediate profits, noting that such investments deliver more lasting social and economic returns.

The forum featured expert briefings from Abubakar Suleiman, Board Member of Sterling Financial Holdings and a promoter of non-interest banking in Nigeria; Dr. Stanley Jacob, Group Chief, Innovation and Technology at Meristem; and Ajibola Tobi-Osho, Executive Director of Tugrande Alliance Limited.

Their presentations covered the business case for ethical capital, the potential of pan-African payment systems and asset tokenisation, and Nigeria’s macroeconomic outlook.

The discussions reinforced The Alternative Bank’s position that building a resilient Nigerian economy requires shared-risk, non-interest financial structures that give investors confidence and ensure investments create cross-generational value.

The bank said it will continue to champion financial models that link capital directly to real assets and productive activity as part of its mandate to drive inclusive and sustainable wealth creation.

World.title: Abia Leadership Academy, Strategic Institution For Training Future Leaders, Says Gov
World.content:
Boniface Okoro in Umuahia

Abia State Governor, Dr. Alex Otti, says the Abia State Leadership Academy was established as a strategic institution where ethics, values, and practical leadership skills would be instilled in Abia youths.

He said the essence was to catch them young, adding “we are committed to getting it right with the younger generation. Otherwise, our wider development efforts will be in jeopardy.”

Governor Otti, represented by his Deputy, Engr. Ikechukwu Emetu, spoke while declaring open the 2026 Youth Leadership Bootcamp of the Abia State Leadership Academy. The batch has 1, 000 participants selected from 7, 000 applicants. The training holds every long vacation at Government College, Umuahia, since the Otti administration came to power.

The governor reaffirmed his commitment to developing young Abians as future leaders of the state and nation and charged the participants to learn with humility and participate actively in the programme.

“This year’s programme is particularly significant, with 1,000 participants selected from more than 7,000 applicants. That response tells us our young people are hungry for genuine transformation—and they trust this administration to deliver it.

“For 2026, we’ve partnered with the Enterprise Development Centre of Pan-Atlantic University—a global-standard institution with ties to the World Bank, Goldman Sachs, and MasterCard.

“To our young participants, your selection is only the beginning. I urge you to learn with humility, participate actively, build meaningful relationships and, most importantly, use what you learn to positively influence your schools, communities and State,” the Governor said.

Earlier, the facilitator of the programme and Chairman of Abia State Civil Service Commission, Pastor Mrs. Eno Jerry –Eze, represented by Rev. Mrs. Ifeoma Agu, said that the programme was an opportunity to for the youths to imbibe the ideals of civic responsibility and urged the participants to be determined to use the lessons of the bootcamp to better their lives as well as bring about the change they crave for.

Mrs. Jerry-Eze thanked the governor for placing the youths in the leadership map in Nigeria and for leaving a legacy that assures that the leadership he has introduced would be sustained.

Delivering a lecture on the theme of the training: ‘The Demands of Stewardship’, the Chief of Staff to the Governor, Pastor Caleb Ajagba, noted that the governor was investing in the lives of the teenagers and young leaders of the state through the academy.

Pastor Ajagba, while describing the initiative as a strategic investment in the future of the state and a lasting legacy that will shape the character, mindset and leadership capacity of generations yet unborn, disclosed that by intentionally preparing young people for responsible leadership, Governor Otti was laying a firm foundation for sustainable development and ensuring that the ideals of integrity, innovation and public service remain deeply rooted in Abia’s future.

He added that it was an honour for all those invited to share their perspectives in the noble vision of raising a generation of principled, disciplined and transformational leaders through the academy and applauded the exemplary life of vision, focus, sacrifice, discipline, competence, integrity of Governor Otti and assuring of the unwavering commitment of the Governor to good governance and purposeful leadership.

Also speaking on behalf of the Executive Director of the development partner – the Enterprise Development Centre (EDC), Pan-Athlantic University, Dr. Uche Egbuna, said the future of every society depends on the quality of leaders it intentionally develops, adding that leadership was about responsibility, integrity and service.

Dr. Egbuna stated that the boot camp was built on four key pillars: leadership and service, enterprise, impact and innovation, and encouraged participants to strive for meaningful impact by becoming problem-solvers and change-makers.

He described the partnership with the Abia State Leadership Academy as a shared commitment to developing ethical leaders, resilient entrepreneurs and innovative young people who will contribute to economic growth and social transformation.

President of Abia State Leadership Academy, Prof. Kenneth Kalu, disclosed that 7052 persons applied for the programme and about 1000 were qualified after the rigorous processes of selection.

Prof. Kalu enjoined the participants to remember that they were expected “to think, reflect and become” future leaders, emphasising that what was more important was not that they participated in the programme but what they become from the programme.

Responding on behalf of the participants, Chukwuemerie Obiorah and Treasure Ogbonna thanked the governor for the opportunity given them to become transformational leaders, assuring that they would not disappoint but make good use of the bootcamp to better citizens in the society.

The opening ceremony of the bootcamp being coordinated by the Programme Manager, Abia State Leadership Academy and Senior Special Assistant to the Governor on Public Communication, Mr. Dodoh Okafor, was graced by Secretary to the State Government, Dr. Emmanuel Meribeole; Commissioner for Tertiary Education, Prof. Uche Emeh Uche; Principal Secretary and Chief Strategist Officer of the state, Mr. Chinenye Mba-Uzoukwu, among other government officials.

World.title: Gov Yahaya Receives Report of Taskforce Committee on Reforms, Revitalisation of Basic, Technical Education
World.content:
Segun Awofadeji in Gombe

Gombe State Governor, Alhaji Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, yesterday received the report of the Taskforce Committee on the Reforms and Revitalisation of Basic and Technical Education in the state, describing it as a critical blueprint for transforming the education sector.

The governor assured that his administration would immediately commence the implementation of the committee’s recommendations as part of its commitment to repositioning basic and technical education for greater efficiency, improved learning outcomes and the development of a skilled, future-ready workforce.

He stated this while receiving the report presented by a member of the committee and foremost educationist, Mr. Mataimaki Tom Maiyashi, alongside the Commissioner of Education, Associate Professor Aishatu Umar Maigari who chaired the Taskforce.

Governor Yahaya stated that his administration remains resolute in its commitment to strengthening the education sector through bold policy decisions and structural reforms that will ensure sustainable development in line with the state’s 10-year development agenda (DEVAGOM).

“On the report, I want to assure you that we are not going to abandon this document. We shall study it immediately and begin implementation of the recommendations,” the governor said.

He disclosed that his administration has already commenced far-reaching structural adjustments in the education sector, citing the recent merger of the Ministry of Higher Education with the Ministry of Education into a single ministry as one of the first major reform initiatives.

“We will do structural adjustments in the education sector. I can even say that we have started because I have now merged the Ministry of Higher Education and the Ministry of Education to become one ministry, which is what is obtainable even at the federal level. This will strengthen coordination, improve policy implementation and enhance service delivery across all levels of education,” he stated.

Reflecting on the progress recorded since assuming office in 2019, Yahaya noted that his administration inherited an education sector confronted by numerous challenges but has, through sustained strategic interventions, recorded remarkable achievements in infrastructure, teacher development, school enrolment, access to quality education and institutional reforms.

“We knew how we met this sector when we came into office in 2019, and we thank God that we have been able to achieve so much. I want to reiterate the pledge I made that we will leave Gombe better than we met it in the education sector. That commitment remains unwavering, and we shall continue to invest in reforms that will guarantee quality education for our children and future generations,” the governor stated.

Speaking on behalf of the committee, foremost educationist and former Commissioner for Education in Kaduna State, Mr. Maiyashi, commended Governor Yahaya for his visionary leadership and foresight in establishing the taskforce.

He observed that the governor’s investments and numerous achievements in the education sector have already laid a strong foundation for sustainable development.

He described the committee’s report as an honest reflection of the realities confronting basic and technical education in Gombe State.

Maiyashi assured the governor that the recommendations are practical, realistic and fully implementable, urging him to earnestly begin the implementation of what the document recommends.

He expressed confidence that the faithful implementation of the recommendations would significantly transform the state’s education system and position Gombe as a model for educational excellence.

Earlier, the Commissioner for Education, Prof. Maigari, who chaired the Taskforce, explained that the committee was inaugurated in November 2025 with the mandate to critically assess the state of basic and technical education in Gombe State, develop actionable strategies, recommend practical reforms capable of restoring the lost glory of the state’s schools, and address all issues incidental to its assignment.

According to her, the committee’s work focused on key thematic areas including teacher-related challenges, infrastructure deficits, governance and administration, student welfare and learning conditions, as well as security and community-related issues affecting schools.

She explained that the findings from these assessments formed the basis of the committee’s recommendations, which were carefully packaged into eight priority reform clusters requiring immediate government intervention to accelerate improvements in the education sector.

The commissioner expressed appreciation to Governor Inuwa Yahaya for demonstrating exceptional political will and commitment to education by constituting a high-powered committee of renowned professionals whose wealth of experience enriched the quality of the report.

The Taskforce Committee comprised eminent education experts and policymakers, including Prof. Maigari, the Gombe State Commissioner for Education; Dr. Yakubu, former Executive Secretary of the National Board for Technical Education (NBTE); Dr. Hamid Bobboyi, former Executive Secretary of the Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC); Mr. Maiyashi, education consultant and former Commissioner for Education in Kaduna State; Dr. Sadiq Gombe, and also the Executive Chairman of the State Universal Basic Education Board (SUBEB); and the Permanent Secretary, Special Services and Political (SS & POL), Government House, Gombe.

World.title: Just In: DSS Arrests Three More Suspects Over Kidnap of Nasarawa Varsity Professor
World.content:
Operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS) have arrested three more suspects linked to the kidnapping of the Dean of Agriculture at Nasarawa State University, Professor Samuel Avengbe Okunsebor.

The suspects were arrested on Friday night at a local brothel along the Mararraban Akunza axis of the Lafia–Makurdi highway.

A security source disclosed that the three suspects were members of the kidnapping gang responsible for the abduction of the university don.

Professor Okunsebor was kidnapped by gunmen in the early hours of Wednesday, July 15, 2026, at Mile Uku, a border community between Lafia and Nasarawa-Eggon Local Government Areas of Nasarawa State.

He was rescued two days later by DSS operatives. Two suspects, including a woman, were also arrested in connection with the incident at the time.

According to a security source, the newly arrested suspects were identified as 25-year-old Yakubu Abubakar, also known as Black or Starboy, a member of the Doemak tribe in Plateau State; 37-year-old Usman Abubakar Mairiga; and 27-year-old Sale Babauro Abubakar.

The source said Mairiga is Hausa, while Sale Babauro Abubakar is Fulani.

The three suspects are currently being held at the DSS State Command for further investigation.

The source added that their continued detention followed a warrant obtained from a magistrate’s court.

The latest arrests bring to five the number of suspects reportedly apprehended in connection with the kidnapping of Professor Okunsebor. Investigations into the incident are ongoing.

World.title: St Stithians ‘murder-suicide’: GBV org points to ‘toxic masculinity, violence’
World.content:
An anti-gender-based violence (GBV) organisation has called on young men, particularly teenagers, to engage in dialogue about intimate partner violence, on the backdrop of the alleged murder-suicide involving St Stithian teens, Cameron Waldeck-Cooks and Ethan Coetzee.

The bodies of the rumoured couple were discovered at a Sabie lodge on Monday, 3 August.

According to a preliminary forensic report, 17-year-old Cameron is believed to have been strangled, while 19-year-old Ethan reportedly took his own life.



GBV ORG ON ST STITHIAN ‘MURDER-SUICIDE’

In a lengthy statement, Not In My Name anti-GBV activist Lesego Mahlangu addressed the deaths of St Stithian teens, Cameron Waldeck-Cooks and Ethan Coetzee.

Mahlangu pointed to police initial findings that the deaths were attributed to a murder-suicide, possibly as a result of a romantic relationship between the teens.

She said: “We are called to reflect more deeply on the nature of intimate partner and close relationships, which are often shaped by toxic masculinity and harmful patriarchal norms. These are social conditions that not only place women and partners at risk; they dehumanise men by discouraging vulnerability, emotional expression, and healthy ways of responding to conflict, rejection, and emotional distress. 

“While women continue to bear the greatest burden of this violence, meaningful prevention requires us to engage men and boys intentionally. We must demand spaces where they are not only spoken to, but where they are encouraged to speak openly about masculinity, emotional well-being, accountability, and violence.

“Challenging toxic patriarchal structures is not simply about protecting women; it is equally about preventing young men from becoming both perpetrators and victims of the same destructive system.

The GBV org went on to claim that the St Stithians double tragedy was an example that “violence knows no racial boundaries”.



She continued: “As we mourn and stand in solidarity with the Waldeck-Cooks family, we also extend our sympathies to the Coetzee family, who are mourning the loss of a young man believed to have been caught in the same cycle of toxic masculinity and violence that continues to devastate families and communities across South Africa.”

‘DOMESTIC VIOLENCE IN TEEN RELATIONSHIPS’

Former DA MP Phumzile van Damme has shared similar sentiments about the St Stithian teens whose lives were cut short.

She shared in a tweet: “We need to start talking about domestic violence in teenage relationships. Too often, the conversation, campaigns and support services are framed around adult couples, when the same patterns can begin long before the age of 18.



“If we want to prevent domestic abuse rather than simply respond to it, we need to recognise it earlier, talk about it openly, and ensure young people know what healthy relationships look like.”

She added, “I know someone will say, ‘No dating before 18 for my kids’. My baby love, they’ll probably date anyway. The only difference is they’ll do it behind your back. And you’ll miss the opportunity to share your experience, spot red flags, and be the person they turn to when something doesn’t feel right.

“Far better to know who they’re dating, get a sense of the relationship yourself, and create an environment where they can talk to you openly without fear. You can’t prevent every tragedy. But where there’s an opportunity to reduce the risk, don’t bury your head in the sand. Teenagers will be teenagers. Our jobs as adults is to make sure they don’t have to navigate inevitable relationships alone.

World.title: ‘A little sad’: Layla Kolbe questions SA All Blacks supporters
World.content:
Layla Kolbe has questioned South Africans who support the All Blacks. Images via Instagram

Layla Kolbe, the wife of Springbok and Stormers player Cheslin Kolbe, has posted a cryptic message criticising South Africans who continue to support the All Blacks.

This comes as the New Zealand rugby team have kicked off their Greatest Rivalry series in South Africa this weekend.

On Friday, the ABs beat the Stormers 38-21 at the DHL Stadium in Cape Town.



LAYLA KOLBE CRITICISES SOUTH AFRICAN ALL BLACKS SUPPORTERS

On her Instagram Stories, Layla Kolbe reposted a post from someone who called out South Africans who chose to support the All Blacks over the Springboks or any South African club.

The post read: “Something is bothering me massively is the amount of All Black supporters that still walk among us after so many years of work being done by SA rugby to make the sport in this country so representative of how diverse we all are.

“I just am a little sad at how many people can’t seem to [support] teams that actually represent them properly for the first time in more than 30 years. The sport code doing the most to get this right in OUR country”.



Like Layla, Cheslin has also referred to the All Blacks’ Western Cape supporters.

A year after winning the 2023 Rugby World Cup trophy, the winger stated that he had hoped the Springboks would “win over more support”.

He said: “The only thing we can do more is to win, and hopefully earn a bit more respect here. Yes, the All Blacks do have a good support base in Cape Town, but I’m sure the majority of supporters will be cheering on the Springboks.”



Outside New Zealand, the All Blacks have the strongest support in South Africa, particularly among the coloured community in the Western Cape. For many, the support is deep-rooted in Apartheid, when New Zealand stood with non-white players who were sidelined from joining the Springboks.

World.title: Pitso Back! SAFA set to announce Mosimane as new Bafana coach next week
World.content:
Pitso Mosimane is set to make a sensational return to Bafana Bafana after the SAFA National Executive Committee (NEC) approved his appointment as the new head coach.

The South African Football Association (SAFA) held an Extraordinary NEC Meeting at SAFA House on Saturday, where members backed Mosimane to take over from Hugo Broos.

Broos stepped down from his position earlier this week after guiding Bafana Bafana through an historic period, including their return to the FIFA World Cup.



Pitso Mosimane to take over Bafana once again

While Mosimane’s appointment has been approved, SAFA says there are still a few matters to be finalised before the former Mamelodi Sundowns coach is officially unveiled.

“The NEC has approved the appointment of coach Pitso to Bafana Bafana, but we still need to tie up some loose ends. We will make a formal announcement of the coach next week,” SAFA president Dr Danny Jordaan said following Saturday’s meeting.

Mosimane’s return would mark a new chapter for the 61-year-old, who previously led Bafana Bafana between 2010 and 2012.



The former Sundowns mentor has also enjoyed considerable success at club level, most notably guiding the Tshwane giants to domestic dominance and continental glory before taking charge of Egyptian giants Al Ahly.

Bafana Bafana, meanwhile, are coming off an historic FIFA World Cup campaign.

The national team qualified for the tournament for the first time in 24 years and went on to reach the knockout stages for the first time in their history.



Their memorable campaign included a 1-0 victory over South Korea in Monterrey, Mexico, with Thapelo Maseko scoring the only goal of the match.

Attention now turns to the next chapter under Mosimane, with SAFA expected to formally confirm his appointment as Bafana head coach next week.

The NEC meeting also covered preparations for SAFA’s Elective Congress, which is scheduled to take place on 12 September 2026.



Nominations for the various positions to be contested at the congress were handed over to the Governance Committee this week.

World.title: Pitso Mosimane named as new Bafana coach
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Pitso Mosimane is set for a return to the Bafana Bafana dugout.

The South African Football Association has approved his appointment as the new national team coach following the departure of Hugo Broos.

The decision was ratified at a Safa National Executive Committee meeting, with members backing Mosimane to take charge of the side that recently made history at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

South Africa reached the knockout rounds round for the first time, highlighted by a memorable victory over South Korea.

While SAFA said a few administrative details still need to be finalised, an official announcement is expected next week.

Mosimane was previously in charge of Bafana in a caretaker capacity in 2007 and from 2010 to 2012.

World.title: RFA flags enforcement gaps in freight sector
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Road Freight Association CEO Gavin Kelly said stronger enforcement is crucial to ease tensions over foreign driver employment in South Africa’s freight sector.

With truck driver associations threatening a freight shutdown, Kelly argued the issue begins with how companies are registered and monitored.

“We are not taking the right steps when we initially register companies. When we register companies, do we ask those companies who are their employees, before we allow the company to be registered?

“We need to ask questions like are you registered with the council that is applicable to your sector of business so that we have inspectors going to all the companies that are active in that sector.

“What happens now is that inspectors to companies they are aware of and that’s the real reason we have been struggling with this. Secondly, the deterrent has to meet this problem. It doesn’t help if you get rid of these foreign nationals and they reappear or the company just employs other foreigners because that destroys the operation of the sector in totality," Kelly said.

World.title: Coalition decisions will be crucial - Mnguni
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The race is on for political parties to garner votes ahead of the November local government elections.

But the reality is many municipalities may end up with coalition governments.

Rise Mzansi said fixing Johannesburg starts with principled leadership, transparent coalition agreements and no deals with parties tainted by criminality.

City of Johannesburg mayoral candidate Lukhona Mnguni said they work based on principles and coalition agreements ought to be signed.

“I do think that people are exceedingly disappointed in how the ANC is governing this city.

The ANC will probably have a huge task to justify why it must be included in a coalition. But those are conversations that become more material when you see the actual results.

“But I think starting with principles, quality of leadership, coalition agreements, and ensuring that residents have a much more transparent path to coalition formation than we have had previously,” Mnguni said.

World.title: Recovering Marchand to skip medleys at European swim champs
World.content:
PARIS - Swimming star Leon Marchand has cut back on the events he will compete in at the European championships starting Monday because of a lingering thigh injury.

The French federation confirmed Saturday that Marchand will not compete in the 200m and 400m individual medley events in Paris.

The Frenchman had already ruled out the 200m breaststroke but remains entered in the 200m butterfly and 400m freestyle that place less strain on the adductor muscles.

He may also participate in one or two relays with the French team.

"The injury is healing well, and recovery is largely complete. However, since competing in the 200m and 400m individual medley carries a non-negligible risk of recurrence, and to safeguard the remainder of the competition, the decision was made not to enter these races," explained team doctor Sebastien Le Garrec.

The four-time Olympic champion injured his adductor during the 200m breaststroke heats at the French championships in June, subsequently withdrawing from the rest of the competition.

He suffered a setback during a training session in Marseille three weeks later.

Earlier this month, he had confirmed his participation in the European championships, though he was doubtful regarding the 400m individual medley.

Ultimately, he decided to withdraw from the shorter distance as well as a precautionary measure.

The withdrawal from his two signature events is a major setback for the 24-year-old, who had made these championships the primary goal of his season.

He had also stated he wanted to break his own world record in the 400m individual medley this season.

"It's something I want to do in the near future, and I imagine doing it in Paris at the European championships would be great," he had said.

World.title: MotoGP leader Martin speeds to British Grand Prix pole
World.content:
LONDON - MotoGP world championship leader Jorge Martin set a new lap record on his way to pole position for both Saturday's sprint race and Sunday's British Grand Prix.

Spanish rider Martin was not only the fastest in Saturday's midday qualifying session in perfect conditions at the Silverstone track, but also broke the all-time lap record with a time of 1min 56.160sec.

It was the second time in two days that the record fell after Martin's Aprilia teammate Marco Bezzecchi blitzed to 1min 56.280sec in practice on Friday despite fracturing a collarbone at the German MotoGP last time out.

Italian Bezzecchi will start fifth on the grid for Saturday's 10-lap sprint race and Sunday's 20-lap Grand Prix.

Behind Martin are compatriot Raul Fernandez, riding another Aprilia for the Trackhouse team, just 0.021sec behind, followed by Japan's Ai Ogura and Italian Fabio Di Giannantonio.

The Marquez brothers, Marc and Alex, round out the top seven.

Marc Marquez revived his title defence by winning in Germany and is only 18 points behind Martin in the standings, and four points adrift of second-placed Ogura.

The top five in the championship race, with Bezzecchi in fourth and Di Giannantonio fifth, are separated by just 24 points.

The sprint race takes place at 1500 GMT.

World.title: Zwakele Mncwango named ActionSA’s eThekwini mayoral candidate
World.content:
KWAMASHU - ActionSA President Herman Mashaba pledges consistency as he urges eThekwini residents to back the party in November’s local government elections.

He told voters they can expect the same governance ActionSA delivers in Tshwane.

He spoke in KwaZulu-Natal as ActionSA unveiled its mayoral candidates.

"We are appealing to people of eThekwini, if they want to see the kind of governance that we are experiencing in the City of Tshwane under Dr. Nasipi Moya, that's what they will get,” Mashaba said.

ActionSA has positioned itself as the alternative to corruption, political patronage and unfulfilled promises.

Tshwane Mayor Nasiphi Moya said ActionSA is ready to govern eThekwini Municipality.

The party has announced its mayoral candidates for eThekwini, KwaDukuza, and Newcastle ahead of the local government elections.

“Today is about declaring that ACTIONSA is ready to govern,” she said.

Mashaba named Zwakele Mncwango as the party’s mayoral candidate in eThekwini.

Mncwango will spearhead ActionSA’s campaign in the metro ahead of November’s elections.

The party joins a crowded field as parties intensify their campaigns for eThekwini.

World.title: POPCRU demands firm response to Reiger Park cop killers
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Police and Prisons Civil Rights Union (POPCRU) has the brutal killing of two members of the South African Police Service’s Anti-Gang Unit in Reiger Park, Ekurhuleni, on Friday.

Reports indicate that Two civilians were Killed. The two officers, who were part of a crime-prevention operation, heard the gunfire and moved towards the source, where they were ambushed.

In a statement, POPCRU said an attack on a police officer is an attack on the authority of the democratic state and on the safety of every South African.

“Criminals cannot be allowed to reach a point where they believe they can ambush and kill police officers with impunity. When those tasked with protecting communities are hunted down while performing their duties, society must recognise that a dangerous line has been crossed,” the statement reads in part.

POPCRU said killing of the officers could not become another statistic followed by expressions of outrage before the country simply moves on.

“Government and SAPS management must confront police killings as a national priority. The Anti-Gang Unit operates on some of the most dangerous fronts in the battle against organised and violent crime.

“Its members confront criminal networks that terrorise communities and undermine the rule of law. Sending officers into these environments without sufficient intelligence, resources and operational support places their lives at unacceptable risk.”

The union has also urged community members to work with the authorities by providing information.

“Criminals survive when communities are intimidated into silence. They must find no sanctuary in our communities.”

World.title: Alleged CIT robbers killed in shootout with KZN police
World.content:
DURBAN - Three suspects who were wanted for various violent crimes in KwaZulu-Natal were in a shootout with police in Kranskop in the early hours of Saturday morning.

KwaZulu-Natal police spokesperson Colonel Robert Netshiunda said police acted on intelligence which uncovered the whereabout of the suspects and when they approached a residence at Mambulu area.

“A shootout ensued between police and an unknown number of suspects. Three suspects were shot and fatally wounded during the shootout and they were found in possession of firearms.

“The suspects are linked to a CIT robbery which happened in the Kranskop CBD on 13 April 2026 where suspects also fired shots at a police station,” he said.

One of the suspects was injured during the explosion of the CIT vehicle and was found dead inside an abandoned vehicle in Nkandla a day after the CIT robbery.

Netshiunda said a search is ongoing for more suspects who are believed to have evaded arrest and are armed, at least with a rifle.

World.title: Charlene Ruto's Koito lights up Kilgoris
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto’s daughter, Charlene Ruto, is engaged to Tanzanian entrepreneur Isaiah Yunge.

The drums rolled, traditional songs filled the air and dancers swayed in colourful rhythm as Kilgoris was transformed into a spectacular theatre of love, culture, wealth and political power.

At the expansive Intonna Heritage Farm in Naserian Village, President William Ruto’s daughter, Charlene Chelagat Ruto, took a major traditional step towards marriage as the First Family hosted her Koito ak Chaik—a colourful Kalenjin engagement and farewell ceremony.

For hours, the skies above Kilgoris were punctuated by helicopters ferrying distinguished guests to the President’s family property, while luxury vehicles streamed through the gates carrying politicians, government officials, business personalities, relatives and friends.

On the ground, the mood was unmistakably festive. Traditional songs echoed across the expansive farm as dancers moved to the rhythm, colourful attire transformed the venue into a sea of elegance and culture, and guests embraced the joy of a ceremony that combined an ancient African tradition with the unmistakable grandeur of Kenya’s First Family.

It was romance wrapped in tradition—and tradition presented on a spectacular scale.

The guest list read almost like a roll call of Kenya’s political establishment. Leaving the Narok delegation was Governor Patrick Ole Ntutu, who joined Kilgoris MP Julius Sunkuli and former Narok Governor Samuel Tunai in celebrating the First Family on the special occasion.

The ceremony also brought together elected leaders from across Narok County, creating an impressive gathering of the county’s political establishment at the heart of Trans Mara.

From governors and Senators to MPs, the event brought together leaders from across the country. Top government officials and senior executives too came dressed for the ceremony

The fashion became part of the spectacle. Brown, maroon and other earthy tones dominated the scene, blending effortlessly with the traditional African setting. It was a celebration in which political leaders seemed determined to make an entrance as memorable as the occasion itself.

But beyond the political faces and the luxury was the heartbeat of the ceremony—culture. Traditional songs rang across the farm. Dancers moved with energy and precision, their performances adding colour and rhythm to a celebration centred on family and love.

The atmosphere shifted between moments of emotion and bursts of exuberance as relatives, friends and guests celebrated Charlene’s transition into a new stage of life.

The contrast was striking. Modern wealth arrived by helicopter, while ancient traditions were celebrated through song and dance. Luxury vehicles lined up outside as cultural performers entertained guests inside. Political heavyweights mingled with family elders.

Politicians arrive for Charlene Ruto's Koito in Kilgoris. [UGC]

And amid the glamour, the central message remained simple: Charlene and her fiancé, Isaiah Yunge, had brought together not just two families but two countries.

Yunge is a Tanzanian technology entrepreneur and digital innovation enthusiast associated with Goodsam Technologies and is a co-founder of Smart Kaya LLC, a smart-home technology venture.

He has been recognised among Forbes Africa’s 30 Under 30 and received the Queen’s Young Leaders Award in 2018. His interest in technology reportedly began at an early age. At 17, he was selected as a UNICEF Africa Youth Ambassador and participated in international advocacy around children's rights.

He later pursued training in sustainable business models through the Swedish Institute, studied Leading Change at Cambridge University and became an alumnus of the Harvard Ministerial Leadership Program.

For all its glamour, the heart of the celebration remained the centuries-old tradition of Koito. Among the Kalenjin, it is a significant engagement ceremony through which the families of the bride and groom formally meet, bless the relationship, exchange gifts and discuss dowry arrangements.

It is a moment when families begin the process of becoming one.
