A deadly Russian strike on the Kyiv region that killed a child has renewed grief and calls for more air defences, while Germany’s RWE abandoned US wind projects in a bruising trade retreat. Amid it all, street parades, festivals and cycling races are offering brief, sweaty moments of escape from the strain.

Spain – Internal Border Controls Imposed on Italy

Madrid acts after Rome refuses to lift its own checks

Spain began temporary passport, nationality and visa checks on all travellers arriving from Italy at midnight on Saturday. Italy moved first, reimposing checks on air and sea arrivals from Spain after the Ceuta breach, so travellers are now checked in both directions.

Madrid linked the controls to Rome’s refusal to lift its own, which run to 31 August; the Spanish measures are set to run until 7 September 2026. One practical trap: Italian paper identity cards stopped being valid travel documents on 3 August, so only an electronic CIE or a passport will do.

A frustrated and defensive mood takes hold

Madrid’s unilateral move signals deep frustration with the lack of a coordinated European response to the Ceuta crisis.

The sudden checks have left Italy diplomatically isolated within the Mediterranean neighbourhood, compounding a sense of disunity at a time when solidarity is badly needed.

Bulgaria – Drone Explosion Near Trans-Balkan Gas Pipeline

Blast near strategic energy link raises immediate alarm

A drone crossed from Romania at around 8:10 a.m. on Saturday and exploded in a sunflower field about 100 metres inside Bulgaria, near the former Kardam checkpoint and roughly a kilometre from a compressor station on the Trans-Balkan gas pipeline, Prime Minister Rumen Radev said.

Bulgaria’s defence ministry made a preliminary assessment that it was most likely a Ukrainian Maya decoy drone, with no indication the country was a deliberate target. That has not stopped the incident from shaking public confidence in territorial security.

Fresh spillover fears grip NATO’s eastern flank

The incident raised concerns about spillover from the war into NATO territory, though on Sofia’s own reading this was drift rather than attack.

For ordinary Bulgarians, the proximity of the explosion to critical energy links has turned distant headlines into a deeply personal security worry.

Sofia’s preliminary assessment is that the drone was a stray Ukrainian decoy rather than a deliberate strike.

Germany – Unidentified Drones at Bundeswehr Base

Mechernich sighting adds to pattern of airspace incidents

Six unidentified drones were observed over the Bundeswehr logistics complex at Mechernich, North Rhine-Westphalia, late on Thursday, a spokesperson for the armed forces confirmed. The site holds an underground weapons and spares depot and a Patriot repair facility; military police watched the aircraft from about 40 metres.

An early assessment points to a Fly-380 vertical take-off drone. State police, the Military Counterintelligence Service and Berlin’s Joint Drone Defence Centre are all investigating, in what is becoming a pattern of incursions across the continent.

A vigilant and economically bruised nation

The intrusion at a Bundeswehr installation stokes security worries at home, while RWE’s retreat from US offshore wind projects signals the rising cost of transatlantic trade friction.

Germany finds itself navigating both a military unease and an economic hit from shifting American policy, leaving the public feeling doubly exposed.

Ukraine – Major Russian Strike on Ukrnafta Production Facilities

One of the largest recent attacks on energy infrastructure

Russia damaged seven Ukrnafta oil and gas production facilities overnight into Friday, one of the largest attacks on the company to date, according to Naftogaz. Several sites suspended operations. In all, 287 Naftogaz-group facilities have been hit so far in 2026, already more than in the whole of 2025.

The strike is part of Moscow’s ongoing campaign to degrade Ukrainian energy capacity, deepening the country’s hardship as it braces for another winter.

Ukraine – Overnight Strikes Kill Civilians in Kyiv Region

Four dead, including a three-year-old child, in latest barrage

Russian strikes overnight into Saturday killed four people. A three-year-old boy and his grandparents died in a drone attack on Puhivka, in the Brovary district about 30 kilometres from Kyiv, and one person was killed in the capital in a strike involving six ballistic missiles.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy responded by calling for stronger international sanctions on Moscow and more air defence systems for Ukraine, capturing a mood of grieving defiance.

Germany – RWE Abandons US Offshore Wind Projects

A US$1.22 billion settlement reshapes transatlantic investment

German energy giant RWE is abandoning several planned US offshore wind projects under a US$1.22 billion settlement with the US Department of the Interior, which pays RWE in return for the company relinquishing leases off New York, California and Louisiana.

RWE says it has invested more than US$1 billion and sees no permitting path, and will redirect the money into US LNG and gas-fired generation. It is the fifth such settlement, with more than US$3.9 billion committed across all five, and several states are suing to block them.

Italy – Southern Europe Endures Severe Heatwave

Major cities swelter under highest heat alert

Italy’s health ministry put all 27 monitored cities on red alert on Friday, the first time the entire network has been at maximum simultaneously, with maximum temperatures near 40°C.

Spain also maintained yellow and orange heat warnings across much of the country on both Friday and Saturday, adding physical exhaustion to the region’s already strained mood.

Switzerland – Zurich Street Parade Draws Large Crowds

Joy and crowds under ongoing heat conditions

The annual Zurich Street Parade, one of Europe’s largest techno and dance music events, took place on Saturday, drawing hundreds of thousands of revellers.

The party atmosphere brought a lighter counterpoint to the week’s grim headlines, though the intense heat kept the mood watchful.

Austria – Shutdown Festival at Zwentendorf Nuclear Site

Electronic music at a plant that never switched on

The Shutdown Festival, an electronic music event held at the Zwentendorf nuclear power plant — built but never commissioned, and never loaded with fuel — opened on 8 August 2026.

The unique venue drew music fans seeking a festive escape, providing a small but welcome breather from Europe’s heavier news cycle.

Germany – Augsburg Peace Festival Observed

A unique local legal holiday in Bavaria

The Augsburger Hohes Friedensfest, a unique local legal holiday observed only in Augsburg, Germany, was marked on Saturday.

The quiet observance stood in gentle contrast to the security alerts and military tensions rippling across the rest of the country.

Spain and Poland – Summer Cycling Races Continue

Vuelta a Burgos Stage 5 and Tour de Pologne Stage 6

Stage 5 of the Vuelta a Burgos professional cycling race took place in Spain on Saturday, while Stage 6 of the Tour de Pologne was held in Poland.

The races offered moments of sporting rhythm and normalcy amid a continent otherwise grappling with heat, security scares and diplomatic strain.

Latin America – Who the Spain-Italy Checks Actually Catch

A practical warning for non-EU residents

Spain hosts the largest Latin American diaspora in Europe, and the new checks require non-EU nationals to produce a visa or residence permit on arrival from Italy. Colombian, Venezuelan, Peruvian, Ecuadorian and Brazilian residents of either country are therefore directly affected, as is anyone from the region transiting Rome or Milan on the way to Madrid or Barcelona.

Because Italy is running its own checks in the opposite direction until 31 August, and Spain’s run to 7 September, both legs of a round trip are now controlled. If you are connecting through an Italian hub in the next month, allow at least two extra hours and carry the residence card rather than assuming an ID card will do.

Germany – Major Music Festivals Open Across the Country

Mera Luna, Hanfparade and lakeside celebrations draw crowds

The Mera Luna gothic and alternative music festival and several other large German summer festivals opened on 8 and 9 August 2026, including the Hanfparade in Berlin and the Konstanzer Seenachtfest.

The crowds brought a summertime buzz, yet the revelry unfolded under a shared awareness of the heat and the tense headlines beyond the festival gates.

The Bigger Picture Europe’s mood on Saturday was edgy and fragmented, as Spain suddenly turned its border with Italy into a checkpoint, demanding passports from all Italian arrivals in a blunt message over the Ceuta migration dispute. The unilateral move left Rome diplomatically isolated just when Mediterranean solidarity is in short supply. Security nerves were raw further east after a drone exploded within a kilometre of Bulgaria’s Trans-Balkan gas pipeline, a stark reminder of Russia’s war spilling beyond Ukraine’s borders. At the same moment, six unidentified drones were seen over a German military base in North Rhine-Westphalia, adding to a pattern of incursions that is fraying public calm. Grief and defiance swept Ukraine overnight into Saturday when Russian strikes killed a three-year-old child and three others in the Kyiv region, prompting President Zelenskyy to demand stronger sanctions and more air defences. The human cost cut through a week already weighed down by a searing heatwave across Italy and Spain, Germany’s costly retreat from American wind projects, and a continent-wide sense that the ground is shifting underfoot.

Europe Intelligence Brief August 8: What We Are Watching

Today – Zurich Street Parade and Shutdown Festival offer brief respite from the heat and tension.

This weekend – Mera Luna and other German festivals open under heat warnings and an anxious national mood.

This weekend – Cycling races continue in Spain and Poland, providing moments of sporting rhythm.

Asia Intelligence Brief August 8 — Key Facts —Mecca Pact Signed Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan signed a mutual defence treaty treating an attack on one as an attack on all. —Typhoon Dolphin Japan ordered mass evacuations and cancelled over 500 flights as Typhoon Dolphin approaches the southwest. —SK Hynix Bet SK Hynix approved 54.3 trillion won, about US$38.3 billion, for new chip plants through 2031. —Taiwan Drills President Lai boarded a missile boat during the Han Kuang exercises; Taipei called Beijing’s typhoon traffic order for the Strait “utterly ridiculous”. —India Rate Hold The RBI held the repo rate at 5.25 per cent on 5 August, raising its growth forecast to 6.7 per cent for FY27. —Singapore Energy Singapore conditionally approved 900 MW of electricity imports from Malaysia to help decarbonise its power supply.

Asia Intelligence Brief August 8 — Asia-Pacific wakes to a Saturday of signatures, storms, and steady strategic positioning. A new three-nation defence pact in Mecca and war games off Taiwan anchor a region visibly hardening its security ties.

Asia traded a day of signatures, storms and steady positioning. (Photo: Internet reproduction)

Beneath the geopolitical noise, commerce hums: China’s trade data offers a surprise upside and South Korea bets big on chips. The mood is watchful, resilient, and nowhere relaxed.

Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Pakistan — Trilateral Mutual Defence Pact Signed

Historic defence alignment in Mecca

Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement on Friday. The pact states that an armed attack on one member will be treated as an attack on all three.

Turkey said the agreement does not conflict with its NATO commitments. The three countries framed the pact as a regional security mechanism, not a sectarian bloc.

Yemen — Houthi Drone Attack Repelled Over Marib

Drones and missiles intercepted

Yemeni government forces shot down several Houthi drones over Marib on Friday. Houthi shelling of the city killed two civilians the same day.

Saudi Arabia separately blamed the Houthis for an attack that injured at least 11 civilians in Najran.

Saudi Arabia blamed the Houthis for a separate attack that wounded at least 11 civilians in Najran.

Japan — Typhoon Dolphin Forces Mass Evacuations and Flight Cancellations

Weary vigilance across the southwest

Japan ordered mass evacuations as Typhoon Dolphin approached southwestern Japan on Friday. More than 500 flights were cancelled due to the storm.

The typhoon disrupted transport and civil protection across the region, adding a layer of exhaustion to communities already on alert.

China — July Trade Data Beats Forecasts on AI-Linked Price Strength

Export and import surprise

China’s July exports beat forecasts, rising about 23 per cent year on year against an expected 22.2 per cent. Imports missed, up 27.5 per cent against an expected 27.9 per cent. The strength was driven by AI-related demand rather than prices: semiconductor exports nearly doubled in value and high-tech exports rose 40.7 per cent, leaving a surplus of US$112.5 billion.

The data was published on Friday night and carried into Saturday coverage, offering a bright spot amid dual-pronged anxiety over flooding and the housing market.

South Korea — SK Hynix Approves 54.3 Trillion Won Chip-Plant Investment

Long-term industrial confidence

SK Hynix’s board approved roughly 54.3 trillion won, about US$38.3 billion, in investments through 2031: 35.2 trillion won for a DRAM fab at Yongin and 19.1 trillion won for the M17 NAND plant at Cheongju.

The approval signals cautious optimism and long-term confidence in semiconductor demand despite global uncertainties.

Taiwan — President Lai Oversees Annual War-Game Drills Amid Cross-Strait Friction

Resolute but edgy coastal exercises

President Lai Ching-te boarded a Kuang Hua VI-class missile boat at the Tsoying naval base in Kaohsiung on Saturday, on day four of the ten-day Han Kuang exercises, as forces rehearsed countering a simulated Chinese assault.

Separately, China ordered northbound ships at the southern entrance of the Taiwan Strait to submit to traffic control ahead of Typhoon Dolphin, framing it as a safety measure. Taiwan’s Mainland Affairs Council called it “utterly ridiculous”.

Singapore — Conditional Approval for 900 MW Electricity Imports from Malaysia

Pragmatic decarbonisation push

Singapore’s Energy Market Authority granted conditional approval to Sembcorp Utilities for 300 MW and to Southern Solar Alliance, a Ditrolic Energy subsidiary, for 600 MW — 900 MW in total, from solar and battery storage in Johor, with commercial operation targeted around 2029. The move is part of Singapore’s push to decarbonise its power supply.

The approval is one of the most consequential Asia-Pacific energy-market items of the day, reflecting steady pragmatic progress.

India — RBI Holds Repo Rate at 5.25%

Steady and guarded policy stance

The Reserve Bank of India kept the repo rate unchanged at 5.25 per cent at its meeting on Wednesday 5 August, a unanimous decision under Governor Sanjay Malhotra that left the stance neutral. The central bank raised its FY27 growth forecast to 6.7 per cent and cut its inflation projection to 5.0 per cent.

The RBI also signalled a possible restart of on-tap licensing for urban cooperative banks and a review of lending-rate rules.

Indonesia — Construction Begins on First Locally Assembled Scorpene Submarine

Naval milestone in Surabaya

PT PAL cut first steel in Surabaya on Friday on the first of two Scorpène Evolved submarines, built under a Naval Group technology transfer, with delivery targeted for 2032.

Indosat also launched Zankore, an AI factory platform with Ooredoo as lead investor alongside Nokia and NVIDIA, starting at about 200 MW in the first half of 2027 and scaling towards a gigawatt.

Singapore — 8 kg of Cocaine Seized from Foreign Vessel

Maritime drug enforcement

Singapore authorities seized 8 kg of cocaine from a foreign-registered commercial vessel in Singapore waters. The seizure was reported in same-day regional headlines.

India — New Security Rules Bar Renewable Projects Within 1 km of International Borders

Border-zone restrictions tighten

India’s Ministry of Home Affairs issued new security guidelines for renewable-energy projects near international borders. New solar, wind and hybrid projects are barred within 1 km of the international border. The zone from 1 to 50 km is designated sensitive, with clearance decided case by case rather than granted automatically, and a separate defence ministry no-objection certificate needed inside 20 km.

The petroleum minister also noted that the U.S. now accounts for about 67 per cent of India’s LPG imports.

China — Beijing Activates Emergency Flood Response as Typhoon Dolphin Nears

Dual-pronged anxiety

China activated an emergency response for floods as Typhoon Dolphin approached, according to a Xinhua wire timestamped early Saturday. The storm added civil-protection anxiety to an already complex picture.

A parallel report noted Beijing easing home-purchase limits and raising provident-fund loan caps, signalling efforts to cushion the housing slowdown.

Bangladesh — Cricket Star Shakib Al Hasan Ready to Face Trial If Guaranteed Security

Uneasy political limbo

Shakib Al Hasan said he was ready to return home and face trial if guaranteed security. He is a known ally of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.

The statement, reported on Saturday, underscored the uneasy political limbo in Bangladesh.

ASEAN — Regional Body Marks 59th Anniversary with Call for Youth Opportunities

A milestone celebration

ASEAN marked its 59th anniversary on Saturday, calling for greater opportunities for youth. U.S. lawmakers issued a statement recognising ASEAN Day.

India — India-China Talks Stress Border Peace and Tranquility

Quiet diplomacy continues

Indian and Chinese officials held talks on Friday, stressing the need for border peace and tranquility to boost the broader bilateral relationship. The talks were the latest substantive diplomatic development in India-China ties.

Philippines — Manila Says It Does Not Condone Threats After Anti-China Caskets Found

Tensions in the capital

Anti-China caskets were found in Manila in the early hours of Friday. The Philippine government said it did not condone threats of violence, and the story remained in circulation on Saturday.

Latin America – What China’s Import Surge Is Running On

Brazilian cargo behind the trade numbers

The import side of China’s July data matters to Latin America more than the export side. China’s soybean imports from Brazil hit a record 12.08 million tonnes in June, up 13.7 per cent year on year, while US volumes fell 20.6 per cent to 1.27 million tonnes. Brazil has widened its lead in the Chinese market despite the Trump-Xi deal.

Iron ore tells the same story: China ran at a record 135 million tonnes of Brazilian imports in the first half, worth about US$9.2 billion. When Chinese demand or Chinese ports wobble, as they are doing this weekend under Typhoon Dolphin, the first place it shows up is the queue of Brazilian bulk carriers waiting to discharge.

New Zealand — Fresh Sanctions Announced Against Russia

New punitive measures

New Zealand announced its 36th Russia sanctions package on Saturday, covering 33 individuals and entities, with Foreign Minister Winston Peters citing cyber actors and the forced deportation of Ukrainian children.

The Bigger Picture Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, President Erdoğan, and Prime Minister Sharif signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement on Friday, creating a trilateral mutual-defence obligation. Turkey stressed the pact does not clash with its NATO role, framing it as a security mechanism; in Yemen, government forces shot down Houthi drones over Marib, while Saudi Arabia blamed the group for a separate attack that wounded at least 11 civilians in Najran. Japan ordered mass evacuations and cancelled more than 500 flights as Typhoon Dolphin approached the southwest, while China activated an emergency flood response; China’s July exports beat forecasts on AI-related demand, though imports came in slightly below expectations. India’s central bank held its key rate at 5.25 per cent on 5 August, and the government barred renewable projects within a kilometre of international borders, noting the U.S. now supplies about 67 per cent of its LPG imports. SK Hynix’s board approved a 54.3 trillion won investment, about US$38.3 billion, in Korean chip plants through 2031; in Taiwan, President Lai Ching-te joined annual war games aboard a missile boat as forces rehearsed countering a simulated Chinese assault, and Taipei dismissed Beijing’s strait traffic order. Elsewhere, Indonesia cut first steel on its first locally built Scorpène Evolved submarine, Singapore seized 8 kg of cocaine from a foreign vessel, and Bangladesh cricket star Shakib Al Hasan said he was ready to face trial if guaranteed security.

Asia Intelligence Brief August 8: What We Are Watching

Today – Typhoon Dolphin tracks across southwestern Japan, bringing heavy rain and disrupting transport.

This week – Military drills continue near Taiwan, while markets digest China’s trade data and India’s rate decision.

World.title: Colombia Recognises Moroccan Sovereignty Over Western Sahara on Day One
World.content:
By subscribing you agree to our privacy policy . We never share your email.

Colombia · FOREIGN POLICY

Key Facts —The decision: Colombia recognised Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara on 8 August 2026 and withdrew its recognition of the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic. —Who announced it: Vice-President José Manuel Restrepo and Foreign Minister Omar Bula Escobar, in a meeting with Morocco’s Foreign Minister Nasser Bourita, who was in Cali for the inauguration. —The timing: Hours after Abelardo De La Espriella was sworn in on 7 August, making it one of the first foreign-policy acts of the new government. —What it reverses: Gustavo Petro restored relations with the Sahrawi republic in 2022 after they had been frozen since 2001, and pledged “unrestricted” support for Sahrawi self-determination as recently as November 2025. —Why it carries weight: Colombia took a non-permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council on 1 January 2026, so it now votes on the MINURSO mandate. —What Rabat said: Bourita called it “a historic decision that will give a great push to the bilateral relationship.”

Colombia’s new government recognised Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara on Saturday and withdrew its recognition of the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic, reversing four years of policy within a day of taking office and changing the arithmetic on a file that reaches the United Nations Security Council, where Colombia now holds a seat.

Bogotá and Rabat both framed the shift around trade. (Photo: Internet reproduction)

What Colombia actually decided

The announcement came out of a meeting in Cali between Vice-President José Manuel Restrepo, Foreign Minister Omar Bula Escobar and Morocco’s Foreign Minister Nasser Bourita, who had travelled to Colombia for Friday’s inauguration. Bula Escobar said a formal communiqué would follow within hours.

The foreign ministry framed it as a reset rather than a rupture: with this decision, it said, Colombia seeks to revitalise its relationship with Morocco on the basis of a long-term vision, in the conviction that closer bilateral ties will fully serve the interests of the Colombian people. Bourita, for his part, called Colombia’s withdrawal of recognition from the Sahrawi republic and its recognition of Moroccan sovereignty “a historic decision that will give a great push to the bilateral relationship.”

Two things are worth separating. Recognising Moroccan sovereignty is one act. Withdrawing recognition of the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic is a second, and it is the harder one to walk back. Colombia has now done both.

Why this is a genuine reversal, not a clarification

Colombia has been here before, and the earlier episode is often misreported. In October 2021, under Iván Duque, Vice-President and Foreign Minister Marta Lucía Ramírez said in Rabat that Colombia supported Morocco’s “territorial integrity” and that its embassy’s consular jurisdiction covered “all Moroccan territory, including the southern provinces.” Several outlets reported that as recognition. The foreign ministry then clarified that it was a consular arrangement, not a sovereignty statement, and reaffirmed support for the UN process.

Gustavo Petro moved in the opposite direction. His government restored relations with the Sahrawi republic in 2022, after a freeze dating to 2001, and as recently as November 2025 pledged “unrestricted” support for Sahrawi self-determination. Saturday’s announcement is therefore the first time Colombia has stated the recognition plainly, and it undoes a position held for four years.

The Security Council seat is what makes this more than symbolism

Colombia began a two-year term as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council on 1 January 2026, elected the previous June with 180 votes. It is the eighth time the country has sat on the Council, alongside Bahrain, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Latvia and Liberia in the current intake.

That matters here because Western Sahara is a standing Council file. The mandate of MINURSO, the UN mission in the territory, comes up for renewal at the Council, and the wording of those resolutions is fought over line by line. A member that has just recognised Moroccan sovereignty votes differently from one that was pledging support for Sahrawi self-determination nine months earlier. Rabat has spent years assembling exactly this kind of incremental diplomatic weight, and a Council seat is the most valuable version of it.

What is actually at stake in the territory

Western Sahara is not empty desert. Morocco, counting the territory, holds roughly 50 billion tonnes of the world’s estimated 74 billion tonnes of phosphate rock reserves — about 70 percent of the global total. That is a reserves figure, not a production one: Morocco accounts for something closer to a seventh of world output. Phosphate is the input for fertiliser, which makes it an input for food.

The Bou Craa deposit inside Western Sahara, operated by Phosboucraa, holds around 800 million tonnes, roughly two percent of the combined Moroccan and Saharan reserve base, with capacity near 2.6 million tonnes a year. Figures putting Bou Craa at a tenth of Moroccan exports conflate it with a different statistic. The Atlantic coastline also supports a substantial fishery, which is what has kept the European Union tangled in litigation over trade and fisheries agreements that touch the territory.

What it signals about De La Espriella’s foreign policy

For readers watching Colombia rather than the Maghreb, the interesting part is the speed. This was settled in a meeting on the margins of the inauguration, before a cabinet had finished being sworn in, and it lands on the same side as Washington, which has backed Morocco’s claim since 2020. The day before, the State Department said it intended, working with Congress, to provide US$1 billion in security assistance to the incoming administration, and Colombia was folded into the United States’ “Shield of the Americas” anti-narcotics bloc.

Read together, those are the first coordinates of a foreign policy that is aligning quickly and visibly with Washington and its partners. Bula Escobar has also floated deeper economic ties with Morocco, without ruling out a future free-trade agreement. Latin America has historically split on Western Sahara, with several governments recognising the Sahrawi republic and others staying neutral; Colombia has now moved off the fence in the other direction.

What to watch next

The formal communiqué is the first thing. The wording will show whether Colombia is recognising sovereignty outright or endorsing Morocco’s autonomy plan as the basis for a settlement, which is a meaningfully weaker position and the one most Western governments have taken.

After that, watch Algiers. Algeria backs the Polisario Front and has downgraded relations with states that have made this move; Colombia closed its embassy in Algeria earlier this year, so there is less left to downgrade. And watch how Colombia votes the next time MINURSO comes before the Security Council. That vote, not the communiqué, is where this decision becomes consequential.

Frequently asked questions

Has Colombia recognised Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara?

Yes. On 8 August 2026 the government of Abelardo De La Espriella recognised Moroccan sovereignty and withdrew Colombia’s recognition of the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic. It was announced after a meeting in Cali between Vice-President José Manuel Restrepo, Foreign Minister Omar Bula Escobar and Morocco’s Nasser Bourita.

Is this a change from Colombia’s previous position?

Yes, and a sharp one. Gustavo Petro restored relations with the Sahrawi republic in 2022 after a freeze dating to 2001, and in November 2025 pledged unrestricted support for Sahrawi self-determination. An earlier 2021 statement by Vice-President Marta Lucía Ramírez was later clarified by the foreign ministry as a consular arrangement rather than recognition.

Why does Colombia’s position matter internationally?

Because Colombia took a non-permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council on 1 January 2026 for a two-year term. Western Sahara is a standing Council file through the MINURSO mandate, so Colombia now has a vote on how those resolutions are worded.

World.title: Where You Can Fly Nonstop to Costa Rica This High Season
World.content:
Getting to Costa Rica is about to get easier from a lot more places. Fourteen new or expanded nonstop flights start between October and March, and several of them connect cities that have never had a direct flight here. One heavily promoted route has already been cancelled, and it is worth knowing which. If you are planning a trip for the high season, or you have family flying down to visit, this is the list you need.

Every route below is confirmed by the airline, with start dates, days of the week and aircraft where those have been published. The expansion follows a strong year for arrivals. Between January and June, 1,605,360 travelers landed in Costa Rica by air, up 7.8% over the same six months of 2025 and the best first half on record.

New flights to San Jose

Las Vegas is off the table. Southwest announced a daily overnight Las Vegas to San Jose route in February, pushed the launch from October to November, then cancelled it in July before a single flight operated. The airline cited fuel costs and a decision to use its aircraft more efficiently, since an overnight leaves a plane parked in Costa Rica for hours. If you were waiting on that one, stop waiting.

That leaves the western United States where it was. From Nevada, Arizona and most of California you are still connecting through Houston, Miami or another gateway to reach Costa Rica.

Breeze Airways arrives from Tampa on October 3. This is the airline’s first-ever service to Costa Rica and makes the country its fifth international destination. Flights run Wednesdays and Saturdays on an Airbus A220 seating 137. Tampa has not had a direct link to San Jose in more than 25 years.

Air Transat starts Quebec City on December 15, once a week. Unlike most of the winter additions, this one is permanent rather than seasonal, and it brings the number of Canadian cities with direct flights to Costa Rica to seven.

Porter connects Toronto Pearson from December 2 through April 30, four flights a week on an Embraer E195-E2 seating 132. The aircraft has no middle seats.

Southwest adds Austin on March 13, 2027, Saturdays only. It is the only nonstop between Central Texas and San Jose. The outbound leaves Austin at 10:25 a.m. and lands at 2:05 p.m., with the return departing at 3:05 p.m. Tickets are already on sale.

New flights to Guanacaste

Liberia keeps pulling ahead. Daniel Oduber Quiros handled its busiest quarter ever in early 2026, and airlines have noticed. Air Canada flies Vancouver from December 13 through April 12, Mondays and Thursdays on a Boeing 737 MAX 8 seating 177. Canadian traffic through Liberia grew 28% in the first half of this year, which is the main reason so many of these routes point north.

WestJet adds Ottawa from December 20 through April 4, Sundays, on a 737 MAX 8 seating 174. Worth knowing before you shop: Porter already flies Ottawa to Liberia weekly through the winter, so from December you have two nonstop options on that route rather than one.

United flies Washington-Dulles daily from December 17 through January 4. Note how short that window is. It is a holiday-season route, not a winter-long one, and if you want it you should book early. The aircraft is a Boeing 737 MAX 9 with 179 seats including 20 in business.

That route also completes something unusual. United will now serve Liberia from all seven of its US hubs, alongside Newark, Denver, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Houston and Chicago. Delta returns to New York JFK from December 19 through April 10, Saturdays only, on an Airbus A321neo seating 194. Delta last flew this route in 2016, and it currently offers no service at all between New York City and Costa Rica.

Southwest adds Nashville from February 13 to March 6, 2027, Saturdays, on a 737 MAX 8. That is a four-week window, the shortest on this list.

Costa Rica gets its first flights from Poland

The most unexpected addition is a charter series. Rainbow Tours and LOT Polish Airlines will run eleven flights into Liberia on a Boeing 787-8 Dreamliner seating 251, the first direct air link between Poland and Costa Rica. Warsaw Chopin operates weekly from October 8 to 29. Katowice takes over weekly from November 5 to December 17.

These are charter operations sold through a tour operator, so you will not find them on a standard flight search. If you have family in Poland planning a visit, that is the booking route.

More Seats from Europe

Three European carriers are adding frequencies rather than new destinations, which matters if you have struggled to find a seat on a specific day.

British Airways moves to Heathrow on October 25 and goes from three to five weekly flights through March, operating Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays on a Boeing 787-8. If you connect onward in Europe, this is the change that matters most. Heathrow is the airline’s main hub, and it has never had scheduled service to Costa Rica or anywhere in Central America until now.

Lufthansa moves from three to five weekly Frankfurt flights from October 25 to March 27, operating Mondays, Wednesdays, Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays. The days change as well as the count, so check yours. The route currently runs Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays. Lufthansa is also switching to a Boeing 787-9 with its newer Allegris cabin.

Iberojet adds a third weekly Madrid flight on Thursdays from late November. The airline expects to make it permanent across 2027 and 2028.

The full list

Airline Route Starts Days Southwest Las Vegas to San Jose Cancelled Dropped before launch Breeze Tampa to San Jose Oct 3 Wed, Sat LOT (charter) Warsaw to Liberia Oct 8 to 29 Weekly British Airways London Heathrow to San Jose Oct 25 (3 to 5 weekly) Tue, Wed, Fri, Sat, Sun Lufthansa Frankfurt to San Jose Oct 25 (3 to 5 weekly) Mon, Wed, Fri, Sat, Sun LOT (charter) Katowice to Liberia Nov 5 to Dec 17 Weekly Iberojet Madrid to San Jose Late Nov (2 to 3 weekly) Adds Thu Porter Toronto to San Jose Dec 2 to Apr 30 4 weekly Air Canada Vancouver to Liberia Dec 13 to Apr 12 Mon, Thu Air Transat Quebec City to San Jose Dec 15 Weekly United Washington-Dulles to Liberia Dec 17 to Jan 4 Daily Delta New York JFK to Liberia Dec 19 to Apr 10 Sat WestJet Ottawa to Liberia Dec 20 to Apr 4 Sun Southwest Nashville to Liberia Feb 13 to Mar 6 Sat Southwest Austin to San Jose Mar 13, 2027 Sat

Before you book

Pick your airport before you pick your flight. Liberia puts you within a short drive of Tamarindo, Nosara, Playas del Coco, Papagayo, Flamingo and Santa Teresa. San Jose is better for the Caribbean side, the Central Valley, the southern Pacific and anywhere you need a domestic connection. Landing at the wrong one can add four or five hours of driving to your first day.

Watch the end dates as closely as the start dates. Several of these routes run for weeks rather than months, and a return flight that does not exist yet is a common way to get stuck paying for a connection you did not plan. Liberia also operates only between 6 a.m. and 9 p.m., so late arrivals are not an option there regardless of what a search engine shows you.

Seasonal routes get pulled when they do not sell. If a specific one matters to your plans, booking it early does more than save money, it helps keep the route on the schedule. That is also the argument for travel insurance on a seasonal route. If an airline drops the flight or shifts the schedule after you have booked hotels and tours around it, a policy that covers trip interruption is what stands between you and paying twice.

World.title: Costa Rica Approves New Rules for Nighttime Ambulance Flights
World.content:
Costa Rica has approved a national protocol governing nighttime air ambulance flights, closing out roughly ten months of uncertainty that began when Civil Aviation barred the practice at most of the airfields last October. Under the framework, night medical flights are permitted at six locations: the airfields at Limón, Palmar Sur and Coto 47 near Ciudad Neily, along with Tobías Bolaños in Pavas, Daniel Oduber in Liberia and Juan Santamaría in Alajuela.

Juan Santamaría must now serve as the arrival point for every nighttime medical flight in the country. The selection came down largely to which fields have runway lighting and a permanent police presence, both treated as prerequisites for safe operations after dark. Coto 47 has both, including a base of the Air Vigilance Service, and Palmar Sur received substantial state investment in lighting and security in recent years.

Left off the approved list are several airfields serving high-traffic tourist areas, among them Tamarindo, Quepos and Puerto Jiménez. Pilots had also identified Cóbano and Nicoya as essential for reaching patients in coastal and peninsular communities far from major hospitals.

The protocol restricts these flights to patients in critical condition whose lives are at immediate risk and who cannot safely wait for daylight. It sets out an eleven-step process that begins when the Costa Rican Social Security Fund identifies an emergency case, moves through coordination with the Air Vigilance Service and Civil Aviation, and ends with a private operator carrying out the flight once conditions and authorization align.

Officials say exceptions outside the formal protocol will still be permitted when a patient’s life is at stake. The rules were drafted jointly by the Ministry of Health, Civil Aviation, the Social Security Fund and the Air Vigilance Service, and are to be reviewed annually.

The finalized protocol ends a dispute that began with a directive issued on October 9 of last year, which prohibited takeoffs and landings between sunset and sunrise at uncontrolled airfields nationwide. Civil Aviation argued the flights had operated for decades without a formal regulatory framework and that medical operations must meet the same technical and legal standards as any other flight.

Transportation Minister Efraím Zeledón Leiva and Social Security Fund president Mónica Taylor defended the restriction at a press conference in February, characterizing the volume of genuinely urgent flights as minimal. Taylor said many transfers went to private hospitals and involved minor complaints. Zeledón referred to irregular commercial arrangements around the flights at Tobías Bolaños, and maintained that extreme emergencies were still being authorized.

That position drew immediate pushback from pilots, ambulance operators and physicians inside the Social Security system. The Fund’s own emergency and disaster center warned the restriction was delaying transfers of patients who needed higher-capacity hospitals, and the hospital in Ciudad Neily fell back on ground transfers with police escorts to speed the run into the Central Valley.

Ricardo Hernández, a paramedic and operations manager at the air and ground transport company SAAT, said roughly 700 people a year need urgent air transport in Costa Rica for medical reasons, and that close to half of all transfers happen at night. Operators separately reported hundreds of night ambulance flights annually before the restriction took effect, and said the country had recorded no accidents in night operations at uncontrolled airfields in eighteen years.

An analysis presented by pilots counted 3,130 nighttime ambulance flights over the previous decade, an average of about 285 a year, without a serious incident. Pilots also noted that the October directive landed at the start of high tourist season, when visitors are more likely to be injured in remote or coastal areas.

For anyone traveling to the more remote parts of the country, including popular surf and beach towns that are not on the approved list, the practical effect is unchanged. A serious nighttime medical emergency in those areas will still mean a lengthy ground transfer rather than an air evacuation, because every flight must now either originate or terminate at one of the six designated locations.

Civil Aviation issued temporary technical standards for qualifying airfields earlier this year while the permanent framework was being finalized. Those interim rules are now replaced. Whether additional airfields can be brought onto the list will depend on lighting, perimeter security and staffing upgrades that have not yet been funded or scheduled.

World.title: Cincinnati Open Opens This Weekend With Practices, Fan Events and New Attractions
World.content:
The Cincinnati Open will begin welcoming fans Saturday, August 8, several days before the first official matches are played, as one of the biggest tournaments on the North American tennis calendar opens with a full weekend of player practices, fan activities and special events.



The two-day Community Weekend at the Lindner Family Tennis Center in Mason, Ohio, will give fans an early look at players preparing for the ATP and WTA 1000 tournament before qualifying begins Tuesday. The opening weekend is part of the tournament’s continued expansion beyond traditional match days, with organizers placing greater emphasis on player access, practices and activities around the grounds.



For tennis fans, the biggest draw may simply be the chance to watch some of the world’s top players practice from much closer than is normally possible during tournament competition.

Players Take to the Practice Courts

Saturday’s Kids Day will run from 10 a.m. until 4 p.m. and include open player practices, tennis drills, autograph sessions, a scavenger hunt, live music and other activities throughout the grounds. Unlike a normal tournament day, when attention is divided between matches taking place across multiple courts, the opening weekend gives spectators an opportunity to follow players through their final training sessions before competition begins.



That could provide an early look at how some of Cincinnati’s leading contenders are adjusting to the hard courts and summer conditions in Ohio. The tournament field includes many of the biggest names in men’s and women’s tennis, along with a sizable Latin American contingent.

Brazil’s João Fonseca and Argentina’s Francisco Cerúndolo are among the leading Latin American men entered, while Colombia’s Camila Osorio headlines the region’s representation on the women’s side. Practice schedules can change and are normally finalized closer to the sessions, meaning fans hoping to see a particular player will need to monitor tournament updates throughout the weekend.

Red Bull BassLine Makes U.S. Debut

Saturday evening will feature a different version of professional tennis when Red Bull BassLine makes its United States debut on Grandstand Court. The exhibition runs from 7 p.m. to 10 p.m. and combines a quick-fire knockout format with music from a live on-court DJ.



Rather than playing traditional full matches, players compete in shorter contests designed to create a faster and more informal atmosphere than a regular ATP or WTA match. The event has previously been staged in Europe and Australia, with Cincinnati becoming its first U.S. location.



It will be separately ticketed from the daytime Community Weekend activities, although a BassLine ticket also provides access to the tournament grounds earlier Saturday.

Cincinnati Open 5K Starts Sunday

Sunday will begin at 8 a.m. with another first for the tournament: the inaugural Cincinnati Open 5K. The run will take participants through the tournament’s 40-acre grounds before finishing with a post-race gathering. After the race, All Access Sunday will run from 10 a.m. until 4 p.m. and include additional player practices, meet-and-greets, autograph sessions, live entertainment and a Center Court photo opportunity.



The tournament will also feature adaptive tennis activities during the weekend. Fans who want another day focused primarily on training rather than matches will have one final opportunity Monday, August 10, when the grounds reopen from 10 a.m. until 4 p.m. for player practices.

Competitive Tennis Begins Tuesday

The atmosphere will change Tuesday morning when qualifying officially begins. Gates are scheduled to open at 9 a.m. on August 11, with the first qualifying matches beginning at 10:30 a.m. The second day of qualifying follows Wednesday before the men’s and women’s main draws begin Thursday, August 13.

The tournament then continues through August 23, when both singles champions are scheduled to be crowned. Cincinnati occupies an important position on the tennis calendar because it is one of the final major tournaments before the US Open in New York. Players use the event not only to compete for significant ATP and WTA ranking points but also to test their games against elite competition under North American hard-court conditions.

That makes the practice sessions and early rounds particularly useful indicators of player form heading toward the year’s final Grand Slam.

Cincinnati Builds on Record 2025 Tournament

The opening weekend follows a record-setting year for the Cincinnati Open. More than 285,000 people attended the tournament in 2025 following a major redevelopment of the Lindner Family Tennis Center. The venue now includes 31 outdoor courts and an expanded campus designed to accommodate the tournament’s larger ATP and WTA fields.



The Cincinnati Open was subsequently named the 1000-level Tournament of the Year by both the ATP and WTA. This year’s tournament extends the experience even further by opening the grounds before qualifying begins, turning what was traditionally preparation time for players into several days of public access.

For fans, it also means the Cincinnati Open effectively begins before the first official point is played. The Tico Times will be there to provide on-site coverage and photography from Mason beginning August 13, following the tournament’s leading storylines and Latin American players as the field moves toward the US Open.

World.title: Belize @45 Workshop Explores Sovereignty and Nationhood
World.content:
Belize @45 Workshop Explores Sovereignty and Nationhood

By Zoila Palma: The Belize @45 Workshop, a three-day professional development training, was held from August 5 to 7, 2026, bringing together educators from across the country to examine what Belize’s independence really means.

The training was a collaborative effort of the Institute for Social and Cultural Research (ISCR), the Belize Archives and Records Service (BARS), the Ministry of Education, Culture, Science & Technology (MOECST), specifically Ms. Ruby Reyes of the Belizean Studies Curriculum and Assessment Unit, the George Price Centre for Peace and Development, the University of Belize, and Galen University.

During the training, historian and diplomat Assad Shoman challenged educators to reflect on the “role of teachers and students in shaping Belize’s future.”

The event included virtual sessions and an in-person learning session at the George Price Centre for Peace and Development in Belmopan, equipping educators with new tools and perspectives to bring Belize’s history and independence journey to life for students.

Organizers emphasized that Belize’s independence is not simply an achievement of the past, but an ongoing process, underscoring the message: “Independence is the beginning!

World.title: Belizeans Travel Across U.S. for Passport and Nationality Services at Evanston Diaspora Hub
World.content:
Belizeans Travel Across U.S. for Passport and Nationality Services at Evanston Diaspora Hub

By Zoila Palma: Belizeans from across the Chicago area and several other parts of the United States travelled to Evanston this weekend to access passport and nationality services brought directly to the diaspora by Belize’s Ministry of Immigration, Governance and Labour.

The three-day Evanston Diaspora Hub runs from August 7 to 9. The event provides passport and nationality services, including first-time and renewal passport applications, as well as applications for Belizean nationality by descent.

The ministry says that the outreach provides a more convenient way to complete important documentation without having to travel to Belize. Belizean passport applicants are required to appear in person at an Immigration Office in Belize or at a designated Belizean diplomatic or consular mission, making mobile outreach efforts particularly valuable for Belizeans living far from those locations.

The Evanston hub also highlighted the strong community ties among Belizeans living in the United States. Some Chicago-area residents noted that they have built a vibrant Belizean community and are preparing to host a fundraiser on Saturday to provide scholarships to 14 Belizean-American students attending school.

Belize’s Ambassador to the United States, H.E. Nestor E. Mendez, visited the hub alongside Belize’s Ambassador for Diaspora Relations, Sandhya Murphy, as officials engaged with Belizeans accessing the services.

The Evanston initiative follows other diaspora outreach efforts by the Government of Belize in the United States. Earlier this year, approximately 230 passports and 17 nationality certificates were delivered to Belizeans abroad during another outreach initiative, reflecting continued demand for documentation services within Belizean communities across the United States.

World.title: Belizeans travel from across the United States to Evanston, Chicago, for immigration services at Diaspora Hub
World.content:
Belizeans travel from across the United States to Evanston, Chicago, for immigration services at Diaspora Hub

By Hugh O’Brien: Belizeans from across the Chicago area and the larger United States, including Texas, Washington and Colorado, travelled to Evanston this weekend to access passport and nationality services being offerred directly to the diaspora by Belize’s Ministry of Immigration, Governance and Labour.

The Diaspora Mobile Hub, being held from August 7 to 9, is providing Belizeans living in the United States with an opportunity to complete nationality and passport applications without having to travel to Belize or wait for an appointment at a designated Belizean diplomatic or consular mission.

While many of those attending came from Evanston, Chicago and surrounding communities, others travelled hundreds or even thousands of miles to take advantage of the outreach initiative. Several Belizeans from the Dallas area made the journey to Evanston to submit applications and complete other documentation processes.

In a public statement posted on its Facebook page, the Ministry said “Some visitors came to renew their Belizean passports, while others submitted first-time passport applications. Families also visited the hub to apply for Belizean nationality by descent, allowing eligible children and other descendants born outside Belize to formally establish their Belizean nationality.”

The Ministry said that these services are being provided through the Nationality and Passports Department as part of the Ministry’s broader effort to bring essential government services closer to Belizeans living abroad.

“For members of the diaspora, having services available in a U.S. city can significantly reduce the time, cost and logistical challenges associated with completing important documentation. Belizean passport applicants are required to appear in person at an Immigration Office in Belize or at a designated Belizean diplomatic or consular mission.”

For this reason, according to the Ministry, Evanston became a destination this weekend not only for Belizeans living in Illinois, but also for members of the diaspora who travelled from across the United States.

“For some families, the visit was simply about renewing a passport and maintaining the ability to travel using Belizean documentation. For others, particularly parents seeking nationality by descent for their children, the process represented another way of passing their connection to Belize from one generation to the next,” said the Ministry.

Belize’s Ambassador to the United States, H.E. Nestor E. Mendez, attended the Ministry’s immigration outreach alongside Belize’s Ambassador for Diaspora Relations, Sandhya Murphy.

Belizean nationality by descent is available to qualifying persons born outside Belize based on Belizean parentage.

The Evanston Diaspora Mobile Hub continues will conclude on Sunday, August 9.

World.title: Halo BPO sweetens the deal: $10 an hour plus commission for home based sales agents
World.content:
Halo BPO sweetens the deal: $10 an hour plus commission for home based sales agents

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Halo BPO is back on the hiring trail, and the terms have improved. The company’s latest recruitment drive for work from home sales agents offers $9.00 BZD per hour during training, rising to $10.00 BZD per hour after training, plus commission and bonuses, with pay issued weekly, an upgrade on the $8.50 flat rate advertised earlier this month.

The role is full time outbound sales, done entirely from home anywhere in Belize. The qualifying bar has risen alongside the pay: applicants now need two or more years of sales experience, and credit repair experience is listed as a plus, suggesting the campaign involves the credit services market.

The technical requirement is the other significant change. Home internet must deliver at least 85 Mbps download and 45 Mbps upload, a specification that in practice points to fibre-grade service, so applicants should run a speed test before applying.

For experienced sellers with strong connections, the package is among the more competitive remote offers advertised locally: guaranteed hourly pay, weekly payout, and commission upside on top.

Applications go to [email protected], and the standing instruction applies: include your full name in the email subject line.

World.title: The weekend keeps its promise: sunshine across Belize
World.content:
The weekend keeps its promise: sunshine across Belize

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): The forecast made the promise on Friday, and Saturday is delivering it in full. Mainly fair weather conditions prevail across Belize, with sunshine overhead, gentle seas, and inland heat reaching 95 degrees, and Sunday is set to repeat the performance.

According to the National Meteorological Service, skies will be sunny with a few cloudy spells today and clear to partly cloudy tonight. Showers or thunderstorms will be isolated, with a medium chance of a few more mostly over the Toledo District tonight, the weekend’s lone exception to the fair pattern.

Temperatures along the coast will reach a high of 89 degrees Fahrenheit (32 Celsius) and a low of 82 (28 Celsius). Inland areas will be the hottest in the country, climbing to 95 degrees Fahrenheit (35 Celsius) before dropping to 73 (23 Celsius). In the hills, expect a high of 83 degrees Fahrenheit (28 Celsius) and a cool low of 67 (19 Celsius). With the mercury at 95 inland, the weekend checklist stays simple: water close and shade often.

At sea, conditions remain at their friendliest, with easterly winds of 5 to 15 knots, a light chop, and waves of 2 to 4 feet, fine water for the weekend’s boaters, snorkelers, and fishing trips.

On the tropical front, the calm holds. Tropical cyclone formation is not expected in the region over the next 48 hours.

Looking ahead to Sunday and Sunday night, similar weather conditions are expected to prevail, carrying the sunshine through the full weekend.

Today’s low tides are at 1:06 PM and 11:32 PM, with a high tide at 7:41 PM and another high at 6:11 AM tomorrow. The sun sets this evening at 6:22 PM and rises tomorrow at 5:34 AM. The forecast was issued by forecaster Tareek Matthews.

World.title: Santander clarifies operations following reports of fish kill in Belize River
World.content:
Santander clarifies operations following reports of fish kill in Belize River

By Zoila Palma: On August 7, 2026, Santander Sugar Group (SSG) released a statement clarifying its operations following reports of aquatic life deaths in the Belize River Valley.

The release states that Santander Sugar Group is “deeply saddened by the loss of aquatic life recently reported in the Belize River Valley.” The company said it recognizes the importance of the Belize River to surrounding communities, the environment and Belize as a whole.

Santander said protecting natural resources remains a core principle of its operations. The company explained that it operates under an approved Environmental Compliance Plan and continuously monitors its operations while implementing measures to minimize runoff and protect surrounding waterways.

The company also said it has fully cooperated with the Department of the Environment (DoE) and other relevant government agencies since the incident was reported. According to SSG, the DoE was granted unrestricted access to its facilities and operations to support the ongoing investigation.

Santander further stated that its processing facility is designed to operate as a closed-loop system and does not operate with a continuous process effluent stream returning to the Belize River. The company said it remains committed to providing any additional information or assistance that may be required as authorities continue their investigation.

World.title: Belize City featured in Commonwealth Study
World.content:
Belize City featured in Commonwealth Study

By BBN Staff: Belize City is being featured in a new Commonwealth study examining how cities and local governments can close the urban finance gap and secure sustainable funding for infrastructure and essential services. The city was selected as one of only three case studies highlighted in the research, alongside Kerala State in India and Kigali, Rwanda.

On Wednesday, August 5, Belize City Mayor Bernard Wagner participated in the Commonwealth Local Government Forum’s webinar, “The Urban Finance Gap: Practical Pathways for Local Government Finance across the Commonwealth.” The discussion explored practical approaches to strengthening local government finance, improving resilience and ensuring cities have the resources needed to deliver critical services.

During the webinar, Wagner emphasized that financing infrastructure projects cannot end once construction is completed. He noted that projects such as drainage systems and roads must be designed to withstand changing conditions while also having adequate funding for operation, maintenance and eventual renewal. The Yarborough Pumping Station was highlighted as an example, having proven effective in draining the city’s waterways during flooding but also requiring significant recurring costs for continued operation and maintenance.

The Belize City Council said the city’s inclusion in the study highlights its fiscal administration, innovative approach to municipal finance and experience with its Municipal Bond Programme. It added that closing the urban finance gap will require greater decentralization, sustainable financing frameworks and increased trust in capable local governments to invest in their communities. Belize City’s experience is being presented as an example of what local leadership can achieve despite limited fiscal space.

World.title: Department of the Environment provides update on Fish Kill in the Belize River Valley area
World.content:
Department of the Environment provides update on Fish Kill in the Belize River Valley area

INVESTIGATION INTO THE FISH KILL IN THE BELIZE RIVER VALLEY AREA

Belmopan, Belize. August 7, 2026: The public is hereby informed that, as part of the ongoing investigation into the fish kill in the Belize River Valley area, the Department of the Environment (DOE) has conducted visual observations and water quality assessments from near Banana Bank, upstream of Santander Farms, to the Burrell Boom Village bridge. Significant fish mortality and changes in water conditions were observed particularly along the approximately 17.5-mile stretch between Isabella Bank and Grace Bank. The Department is also assessing discharge points and other activities along and within the vicinity of the river as part of its investigation into the possible source or sources of the event.

On-site water quality testing and sampling have been conducted at various locations along the river. Preliminary field results recorded extremely low levels of dissolved oxygen in areas where significant fish mortality was observed, together with elevated conductivity, chlorophyll-a and turbidity at certain locations. These conditions can adversely affect aquatic life. Samples have been submitted for laboratory analysis to assist in determining the cause of the observed conditions.

As part of the ongoing investigation, the DOE has also collected water samples from the Santander Farms drainage system and at locations downstream for chemical analysis. Fish and sediment samples are also being collected and analysed to assist in determining the cause of the fish mortality and whether contaminants may have contributed to the event.

The Department is additionally reviewing satellite imagery from before and during the event to assess changes in water conditions, land-clearing activities and other factors that may assist in identifying potential contributing sources. Investigations and assessments are also being conducted in relation to other developments, activities and potential discharge points within the wider area.

At this stage, the Department has not determined the source or responsible party associated with the fish kill. The investigation remains ongoing, and any determination will be based on the results of laboratory analyses and the totality of the scientific and technical evidence collected.

The precautionary advisory issued by the Department on August 5, 2026, remains in effect. The public is therefore advised not to consume fish or other aquatic resources from the affected areas and not to use untreated river water for drinking, cooking, food preparation, livestock or pets until further notice. This advisory applies to untreated water taken directly from the river and does not apply to treated potable water supplied by Belize Water Services Limited.

The DOE continues to coordinate with relevant government agencies and other authorities in monitoring the situation and advancing the investigation. The public will be informed as laboratory results and other verified findings become available.

The Department of the Environment remains committed to protecting Belize’s environment, safeguarding our natural resources and public health, and ensuring that all potential sources are thoroughly investigated and that appropriate action is taken where the evidence establishes a breach of Belize’s environmental laws.

END

For More Information Contact: Anthony Mai, Chief Environmental Officer

Department of the Environment
